title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
飭新規百度惟貞内外允秩
乃合試提學副使熊汲副使
張謙先後所取士三千有奇
得中式者九十人錄其名氏
與文以
獻洪邁謹序而言曰人才之盛豈
偶然哉則嘗稽諸古昔以驗
===
今日而有以知之矣夫閩在禹
服固東南之奧區也牒記靡
著往已至唐而歐陽詹者始
以科目顯自楊中立載道而
南而朱李鉅儒繼聲振響縉
紳衣屨之士談仁服義甲乙
鄒魯駸駸乎盛矣我
punctuated: 飭新規，百度惟貞，内外允秩。乃合試提學副使熊汲、副使張謙先後所取士三千有奇，得中式者九十人，錄其名氏與文以獻。洪邁謹序而言曰：「人才之盛，豈偶然哉？則嘗稽諸古昔，以驗今日，而有以知之矣。夫閩在禹服，固東南之奧區也。牒記靡著，往已。至唐，而歐陽詹者始以科目顯。自楊中立載道而南，而朱李鉅儒繼聲振響，縉紳衣屨之士談仁服義，甲乙鄒魯，駸駸乎盛矣。我
translation_en:
…new regulations were put in order; all administrative measures were correct, and affairs within and without were duly ordered. A joint examination was then held for the more than three thousand scholars selected successively by Xiong Ji, Vice Commissioner serving as Education Intendant, and Vice Commissioner Zhang Qian. Ninety candidates passed. Their names and compositions were recorded for presentation to the throne.
Hong Mai [?] respectfully provides this preface, saying: “Could such an abundance of talent be merely accidental? I have examined antiquity to test the circumstances of the present, and thereby have come to understand it. Min, within the domains of Yu, has always been a choice region of the southeast. Since the documentary records are indistinct, let us leave the distant past aside. Only in the Tang did Ouyang Zhan first achieve distinction through the examinations. After Yang Zhongli brought the Way south, the great Confucian scholars Zhu and Li carried on his teaching and made it resound. Gentlemen wearing the sashes, robes, and shoes of the educated elite discoursed on benevolence and practiced righteousness, rivaling Zou and Lu, and advanced rapidly toward flourishing eminence. Our …”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
國家縣隔八郡遂稱名藩衣冠
之族半於里巷一時能自表
見功業文章項背相望豈非
風氣盤鬱有待而開而聲敎
之漸被使然哉我
皇上躬脩文治益張前烈詩書禮
樂之澤流布宇內屬採禮官
===
議以文尚頗僻士習有關
勅羣有司舉士諸不應經義而謬
錄者罪其舉主匪以飾聽凡
以崇文敎而敦古朴也一時
待徵之士罔不回慮惕心仰
承
休德今其文之可錄者率平實典
punctuated: 國家縣隔八郡，遂稱名藩。衣冠之族半於里巷，一時能自表見，功業文章項背相望。豈非風氣盤鬱，有待而開，而聲敎之漸被使然哉？我皇上躬脩文治，益張前烈，詩書禮樂之澤流布宇內。屬採禮官議，以文尚頗僻，士習有關，勅羣有司舉士，諸不應經義而謬錄者，罪其舉主。匪以飾聽，凡以崇文敎而敦古朴也。一時待徵之士，罔不回慮惕心，仰承休德。今其文之可錄者，率平實典
translation_en:
…under our dynasty, the region was divided into eight prefectures [?] and thus became renowned as a provincial domain. Families of officials and scholars account for half the households in its neighborhoods. Men able to distinguish themselves through achievements and literary compositions have appeared in close succession. Surely this resulted from the region’s accumulated cultural energies, awaiting their moment to unfold, together with the gradual extension of imperial instruction!

Our Emperor personally cultivates civil governance, further magnifying the illustrious achievements of his predecessors. The beneficent influence of the Odes, Documents, rites, and music spreads throughout the realm. Recently, he adopted a proposal from the ritual officials: because literary preferences had become biased and wayward, with consequences for scholars’ habits, he commanded the responsible officials selecting candidates that whenever they mistakenly accepted work inconsistent with the meaning of the Classics, those responsible for recommending its author should be punished. This was no mere pronouncement for public effect; its purpose was to exalt literary instruction and foster the simplicity of antiquity. Among the scholars awaiting summons, none failed to reconsider their thinking and alert their hearts, reverently receiving his admirable virtue. Now, those of their compositions worthy of inclusion are generally plain, substantial, and classical…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
雅出入於經史而折衷於孔
孟蔚乎治世之能言曾未移
時而聲敎所被迎風雅化不
但俄頃之助已也於乎盛矣
夫人才之成雖不係於地而
卜宅者必期於仁里豪傑之
興固無待於時而潜德者尤
===
快於利見今夫秋葯漸之而
臭素絲染之而黑千里之駒
不經服習之敎不可以致遠
故學齊言者不楚傅而獲夜
光者不晝售魯無君子則子
賤無所取以成德世有文王
則中林野人且爲公侯之腹
punctuated:
雅，出入於經史，而折衷於孔孟，蔚乎治世之能言。曾未移時，而聲敎所被，迎風雅化，不但俄頃之助已也。於乎，盛矣！
夫人才之成，雖不係於地，而卜宅者必期於仁里；豪傑之興，固無待於時，而潜德者尤快於利見。今夫秋葯，漸之而臭；素絲，染之而黑。千里之駒，不經服習之敎，不可以致遠。故學齊言者不楚傅，而獲夜光者不晝售。魯無君子，則子賤無所取以成德；世有文王，則中林野人且爲公侯之腹
translation_en:
…elegant, ranging through the classics and histories while taking Confucius and Mencius as their standard: a splendid expression worthy of an age of good government. Before any time had passed, wherever the transforming influence of imperial instruction reached, people responded to it and were refined. Its benefit was more than momentary. Ah, how flourishing!
Although the cultivation of talented people does not depend on place, those choosing where to dwell invariably seek a benevolent neighborhood. Although the emergence of outstanding men need not await a particular age, those whose virtue remains hidden especially rejoice in an opportunity to appear before a great person. Consider autumn angelica: steep it, and it gives off a scent; dye white silk, and it turns black. A colt capable of traveling a thousand li cannot reach distant places without training and practice. Thus, one learning the speech of Qi does not take a teacher from Chu, and one who obtains a night-shining pearl does not offer it for sale by daylight. Had Lu possessed no gentlemen, Zijian would have had no one from whom to draw the means of perfecting his virtue; when a King Wen is present in the world, even rustic men dwelling deep in the woods may become the trusted confidants of dukes and marquises…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
心何者明盛之會難逢而漸
染之化易成也是故道悅周
孔陳良不免於北學人存伊
洛游楊必期於遠遊爾諸士
生君子之鄉遺範餘休往往
而在蓋不必遠慕而有餘師
矣而況親炙
===
聖德之光而沐浴菁莪之化
文敎日宣而盛美益振宜人才
之盛獨見於
今日也夫士之生不幸不得其
地得其地矣又患不遇其時
今
聖明在上固才智奮庸之日也則
punctuated: 心。何者？明盛之會難逢，而漸染之化易成也。是故道悅周孔，陳良不免於北學；人存伊洛，游楊必期於遠遊。爾諸士生君子之鄉，遺範餘休往往而在，蓋不必遠慕而有餘師矣。而況親炙聖德之光，而沐浴菁莪之化，文敎日宣，而盛美益振，宜人才之盛獨見於今日也。夫士之生，不幸不得其地；得其地矣，又患不遇其時。今聖明在上，固才智奮庸之日也，則
translation_en:
…trusted confidants of dukes and lords. Why is this? An enlightened and flourishing age is difficult to encounter, yet transformation through gradual influence is readily accomplished. Thus, delighting in the Way of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius, Chen Liang could not forgo studying in the north; while masters lived in the Yi and Luo region, You Zuo and Yang Shi were determined to journey far to study with them. You scholars were born in a land of gentlemen, where inherited examples and enduring beneficent influence are everywhere to be found. Surely you need not seek distant exemplars to have teachers in abundance. Moreover, you personally bask in the radiance of the sage emperor’s virtue and are nurtured by the educational influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Mugwort.” Civil instruction spreads daily, and its splendid achievements grow ever more manifest. It is fitting that such an abundance of talent should be seen uniquely today.

A scholar may have the misfortune of being born in the wrong place; even if he finds the right place, he still fears that he may not encounter the right age. Now that a sage and enlightened ruler reigns above, this is indeed the time for men of talent and wisdom to exert themselves in service. Then…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
所以增光先達而仰答
明時責將誰諉哉故緣飾詩書譁
衆市譽以曲趨巧售者先民
之敝德詭辭謬進幼學壯違
以徼取富貴者
清朝之棄才有一於此是墜前脩
之光而干
===
明主之典非所以自靖而圖報也
夫豈惟主司之憂抑亦二三
子者之羞是舉也提督南贛
軍務右副都御史顧遂綏靖
一方文事有賴左參議夏寶
僉事利賓戴鯨韓柱張合署
都指揮僉事李翱盧鎧防翊
punctuated:
所以增光先達而仰答明時，責將誰諉哉？故緣飾詩書，譁衆市譽，以曲趨巧售者，先民之敝德；詭辭謬進，幼學壯違，以徼取富貴者，清朝之棄才。有一於此，是墜前脩之光而干明主之典，非所以自靖而圖報也。夫豈惟主司之憂，抑亦二三子者之羞。
是舉也，提督南贛軍務右副都御史顧遂，綏靖一方，文事有賴；左參議夏寶，僉事利賓、戴鯨、韓柱、張合，署都指揮僉事李翱、盧鎧，防翊
translation_en:
…upon whom, then, can the responsibility for adding glory to distinguished predecessors and requiting this enlightened age be shifted? Those who embellish their words with the Poetry and Documents, clamour for popular attention and purchase acclaim, seeking advancement through crooked compliance and clever self-promotion, exhibit the corrupt conduct condemned by the ancients. Those who advance through deceptive words and improper means, betraying in adulthood what they learned in youth in order to secure wealth and rank, are talents cast aside by this enlightened court. To commit either fault is to diminish the glory of worthy predecessors and transgress the statutes of an enlightened ruler. This is no way to fulfil one’s own moral obligations and seek to repay imperial favour. Surely this would be not only a source of anxiety for those presiding over the examination, but also a disgrace to you candidates.
For this examination, Gu Sui, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Superintendent of Military Affairs in southern Jiangxi, brought peace and stability to the region, providing support upon which these literary undertakings depended. Xia Bao, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Li Bin, Dai Jing, Han Zhu, and Zhang He, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and Li Ao and Lu Kai, acting Regional Assistant Military Commissioners, provided protection and support…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
宣勞入
覲右參議柯喬僉事徐緯署都指
揮僉事路正始事協議刑部
署員外郎事主事盧璘奉使
玆土樂觀厥成法皆得書者
也直隸蘇州府儒學敎授向
洪邁謹序
punctuated:
宣勞；入覲右參議柯喬、僉事徐緯、署都指揮僉事路正，始事協議；刑部署員外郎事主事盧璘，奉使玆土，樂觀厥成。法皆得書者也。
直隸蘇州府儒學敎授向洪邁謹序。
translation_en:
…rendered meritorious service. Ke Qiao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner attending court audience; Xu Wei, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and Lu Zheng, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, joined in deliberations when the undertaking began. Lu Lin, a Secretary in the Ministry of Justice acting as Vice Director, came to this region on an official mission and was pleased to witness its successful completion. By established convention, all deserve to be recorded here.
Preface respectfully written by Xiang Hongmai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region.

translation_en:
Fujian Provincial Examination, Twenty-fifth Year of Jiajing (1546)

Supervising Official
Zhao Yingxiang, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Fujian, had the courtesy name Bozheng and was from Changsha Guard, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the yiwei year.

Proctors
Xiao Wan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Fujian, had the courtesy name Qidan and was from Jishui County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.
Li Sui, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of Fujian, had the courtesy name Bangliang and was from Fengcheng County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Examination Monitors
Zhou Yan, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, had the courtesy name Nanqiao and was from Jishui County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guiwei year.
Wang Dashou, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Fujian, had the courtesy name Shuke and was from Wuyuan County in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili). He became a metropolitan graduate in the jichou year.

Examiners
Xiang Hongmai, Professor in the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Jinggao and was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.
Li Mengyun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Wuyun and was from Linhai County, Zhejiang. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the gengzi year.

Associate Examiners
Xie Decong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Yiwen and was from Anfu County, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student in the dingyou year.
Fang Chunren, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zou County, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Shimian and was from Wuyuan County, Zhili. He became a tribute student in the jiawu year.
Zhu Wen, Instructor in the Confucian School of Linqu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Maozheng and was from Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. He became a tribute student in the jiawu year.
Chen Shou, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xun County, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Shupei. He was registered in an officer household of Xi’an Rear Guard, Shaanxi, and was a native of Macheng County, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the jiawu year.
Shao Dajue, Instructor in the Confucian School of Rugao County, Tai Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zixiu and was from Jingzhou Right Guard, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the gengzi year.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
極高明而道中庸
以友天下之善士爲未足又尚論古之人
頌其詩讀其書不知其人可乎是以論
其世也是尚友也
===
易
忠信所以進德也修辭立其誠所以居業
也
恒久也剛上而柔下雷風相與巽而動剛
柔皆應恒
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也
兼三才而兩之故易六畫而成卦分陰分
陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

極高明而道中庸。

以友天下之善士爲未足，又尚論古之人。頌其詩，讀其書，不知其人，可乎？是以論其世也。是尚友也。

易

忠信，所以進德也；修辭立其誠，所以居業也。

恒，久也。剛上而柔下，雷風相與，巽而動，剛柔皆應，恒。

夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。

兼三才而兩之，故易六畫而成卦；分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Zengzi replied, “Yes.” After the Master went out, the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Zengzi said, “The Master's Way is simply doing one's utmost for others and treating them as one would oneself.”

Reach the utmost height and illumination, yet follow the course of the Mean.

Finding it insufficient to befriend the good scholars of the world, one goes further and discusses the people of antiquity. Can one recite their poems and read their writings without knowing what sort of people they were? Thus one examines their age. This is befriending those of the distant past.

Book of Changes

Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue; refining one's words and establishing sincerity are the means of abiding in one's work.

Heng means enduring. The firm is above and the yielding below; thunder and wind interact; there is movement with gentle compliance; the firm and yielding all respond to one another: this is Heng, Duration.

The Changes is the means by which the sages fathom the depths and investigate the incipient signs of things.

It encompasses the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and doubles them; thus, in the Changes, six lines form a hexagram. It distinguishes yin and yang and employs yielding and firm lines alternately; thus, in the Changes, the six positions form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄

以閏月定四時成歲

皇極之敷言是彞是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
惟爾令德孝恭惟孝友于兄弟克施有政
命汝尹兹東郊敬哉昔周公師保萬民
民懷其德往慎乃司兹率厥常懋昭周
公之訓惟民其乂
詩
===
采采芣苢薄言采之采采芣苢薄言有之
采采芣苢薄言掇之采采芣苢薄言捋
之采采芣苢薄言袺之采采芣苢薄言
襭之
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
申伯之德柔惠且直揉此萬邦聞于四國
吉甫作誦其詩孔碩其風肆好以贈申
伯
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
punctuated:
以閏月定四時，成歲。

惟說式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。

皇極之敷言，是彞，是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓，是行，以近天子之光。

惟爾令德，孝恭；惟孝，友于兄弟，克施有政。

命汝尹兹東郊。敬哉！昔周公師保萬民，民懷其德。往慎乃司，兹率厥常，懋昭周公之訓，惟民其乂。

詩

采采芣苢，薄言采之。采采芣苢，薄言有之。采采芣苢，薄言掇之。采采芣苢，薄言捋之。采采芣苢，薄言袺之。采采芣苢，薄言襭之。

有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。

申伯之德，柔惠且直，揉此萬邦，聞于四國。吉甫作誦，其詩孔碩，其風肆好，以贈申伯。

有飶其香，邦家之光。有椒其馨，胡考之寧。
translation_en:
By means of intercalary months, fix the four seasons and complete the year.

You, Yue, must reverently carry out your charge, seek widely for men of outstanding talent and ability, and place them in the various offices.

The Sovereign's Ultimate, set forth in words, is the constant rule and the teaching; it is the teaching of the Sovereign on High. Let all the common people take the words setting forth the Ultimate as their instruction and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven.

Your excellent virtue is filial and reverent. Through filial devotion and friendship toward your brothers, you can extend these qualities to government.

I appoint you to govern this eastern suburb. Be reverent! Formerly, the Duke of Zhou instructed and protected the myriad people, and the people cherished his virtue. Go and attend carefully to your charge. Follow his constant principles here, and strive to make the Duke of Zhou's teachings manifest; then the people will be well governed.

Book of Odes

We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us pick it.
We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us take it.
We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us pluck it up.
We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us strip off its seeds.
We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us hold it in our lifted skirts.
We gather, gather the plantain;
Come, let us tuck our skirts into our belts and carry it.

Dense are the gathering clouds;
Abundantly the rain arises.
Rain upon our public fields,
And then reach our private fields as well.

The virtue of the Earl of Shen
Is gentle, kindly, and upright.
He brings harmony to these myriad states;
His fame is heard throughout the four quarters.
Jifu composed this song of praise;
His poem is exceedingly great,
Its influence far-reaching and good,
To present to the Earl of Shen.

Fragrant is its aroma,
The glory of the state and ruling house.
Pepper-sweet is its scent,
Bringing peace in ripe old age.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
春秋
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕吳子使札來聘
〔襄公二十有九年〕
丁亥楚子入陳〔宣公十有一年〕晉人宋人
衛人曹人同盟于清丘宋師伐陳衛
人救陳〔俱宣公十有二年〕
公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子
杞伯救鄭〔成公七年〕
===
秋季孫意如會晉韓起齊國弱宋華亥衛
北宮佗鄭罕虎曹人杞人于厥憖〔昭公
十有一年〕三月公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡
侯衛侯陳子鄭伯許男曹伯莒子邾子
頓子胡子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國
夏于召陵侵楚〔定公四年〕
禮記
君子察於此三者可以有志於學矣
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
punctuated:
春秋

夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕吳子使札來聘。〔襄公二十有九年〕

丁亥，楚子入陳。〔宣公十有一年〕晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘。宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔俱宣公十有二年〕

公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、杞伯救鄭。〔成公七年〕

秋，季孫意如會晉韓起、齊國弱、宋華亥、衛北宮佗、鄭罕虎、曹人、杞人于厥憖。〔昭公十有一年〕三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕

禮記

君子察於此三者，可以有志於學矣。

春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

In summer, the duke met at Kuiqiu with the Duke of Zhou, the royal chief minister; the Marquis of Qi; the heir of Song; the Marquis of Wei; the Earl of Zheng; the Baron of Xu; and the Earl of Cao. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi〕 The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit to our state. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang〕

On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xuan〕 Representatives of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao joined in a covenant at Qingqiu. The army of Song attacked Chen, and men of Wei came to Chen’s aid. 〔Both entries are from the twelfth year of Duke Xuan〕

The duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and the Earl of Qi to come to Zheng’s aid. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng〕

In autumn, Jisun Yiru met at Jueyin with Han Qi of Jin, Guo Ruo of Qi, Hua Hai of Song, Beigong Tuo of Wei, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Cao and Qi. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Zhao〕 In the third month, the duke met at Shaoling with the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi, and they invaded Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding〕

Book of Rites (Liji)

When the gentleman understands these three things, he can set his mind on learning.

Bringing forth in spring and nurturing growth in summer are benevolence; gathering in autumn and storing in winter are righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
義近於禮
所以治愛人禮爲大所以治禮敬爲大
溫良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也
第貳場
論
天地之所以爲大
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以戶部侍郎裴垍爲中書侍郎同平
章事誥〔元和三年〕
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士
謝表〔景德二年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
轉解官物
punctuated:
義近於禮。
所以治愛人，禮爲大；所以治禮，敬爲大。
溫良者，仁之本也；敬慎者，仁之地也；寬裕者，仁之作也；孫接者，仁之能也；禮節者，仁之貌也；言談者，仁之文也；歌樂者，仁之和也；分散者，仁之施也。
第貳場
論
天地之所以爲大。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬唐以戶部侍郎裴垍爲中書侍郎、同平章事誥〔元和三年〕。
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士謝表〔景德二年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
轉解官物。
translation_en:
…righteousness is close to ritual propriety.
For regulating love for others, ritual propriety is paramount; for regulating ritual propriety, reverence is paramount.
Gentleness and goodness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are its foundation; generosity and forbearance are its expression in action; humility in dealing with others is its capacity; ritual observances are its outward appearance; speech and conversation are its refinement; song and music are its harmony; distributing resources is its beneficent application.
Second Session
Discourse
What makes Heaven and Earth great.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these categories [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han granting the people remission of half of this year’s land tax. 〔Second year of Emperor Wen’s reign.〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang appointing Pei Ji, Vice Minister of Revenue, as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Joint Manager of Affairs. 〔Third year of Yuanhe.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song for Yang Yi’s appointment as a Hanlin Academician. 〔Second year of Jingde.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Forwarding government property.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
禁止迎送
遞送公文
侵占街道
第叁塲
策五道
問帝王之治必本於德而其爲政也必先
於教古今言治者必曰唐虞而稱聖德
者必曰堯舜雖功格於放勳而化成於
無虞然精一執中之教實開萬世心學
===
之源豈非推行有本而功化之極固不
待外求也我
太祖高皇帝
謨訓功烈度越百世今
聖政記
大明日曆之紀載煥如日星其於精一之傳若
合符節有可舉而言之與我
皇上懋德建中政化之成四達不悖是故
敬一有箴
punctuated:
禁止迎送。
遞送公文。
侵占街道。

第叁塲，策五道。

問：帝王之治必本於德，而其爲政也必先於教。古今言治者必曰唐虞，而稱聖德者必曰堯舜。雖功格於放勳，而化成於無虞，然精一執中之教，實開萬世心學之源，豈非推行有本，而功化之極固不待外求也？我太祖高皇帝謨訓功烈，度越百世。今《聖政記》《大明日曆》之紀載，煥如日星，其於精一之傳，若合符節，有可舉而言之與？我皇上懋德建中，政化之成，四達不悖。是故敬一有箴，
translation_en:
Prohibiting ceremonial receptions and send-offs.
Delivering official documents.
Encroaching upon streets.

Third session: five policy questions.

Question: The governance of emperors and kings must be rooted in virtue, and in administering government they must give priority to instruction. Those who discuss governance, past or present, invariably invoke Tang and Yu; those who praise sagely virtue invariably invoke Yao and Shun. Although their achievements attained “all-embracing merit” and their transforming influence brought about “freedom from anxiety” [?], it was their teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean that truly opened the wellspring of the learning of the mind for all generations. Was this not because their practice had a firm foundation, so that the highest achievements and transforming influence assuredly needed no external source?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao surpassed a hundred generations in his counsels, instructions, and glorious achievements. The accounts now recorded in the Record of Sagely Governance and the Daily Calendar of the Great Ming shine like the sun and stars. They accord with the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness like the matching halves of a tally. Can you cite and discuss examples?

Our reigning emperor diligently cultivates virtue and establishes the mean. The accomplishments of his government and transforming influence extend in all four directions without discord. Thus there is an Admonition on Revering the One…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
視聽言動心箴有註
微詞奧旨妙契往聖爾諸士服膺有年矣其
有能賛揚萬一以光昭
盛美者乎夫商周有頌詩人所以歌上德也
彰
盛實而宣
鴻休非士者職分事哉不然則與擊壤之夫
莫知帝力者等也
問先儒謂文以載道則道以文而明文以
===
道而傳者也六經之聖無心於文而至
道存焉不可尚矣嗣是則孔孟筆削於
春秋問答於門第固將以存志也而他
日無言之教不得已之辨蓋嘗屢致其
意焉豈道固不貴於有文耶漢之遷固
名山金匱之藏不可謂非一代之典也
而核直贍詳之文終愧六經豈其果無
所發明於道耶魏晉無文昔人所鄙浮
華纖麗之習誠不足以昭物而章軌也
punctuated:
視聽言動心箴有註，微詞奧旨，妙契往聖。爾諸士服膺有年矣，其有能賛揚萬一，以光昭盛美者乎？夫商周有頌，詩人所以歌上德也。彰盛實而宣鴻休，非士者職分事哉？不然，則與擊壤之夫莫知帝力者等也。
問：先儒謂文以載道，則道以文而明，文以道而傳者也。六經之聖，無心於文，而至道存焉，不可尚矣。嗣是，則孔孟筆削於春秋，問答於門第，固將以存志也。而他日無言之教、不得已之辨，蓋嘗屢致其意焉。豈道固不貴於有文耶？漢之遷固，名山金匱之藏，不可謂非一代之典也。而核直贍詳之文，終愧六經，豈其果無所發明於道耶？魏晉無文，昔人所鄙。浮華纖麗之習，誠不足以昭物而章軌也。
translation_en:
…and the Admonitions on Seeing, Hearing, Speaking, Acting, and the Mind have commentaries. Their subtle wording and profound meaning accord wondrously with the sages of old. You scholars have cherished these teachings for years. Is there anyone among you who can extol even a tiny part of them, thereby illuminating this magnificent excellence? Shang and Zhou had their hymns, through which the poets sang of their rulers’ virtue. Is it not the proper duty of scholars to make manifest these splendid accomplishments and proclaim these great blessings? Otherwise, you would be no different from the fellow who played at striking the earth, unaware of the emperor’s contribution to his well-being.
Question: Earlier Confucian scholars said that writing conveys the Way. Thus the Way is illuminated through writing, and writing is transmitted through the Way. The sageliness of the Six Classics lies in their having no deliberate concern with literary art, yet the ultimate Way resides within them: they cannot be surpassed. Thereafter, Confucius and Mencius, in composing and editing the Spring and Autumn Annals and in questions and answers within their schools [?], surely intended to preserve their aspirations. Yet on other occasions they repeatedly expressed their intentions through the ideas of teaching without words and disputing only when compelled. Could it be that the Way does not, after all, value literary expression? The works of Sima Qian and Ban Gu of the Han, preserved in famous mountains and metal coffers, cannot be denied the status of authoritative records of a dynasty. Yet their writing, exact and forthright, ample and detailed, ultimately falls short of the Six Classics. Can it really be that they did nothing to elucidate the Way? That Wei and Jin had no worthy writing was a judgment of scorn made by men of former times. The prevailing taste for superficial ornament and delicate elegance was indeed insufficient to illuminate things and make guiding principles manifest.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
其後言唐文者必歸韓柳而因文見道
之稱柳子不與焉其於昌黎何取言宋
文者惟美歐蘇而宋有文字四篇二子
無取焉其於歐蘇何病原道之作卓乎
有見矣而其時智如子房才如賈誼而
文足以經國制變者視韓子爲孰優太
極圖西銘諸作筆力高古矣而其時接
正傳於濂洛集大成於諸子者論其文
夫豈劣夫篤實而藝書美愛而久傳先
===
儒固有定說矣諸士子抱藝而來將必
有所發明而不徒事於文者幸究言之
以觀所蘊
問周禮周公治周之成書而貽世之典則
也後之言政者稽焉然是非頗謬而疑
信未協雖更以程朱蘇胡諸大儒之論
莫之取衷其詳可得而言與夫政莫重
於建官而法必先於出令唐虞惟百夏
商用倍周俗繁簡不應遽爾異也今五
punctuated:
其後言唐文者必歸韓柳，而因文見道之稱，柳子不與焉，其於昌黎何取？言宋文者惟美歐蘇，而宋有文字四篇，二子無取焉，其於歐蘇何病？《原道》之作，卓乎有見矣，而其時智如子房、才如賈誼，而文足以經國制變者，視韓子爲孰優？《太極圖》《西銘》諸作，筆力高古矣，而其時接正傳於濂洛、集大成於諸子者，論其文，夫豈劣？夫篤實而藝，書美愛而久傳，先儒固有定說矣。諸士子抱藝而來，將必有所發明而不徒事於文者，幸究言之，以觀所蘊。
問：周禮，周公治周之成書，而貽世之典則也，後之言政者稽焉。然是非頗謬，而疑信未協，雖更以程朱蘇胡諸大儒之論，莫之取衷，其詳可得而言與？夫政莫重於建官，而法必先於出令。唐虞惟百，夏商用倍，周俗繁簡不應遽爾異也。今五
translation_en:
…Thereafter, those discussing Tang prose invariably turn to Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan. Yet Liu is excluded from the praise of “perceiving the Way through writing.” What merits this praise in Changli [Han Yu]? Those discussing Song prose praise only Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. Yet in the assertion that the Song produced four pieces worthy of being called writing, neither man’s works are included. What fault is found with Ouyang and Su? Inquiry into the Way displays outstanding insight. Yet among those of that age whose wisdom resembled Zifang’s [Zhang Liang’s], whose talent resembled Jia Yi’s, and whose writing sufficed to order the state and manage change, who was superior when compared with Master Han? Such works as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription possess an elevated, antique literary power. Yet those of that age who received the orthodox transmission from Lian and Luo and brought the teachings of the various masters to their fullest synthesis—could their writing possibly be inferior? As for being substantial and accomplished, and writings being beautiful, cherished, and long transmitted [?], earlier Confucian scholars already had settled explanations. You candidates have come bearing your literary accomplishments; surely you have insights to disclose beyond merely attending to literary form. Please discuss these matters fully, so that we may see what you hold within.
Question: The Rites of Zhou is the completed record of the Duke of Zhou’s governance of Zhou and a body of normative standards bequeathed to posterity. Later writers on government have consulted it. Yet judgments of its merits and faults diverge considerably, and doubts and convictions remain unreconciled. Even after considering the arguments of such great Confucian scholars as Cheng, Zhu, Su, and Hu, no balanced conclusion has been reached. Can the particulars be explained? In government, nothing is more important than establishing offices; in instituting rules, issuing commands must come first. Under Tang and Yu there were only a hundred officials, and under Xia and Shang twice that number. The complexity or simplicity of Zhou customs cannot have differed so abruptly. Now, the five…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
官之屬自內史宮正以至鄉師甸師胥
廛封牧藁校雍薙之類衆至數萬而比
閭卒伍之長不與焉不知畿甸千里之
內爲田幾井而又有王官公族食采四
地之一此等將仰給於公抑自食其力
耶古者爲而不有應而不求百姓日遷
善而不知周去古未遠也今歲朔孟仲
考藝讀法詢事振旅凡大聚會月必屢
至而飲射酺蜡之類不與焉不知一月
===
之內爲日幾何而又有供給徵召蒐獼
田狩之役此等豈在官之庶人抑南畝
之耕夫耶夫選用旣衆理難必其皆賢
徵會不時勢不能於無擾况代耕不足
而妨業尤多豈古今政俗若是不同耶
昔人謂如有用我者執此以往講求不
素則推行必悖爾諸士固豫養以待用
者其有以告我
問天地之氣下爲河嶽上則列星經緯昭
punctuated:
官之屬，自內史、宮正以至鄉師、甸師、胥、廛、封、牧、藁、校、雍、薙之類，衆至數萬，而比閭卒伍之長不與焉。不知畿甸千里之內，爲田幾井，而又有王官公族食采四地之一，此等將仰給於公，抑自食其力耶？古者爲而不有，應而不求，百姓日遷善而不知。周去古未遠也，今歲朔孟仲，考藝、讀法、詢事、振旅，凡大聚會，月必屢至，而飲射酺蜡之類不與焉。不知一月之內爲日幾何，而又有供給、徵召、蒐獼、田狩之役，此等豈在官之庶人，抑南畝之耕夫耶？夫選用旣衆，理難必其皆賢；徵會不時，勢不能於無擾。况代耕不足，而妨業尤多，豈古今政俗若是不同耶？昔人謂：「如有用我者，執此以往。」講求不素，則推行必悖。爾諸士固豫養以待用者，其有以告我。

問：天地之氣，下爲河嶽，上則列星，經緯昭
translation_en:
…the personnel belonging to these offices, from the Interior Secretary and Palace Rectifier down to the District Preceptors, Directors of the Royal Fields, and officials concerned with market administration, market premises, boundaries, pastures, fodder, horses, waterways [?], and clearing vegetation, number tens of thousands. This does not include the heads of neighborhood and military units. How many well-field units of farmland are there within the royal domain, a thousand li square? Moreover, royal officials and members of the ducal lineages draw revenues from a quarter of its land. Are all these people to depend upon public provision, or to support themselves by their own labor?

In antiquity, rulers acted without claiming possession and responded without making demands; the common people daily advanced toward goodness without knowing it. The Zhou was not far removed from antiquity. Yet here, at the beginning of the year and in the first and second months of the seasons [?], there were assessments of accomplishments, readings of laws, consultations on affairs, and military reviews. Major assemblies occurred repeatedly each month, even without counting communal drinking ceremonies, archery ceremonies, communal feasts, and year-end agricultural sacrifices. How many days are there in a month? There were also duties of providing supplies, answering summonses, and participating in seasonal hunts [?]. Were those performing these duties commoners employed in government service, or farmers who tilled the southern fields?

With so many people selected for employment, it would plainly be difficult to ensure that all were worthy. With summonses to assemblies issued at irregular times, disturbance would necessarily be unavoidable. Moreover, remuneration in lieu of farming was insufficient, while interference with people’s occupations was especially frequent. Could governmental practices and customs in antiquity and today really differ so greatly? A man of former times said: “If someone were to employ me, I would take this with me and proceed.” Unless one has studied and investigated it beforehand, putting it into practice will certainly go awry. You scholars are, of course, cultivating yourselves in advance while awaiting employment. Tell me what you have to say on this.

Question: The vital force of Heaven and Earth forms rivers and mountains below and the arrayed stars above, ranged lengthwise and crosswise in shining…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
回以垂天象匯流盤峙以奠地宜莫不
有理焉古昔聖王知其然故立司天司
地之官而星官堪輿之說昉於史傳矣
粵嘗稽之黃帝羲和之命車區之占唐
虞鳥火之識璣衡之在何當時以為急
務而後世之業其官者乃反有不知與
星象之書古凡幾家誰為最著今其所
傳者可得而聞其要與漢唐而下精於
其術者代不乏人亦可舉而言其優劣
===
與若堪輿之書今則無傳矣僅見於周
禮者有辨方正位之辭而求其制則惟
土圭測景而已其作用之遺意猶有可
考者與冬官土宜之辨以相民宅歷代
形勝之據以建國都蓋必有所見也其
亦可得而言與或者又謂懸象在天其
本在地於是又有分野之說而論者疑
其星野之不相值是果然與昔之人有
能推古聖人敬天理地之意而著為定
punctuated: 回以垂天象，匯流盤峙以奠地宜，莫不有理焉。古昔聖王知其然，故立司天司地之官，而星官堪輿之說昉於史傳矣。粵嘗稽之，黃帝羲和之命、車區之占，唐虞鳥火之識、璣衡之在，何當時以為急務，而後世之業其官者乃反有不知與？星象之書，古凡幾家？誰為最著？今其所傳者，可得而聞其要與？漢唐而下，精於其術者代不乏人，亦可舉而言其優劣與？若堪輿之書，今則無傳矣。僅見於《周禮》者，有辨方正位之辭，而求其制，則惟土圭測景而已。其作用之遺意，猶有可考者與？冬官土宜之辨，以相民宅；歷代形勝之據，以建國都，蓋必有所見也。其亦可得而言與？或者又謂懸象在天，其本在地，於是又有分野之說，而論者疑其星野之不相值，是果然與？昔之人有能推古聖人敬天理地之意，而著為定
translation_en:
…revolving in brilliance to display the celestial signs, and gathering into streams or standing in massive heights to establish the proper configuration of the earth: all have their underlying principles. The sage kings of antiquity understood this, and therefore established officials charged with overseeing Heaven and Earth. Accounts of the stellar offices and of geomancy thus began to appear in historical records and traditions. I have examined the Yellow Emperor’s appointment of Xi and He and the prognostications of Chequ [?], and, in the times of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, the recognition of the Bird and Fire stars and the placement of the armillary instrument [?]. Why were these regarded as urgent duties at the time, while among those who held such offices in later ages there were actually some who knew nothing of them? How many schools of writings on celestial phenomena were there in antiquity? Which was the most distinguished? May we hear the essentials of those writings transmitted today? From the Han and Tang onward, every age had people proficient in these arts. Can you also name them and discuss their relative merits?

As for writings on geomancy, none are now transmitted. What little appears in the Rites of Zhou includes statements about distinguishing directions and correctly determining positions; yet when we seek the actual procedures, we find only the measurement of shadows with the earth tablet, or tugui. Can anything still be ascertained of the purposes underlying its use? The distinctions of suitable soils made by the Ministry of Works served to select dwelling sites for the people, while successive dynasties relied on advantageous terrain to establish their capitals. Surely these practices rested on some discernment. Can this too be explained? Some further say that the signs suspended in Heaven have their roots on Earth. Hence there is also the doctrine of corresponding celestial and terrestrial regions. Yet commentators doubt whether the stellar regions and their terrestrial counterparts actually match. Is this indeed so? Among people of former times, there were those able to develop the intentions of the ancient sages in revering Heaven and ordering Earth, and to set them down as definitive…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
論者君子取之若然則義非高遠道存
民用是亦學者之所當講也諸生宜毋
諉之術數之學
問經國致治莫切於利用而用之利者莫
踰於錢幣所以通貨源而資民生也粤
稽之古有謂之泉有謂之布者其義何
居有鑄於歷山有鑄於莊山者其意安
在漢之筴錢八銖四銖五銖名亦多矣
何為而五銖獨用唐之開元天寶乾元
===
制亦善矣何為而開元可行迨至宋元
更造不一惟我
國家因時酌宜設局鼓鑄兼用前代行之四
方而大江以南壤地千里錢不為市何
耶或謂南北異俗不可强同然嶺海之
間以之貿遷豈通於彼而獨塞於此乎
玆欲使錢幣大行而民情俱協抑何道
可以致之古有外府泉府邦布邦市之
法不知可倣而行之否乎夫稽實致用
punctuated:
論者，君子取之。若然，則義非高遠，道存民用，是亦學者之所當講也。諸生宜毋諉之術數之學。

問：經國致治，莫切於利用，而用之利者，莫踰於錢幣，所以通貨源而資民生也。粤稽之古，有謂之泉，有謂之布者，其義何居？有鑄於歷山，有鑄於莊山者，其意安在？漢之筴錢、八銖、四銖、五銖，名亦多矣，何為而五銖獨用？唐之開元、天寶、乾元，制亦善矣，何為而開元可行？迨至宋元，更造不一。惟我國家，因時酌宜，設局鼓鑄，兼用前代，行之四方。而大江以南，壤地千里，錢不為市，何耶？或謂南北異俗，不可强同，然嶺海之間，以之貿遷，豈通於彼而獨塞於此乎？玆欲使錢幣大行，而民情俱協，抑何道可以致之？古有外府、泉府、邦布、邦市之法，不知可倣而行之否乎？夫稽實致用，
translation_en:
…such conclusions are accepted by gentlemen. If so, their principles are neither lofty nor remote: the Way resides in what serves the people’s needs. This, too, is something scholars ought to investigate. You candidates should not dismiss it as a matter belonging to the arts of calculation and divination.

Question: In ordering the state and achieving good government, nothing is more pressing than making resources useful; and among useful instruments, none surpasses coinage, which facilitates the circulation of goods and sustains the people’s livelihood. Looking back to antiquity, we find money called quan, “spring,” and bu, “cloth.” What do these names mean? Some coins were cast at Lishan and others at Zhuangshan. What was the intention behind this? Under the Han, there were many names for coins: ce coins [?], eight-zhu coins, four-zhu coins, and five-zhu coins. Why were five-zhu coins alone retained in use? Under the Tang, the Kaiyuan, Tianbao, and Qianyuan coinages were also well designed. Why was the Kaiyuan coinage the one that proved practicable? By the Song and Yuan, coinages were repeatedly replaced and newly cast.

Our own dynasty has adapted its measures to the times, establishing bureaus to cast coins and using coins of earlier dynasties alongside them, circulating these throughout the realm. Yet south of the great Yangzi River, across a territory extending a thousand li, coins are not used in market transactions. Why is this? Some say that northern and southern customs differ and cannot be forcibly made uniform. Yet in the region between the mountains of Lingnan and the sea, coins are used in trade. How can they circulate there but be obstructed here alone? If we now wish coinage to circulate widely and to accord fully with the people’s preferences, by what means can this be achieved? In antiquity there were arrangements for the Outer Treasury and the Treasury of Exchange, for state currency and state markets. Could these be emulated and put into practice? As for investigating actual conditions and putting knowledge to practical use…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
通變宜民亦士之所當究願著于篇以
觀所學
punctuated: 通變宜民，亦士之所當究。願著于篇，以觀所學。
translation_en: …adapting to changing circumstances for the people's benefit is also something scholars ought to investigate. Please set out your views in an essay, so that we may assess your learning.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
洪世遷
考試官學正李批詞不費而意義自見蓋聞聖
敬而有得者
考試官教授向批一貫之旨發於忠恕意語渾
𩓑僅見此作
===
大賢聞聖道而有得而因以發之也夫道一而
已大賢唯於有聞而發於所問聖門授受之妙
可知矣昔曾子造深於眞積而功竭於末由夫
子知其有得也故呼其名而告之以為道惟一
本而物有殊致渾然在中者實涵萬化之原寂
然不動者自妙順應之感蓋守之至約則裕用
而不窮而操之有要則多學非所事也曾子聞
言而悟應聲而唯不必擬議於言語之間而眞
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

洪世遷

考試官學正李批：「詞不費而意義自見，蓋聞聖敬而有得者。」

考試官教授向批：「一貫之旨，發於忠恕，意語渾𩓑，僅見此作。」

大賢聞聖道而有得，而因以發之也。夫道一而已，大賢唯於有聞而發於所問，聖門授受之妙可知矣。昔曾子造深於眞積，而功竭於末由。夫子知其有得也，故呼其名而告之，以為道惟一本，而物有殊致；渾然在中者，實涵萬化之原；寂然不動者，自妙順應之感。蓋守之至約，則裕用而不窮；而操之有要，則多學非所事也。曾子聞言而悟，應聲而唯，不必擬議於言語之間，而眞
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded through by a single principle.” Zengzi said, “Yes.” When the Master went out, his disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Zengzi said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of doing one’s utmost for others and treating others as oneself.”

Hong Shiqian

Comment by Examiner Li, School Director: “The wording is economical, yet the meaning emerges of itself. This is surely the work of one who has heard the sage’s reverence [?] and gained understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: “The purport of the single unifying principle is brought out through doing one’s utmost for others and treating others as oneself. Thought and expression are rounded and whole [?]; only in this composition have I seen this.”

The great worthy heard the sage’s Way and gained understanding, and accordingly expounded it. The Way is but one. The great worthy assented to what he heard and expounded it in response to a question: here we may perceive the subtlety of transmission and reception within the sage’s school.

In former times, Zengzi attained profound understanding through the steady accumulation of genuine effort, yet exhausted his efforts at the point where there seemed no way forward. The Master knew that he had gained understanding, and therefore called him by name and instructed him: the Way has but one root, while things have their distinct manifestations. What abides within as an undivided whole truly contains the source of all transformations; what remains still and unmoving possesses of itself the wondrous capacity to respond fittingly to what affects it. Thus, when what one holds to is supremely simple, its application is ample and inexhaustible; when one grasps the essential, extensive learning is no longer one’s pursuit. Zengzi heard these words and understood, immediately responding with assent. He had no need to deliberate over the words, but truly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
有得於口耳之外者矣然道不可以易聞而學
不容以頓悟此門人何謂之問所以發於夫子
旣出之後也曾子曉之以為至道難言而近取
自足故四教無隱不聞所謂忠乎盡己不欺而
恕之體以立一言可行不聞所謂恕乎推心及
物而忠之用以行下學之成功即上達之心法
不可以殊觀也聖人之能事亦學問之極功初
非有二致也是則道有眞見則言無費辭觀於
忠恕之喻而一貫之唯夫豈徒聞也哉大抵聖
===
教無隱而至道難聞一貫之旨固門人所共承
而曾子所獨唯豈非時雨之化溥物均施而生
息之機隨分各足者哉是故四勿請事惟顏氏
子直任而不辭而方信忽疑雖穎悟如子貢而
猶有所未達也故曰參也竟以魯得之
極高明而道中庸
周欽
同考試官教諭邵批講高明中庸處詞理精到
獨異諸作錄之
punctuated:
有得於口耳之外者矣。然道不可以易聞，而學不容以頓悟，此門人「何謂」之問所以發於夫子旣出之後也。曾子曉之以為至道難言，而近取自足。故四教無隱，不聞所謂忠乎？盡己不欺，而恕之體以立。一言可行，不聞所謂恕乎？推心及物，而忠之用以行。下學之成功，即上達之心法，不可以殊觀也。聖人之能事，亦學問之極功，初非有二致也。是則道有眞見，則言無費辭。觀於忠恕之喻，而一貫之唯，夫豈徒聞也哉？大抵聖教無隱，而至道難聞。一貫之旨，固門人所共承，而曾子所獨唯，豈非時雨之化溥物均施，而生息之機隨分各足者哉？是故四勿請事，惟顏氏子直任而不辭；而方信忽疑，雖穎悟如子貢，而猶有所未達也。故曰：「參也竟以魯得之。」

極高明而道中庸
周欽
同考試官教諭邵批：「講高明中庸處，詞理精到，獨異諸作，錄之。」
translation_en:
…had attained an understanding beyond what passes between mouth and ear. Yet the Way cannot readily be learned merely by hearing, nor can learning be accomplished through sudden enlightenment. This is why the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” only after the Master had gone out. Master Zeng enlightened them: the ultimate Way is difficult to express, yet seeking it close at hand is sufficient. Thus, nothing was concealed in the Master's four teachings: had they not heard of wholeheartedness? By fully exerting oneself without deception, one establishes the substance of reciprocity. As for the single word that could guide one's conduct, had they not heard of reciprocity? By extending one's own heart to others, one puts wholeheartedness into practice. Success in learning what is below is precisely the method of the mind by which one attains what is above; these cannot be regarded as separate. What the sage can accomplish is also the utmost achievement of learning: there were never two distinct ends. Thus, where there is genuine insight into the Way, words are not wasted. Considering his explanation in terms of wholeheartedness and reciprocity, could his assent to the teaching of a single thread running through all have amounted merely to hearing it?

Generally, the sage's teaching conceals nothing, yet the ultimate Way is difficult to apprehend. The teaching of the single thread was received by all the disciples, but Master Zeng alone responded with assent. Is this not like the transforming influence of timely rain, which spreads equally over all things, while each possesses a sufficient capacity for growth according to its own measure? Thus, when asking to put the four prohibitions into practice, only Yan Hui directly took on the responsibility without declining it. Others had scarcely begun to believe before suddenly doubting; even one as perceptive as Zigong still had things he had not understood. Hence the saying: “Shen ultimately attained it through his dullness.”

“Reach the utmost height and brilliance, yet follow the Mean in ordinary practice”
By Zhou Qin.

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: “In its exposition of height and brilliance and the Mean in ordinary practice, both the language and the reasoning are refined and exact. It stands apart from the other compositions. Include it in the record.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批說理明白而辭意渾融中庸
義當如此可式
考試官學正李批簡潔明當蓋精於中庸之理者
考試官教授向批辭不費而理自足
心復其體而事循其則君子修凝之功也蓋高
明者心之體而中庸者事之則也君子復之循
之而所以存心致知者於是盡矣中庸之意謂
夫天下之道統於吾心而散於事理心不復其
本然則無以為致用之體事不究其當然則無
===
以周全體之用非所以合内外也君子之學何
如哉是故至虛之涵而清通無際至靈之瑩而
旁燭無疆吾心之體本高明也而累之於欲則
卑暗矣其必務崇有功而使其高者不少屈於
狥物渾然天啓之衷與太虛同其象焉緝煕有
學而使其明者不少昏於外誘洞然神發之知
於萬物無不照焉如是則心之體以立矣然豈
可徒狥于内而無所用乎彼物齊於正道而體
無所偏行本於定理而人不可易萬事之則有
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：說理明白，而辭意渾融，中庸義當如此，可式。
考試官學正李批：簡潔明當，蓋精於中庸之理者。
考試官教授向批：辭不費而理自足。
心復其體而事循其則，君子修凝之功也。蓋高明者，心之體；而中庸者，事之則也。君子復之循之，而所以存心致知者於是盡矣。中庸之意謂：夫天下之道，統於吾心而散於事理。心不復其本然，則無以為致用之體；事不究其當然，則無以周全體之用，非所以合内外也。君子之學何如哉？是故至虛之涵而清通無際，至靈之瑩而旁燭無疆，吾心之體本高明也。而累之於欲，則卑暗矣。其必務崇有功，而使其高者不少屈於狥物，渾然天啓之衷，與太虛同其象焉；緝煕有學，而使其明者不少昏於外誘，洞然神發之知，於萬物無不照焉。如是，則心之體以立矣。然豈可徒狥于内而無所用乎？彼物齊於正道而體無所偏，行本於定理而人不可易，萬事之則有
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear, and the language and meaning form a harmonious whole. This is how the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean should be explained. It may serve as a model.”
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “Concise, clear, and apt: surely the work of someone with a refined understanding of the principles of the Doctrine of the Mean.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “The language is economical, yet the reasoning is complete.”
Restoring the mind to its essential constitution and conducting affairs according to their proper standards—these are the accomplishments of the gentleman’s cultivation and consolidation. Loftiness and illumination are the essential constitution of the mind; centrality and constancy are the standards governing affairs. The gentleman restores the former and follows the latter, thereby fulfilling all that is required to preserve the mind and extend knowledge. The meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean is this: the Way of all under Heaven is unified in our minds and distributed among the principles of affairs. Unless the mind recovers its original condition, there is no essential foundation from which to put it into practice; unless one thoroughly investigates what is fitting in affairs, one cannot realize the full functioning of that entire constitution. This would not unite the inner and the outer. What, then, should the gentleman’s learning be like?
Utterly empty in its capacity to contain, clear and unimpeded without limit; supremely numinous in its brilliance, illuminating all around without bounds: the essential constitution of our mind is originally lofty and luminous. Yet burden it with desires, and it becomes low and dark. One must therefore work to exalt it, achieving results so that its loftiness is not diminished in the slightest by subservience to things. Then the undivided inner nature disclosed by Heaven shares the aspect of the Great Void. Through learning, one must continually brighten it, so that its illumination is not dimmed in the slightest by external enticements. Then its penetrating awareness, issuing from its numinous power, illuminates every one of the myriad things. In this way the mind’s essential constitution is established. Yet could one merely devote oneself to the inner and never put it to use? Things accord with the correct Way, and their constitution is free from partiality; conduct rests upon settled principles that people cannot alter. The standards governing all affairs possess …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
中庸也而動之以私則差謬矣又必精裁度於
物來之應而用中善天下之則理有至當吾不
敢以高明之資而過於範圍也詳擬議於制事
之宜而庸行會天下之趨道有共由吾不敢以
偏陂之私而舍其正路也如是則道之用以行
矣夫體立而心存用行而知致内外交養所以
脩德也而道不於是凝哉抑觀子思上言君子
致廣大盡精微矣此復言其極高明而道中庸
夫廣大若蕩高明若虛也然道體之大非高廣
===
則無以容之而且精微之盡中庸之道則行之
而有常析之而不亂矣此君子之所以道會小
大而作聖之功於是為盡後之儒者乃主其一
偏而滋學者之惑噫其何以與於斯
以友天下之善士為未足又尚論古之人
頌其詩讀其書不知其人可乎是以論
其世也是尚友也
陳南星
同考試官教諭夏批講頌詩讀書作平日工夫
punctuated:
中庸也，而動之以私則差謬矣。又必精裁度於物來之應，而用中善天下之則。理有至當，吾不敢以高明之資而過於範圍也；詳擬議於制事之宜，而庸行會天下之趨。道有共由，吾不敢以偏陂之私而舍其正路也。如是，則道之用以行矣。夫體立而心存，用行而知致，内外交養，所以脩德也，而道不於是凝哉？抑觀子思上言君子致廣大、盡精微矣，此復言其極高明而道中庸。夫廣大若蕩，高明若虛也，然道體之大，非高廣則無以容之。而且精微之盡、中庸之道，則行之而有常，析之而不亂矣。此君子之所以道會小大，而作聖之功於是為盡。後之儒者乃主其一偏，而滋學者之惑。噫！其何以與於斯？
以友天下之善士為未足，又尚論古之人。頌其詩，讀其書，不知其人，可乎？是以論其世也，是尚友也。
陳南星
同考試官教諭夏批：講頌詩讀書作平日工夫。
translation_en:
…the constant mean; but when selfish motives set them in motion, they become distorted and erroneous. One must also exercise precise judgment in responding to things as they arise, applying the mean to perfect the standards of the world. Principle has its utmost appropriateness: I dare not, on the strength of my lofty and luminous capacities, exceed its bounds. One must deliberate carefully about what is fitting in managing affairs, and through ordinary conduct bring together the courses pursued throughout the world. The Way has a path that all share: I dare not abandon its proper road out of selfish partiality. In this way, the functioning of the Way is put into practice. When the substance is established, the mind is preserved; when its functioning is enacted, knowledge is fully extended. Cultivating the inner and outer together is how one cultivates virtue. Does not the Way thereby become firmly established? Moreover, consider how Zisi spoke above of the gentleman extending himself to breadth and greatness while exhausting the subtle and minute. Here he again speaks of reaching the utmost height and luminosity while following the constant mean. Breadth and greatness may seem unbounded, and height and luminosity may seem empty; yet without height and breadth, nothing could accommodate the greatness of the Way’s substance. Furthermore, exhausting the subtle and minute and following the constant mean ensure that practice has constancy and analysis does not become confused. This is how the gentleman unites the small and the great in the Way, bringing the work of becoming a sage to completion. Later Confucians instead champion one partial aspect, increasing the confusion of learners. Alas! How could they participate in this achievement?
Considering friendship with the good men of the world insufficient, one goes further and discusses the people of antiquity. Reciting their poems and reading their writings, can one fail to know what sort of people they were? Thus one examines the age in which they lived. This is reaching back to befriend the ancients.
Chen Nanxing
Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: He explains reciting poetry and reading writings as the work of daily cultivation…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
最爲有見他作未及此也
同考試官教諭方批順理發揮得孟子立言之意無
結末歸之立志可占所養
考試官學正李批說尚友處得旨
考試官教授向批辭意精雅
大賢言士能進友古人則取善遠矣夫進善無
止法也友盡天下而復求古人斯其爲善進也
哉昔孟子告萬章取友至此若謂士之取善以
言乎廣則天下以爲量以言乎遠則千古以爲
===
徒今夫天下之善士吾旣得而友之矣然善士
之成名不可多見於斯世而其人之純德懿行
容有未備於所友者乎是未可以遽自足也君
子之取友不必盡出於一時而古人之令聞百
世孰非吾所當論交者乎是不可以弗之考也
是何也蓋古人往矣而其道在詩書吾旣嘗誦
其詩矣曰是古人之和聲述志者也然詩其聲
也其人不在是也習其聲而不知其人君子有
弗取焉又嘗讀其書矣曰是古人之立言道事
punctuated:
最爲有見，他作未及此也。
同考試官教諭方批：順理發揮，得孟子立言之意無。結末歸之立志，可占所養。
考試官學正李批：說尚友處得旨。
考試官教授向批：辭意精雅。
大賢言士能進友古人，則取善遠矣。夫進善無止法也，友盡天下而復求古人，斯其爲善進也哉！昔孟子告萬章取友至此，若謂士之取善，以言乎廣，則天下以爲量；以言乎遠，則千古以爲徒。今夫天下之善士，吾旣得而友之矣。然善士之成名，不可多見於斯世，而其人之純德懿行，容有未備於所友者乎？是未可以遽自足也。君子之取友，不必盡出於一時，而古人之令聞百世，孰非吾所當論交者乎？是不可以弗之考也。是何也？蓋古人往矣，而其道在詩書。吾旣嘗誦其詩矣，曰：是古人之和聲述志者也。然詩其聲也，其人不在是也。習其聲而不知其人，君子有弗取焉。又嘗讀其書矣，曰：是古人之立言道事
translation_en:
…shows exceptional insight; the other compositions do not attain this.

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, an Instructor: The exposition follows the underlying principles and grasps Mencius’s intention in making this statement [?]. The conclusion returns to establishing one’s resolve, revealing the writer’s cultivation.

Comment by Examiner Li, a School Instructor: The discussion of befriending the ancients captures the essential meaning.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, a Professor: The language and ideas are refined and elegant.

The great worthy says that when a scholar can advance to befriending the ancients, his search for goodness reaches far indeed. There is no fixed stopping point in advancing toward goodness. Having befriended worthy men throughout the world, to seek further among the ancients—is this not progress in goodness? When Mencius spoke to Wan Zhang about choosing friends, his discussion reached this point. It was as though he were saying that, in a scholar’s search for goodness, its breadth takes the whole world as its measure, while its reach takes the men of a thousand ages as companions.

Now, I have already found and befriended the good scholars of the world. Yet good scholars who have achieved renown are not often encountered in this age. Might there be pure virtues and admirable conduct not fully represented among those I have befriended? Thus I cannot hastily rest content. A gentleman need not choose all his friends from a single age. Among the ancients whose fine reputations endure for a hundred generations, who is there with whom I should not consider forming a friendship? Thus I cannot fail to investigate them.

Why is this? The ancients have passed away, but their Way remains in their poems and writings. I have recited their poems, saying: These are the harmonious sounds through which the ancients expressed their aspirations. Yet poems are their voices; the men themselves are not contained therein. To become familiar with their voices without knowing the men is something a gentleman will not accept. I have also read their writings, saying: These are the means by which the ancients set forth their words and recounted events…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
者也然書其言也其人則其行也得其言而弗
求其行吾不知其可焉故必稽載籍之所傳徵
往哲之遺行而其動爲世道於當時者吾將麗
其澤以自益卽詩書之陳言考古人之實事而
其行爲世法於平生者吾將通其志而定交如
是則其於取友也不亦尚矣哉蓋友以天下特
兼善天下耳而復能求之古人則其取善以自
淑者當必與終古而俱遠矣夫何有窮已耶友
盡一世特一世之士耳而至於取友前世則其
===
觀人以成己者方且等百世而上之矣夫何可
限量耶取友之道於是爲盡而士之爲士蓋將
終其身而不能以一日無友矣章也其知此義
哉大抵士生天地間欲爲千百世之名則當有
千百世之志故伊尹之慕道堯舜孟子之願學
孔子皆志定也厥後一德相湯以成聖業七篇
傳道以詔萬世而伊孟之名卒與堯舜孔子竝
傳使其在當時訑訑然曰我旣爲天下善士矣
則考德其時信莫有過之而未必有後世之名
punctuated: 者也。然書其言也，其人則其行也。得其言而弗求其行，吾不知其可焉。故必稽載籍之所傳，徵往哲之遺行，而其動爲世道於當時者，吾將麗其澤以自益；卽詩書之陳言，考古人之實事，而其行爲世法於平生者，吾將通其志而定交。如是則其於取友也，不亦尚矣哉！蓋友以天下，特兼善天下耳，而復能求之古人，則其取善以自淑者，當必與終古而俱遠矣，夫何有窮已耶？友盡一世，特一世之士耳，而至於取友前世，則其觀人以成己者，方且等百世而上之矣，夫何可限量耶？取友之道於是爲盡，而士之爲士，蓋將終其身而不能以一日無友矣。章也，其知此義哉！大抵士生天地間，欲爲千百世之名，則當有千百世之志。故伊尹之慕道堯舜，孟子之願學孔子，皆志定也。厥後一德相湯以成聖業，七篇傳道以詔萬世，而伊孟之名卒與堯舜孔子竝傳。使其在當時訑訑然曰：「我旣爲天下善士矣。」則考德其時，信莫有過之，而未必有後世之名
translation_en:
…were the means by which the ancients set forth their teachings and related affairs. Yet writings are their words, whereas the people themselves are revealed in their conduct. To obtain their words without seeking to understand their conduct—I do not see how this could be acceptable. Thus one must examine what the records transmit and seek evidence of the conduct left behind by past worthies. Where their actions upheld the moral order in their own time, I shall draw upon their beneficent influence to improve myself. Through the words preserved in the Odes and Documents, I shall investigate the actual deeds of the ancients. Where their lifelong conduct served as a model for the world, I shall comprehend their aspirations and establish friendship with them. Is this not an exalted way of choosing friends?

To take friends throughout the world is merely to embrace the goodness found throughout the world. But if one can also seek friends among the ancients, then one’s efforts to draw upon goodness and improve oneself must extend as far as all antiquity. How could there be any end to them? Even if one befriends everyone in an age, they are only the scholars of that age. But when one comes to choose friends from earlier ages, one’s observation of others as a means of perfecting oneself reaches back through a hundred generations and beyond. How could it be bounded or measured? Here the way of choosing friends reaches its fullest extent. A scholar, in being a scholar, cannot therefore pass even a single day of his life without friends. Zhang, may you understand this meaning!

In general, a scholar born between Heaven and Earth who wishes to win a name lasting a thousand or a hundred generations must possess aspirations reaching across a thousand or a hundred generations. Thus Yi Yin’s yearning for the Way of Yao and Shun, and Mengzi’s wish to learn from Kongzi, both arose from firmly settled aspirations. Thereafter, Yi Yin, with undivided virtue, assisted Tang in accomplishing the work of a sage; Mengzi transmitted the Way in seven books to instruct ten thousand generations. In the end, the names of Yi Yin and Mengzi were handed down alongside those of Yao, Shun, and Kongzi. Had they arrogantly declared in their own time, “I am already a good scholar of the world,” then, judging their virtue against that of their contemporaries, surely none would have surpassed them; yet they would not necessarily have attained a reputation among later generations…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
如此也矣孟子之告萬章即其所自爲志者而
惜乎章之不足以語此
易
忠信所以進德也修辭立其誠所以居業
也
周欽
同考試官教諭邵批進德居業不外乎誠此作發
揮明白而於居業處尤善體貼殆知學者
同考試官教諭陳批發得精詳居業意出錄之
===
考試官學正李批體認親切語不煩而意盡
考試官教授向批簡潔
内外一本於誠君子進脩之功也夫誠者聖功
之本也君子德業之盛非誠而能之乎文言申
九三乾乾惕若之意謂夫及時進脩者君子之
心合一爲功者進脩之道是故蘊之而爲德行
君子固欲其進矣是豈可以襲取乎哉必其主
於心者存誠以立其體克己以復其初志意之
所在旣盡己而無偽念慮之所發復以實而不
punctuated:
如此也矣。孟子之告萬章，即其所自爲志者，而惜乎章之不足以語此！

易

忠信所以進德也，修辭立其誠，所以居業也。

周欽

同考試官教諭邵批：進德居業不外乎誠，此作發揮明白，而於居業處尤善體貼，殆知學者。

同考試官教諭陳批：發得精詳，居業意出，錄之。

考試官學正李批：體認親切，語不煩而意盡。

考試官教授向批：簡潔。

内外一本於誠，君子進脩之功也。夫誠者，聖功之本也。君子德業之盛，非誠而能之乎？文言申九三乾乾惕若之意，謂夫及時進脩者，君子之心；合一爲功者，進脩之道。是故蘊之而爲德行，君子固欲其進矣。是豈可以襲取乎哉？必其主於心者，存誠以立其體，克己以復其初。志意之所在，旣盡己而無偽；念慮之所發，復以實而不
translation_en:
…of such distinction. What Mengzi told Wan Zhang was precisely what he had set his own aspirations upon. Alas, Zhang was not sufficiently prepared to discuss this!

Book of Changes

“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue; refining one's words and establishing one's sincerity are the means of abiding in one's work.”

Zhou Qin

Associate Examiner Shao, an Instructor, comments: “Advancing virtue and abiding in one's work do not go beyond sincerity. This composition expounds the matter clearly, and its treatment of abiding in one's work shows particularly sensitive understanding. The author seems to understand learning.”

Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: “The exposition is precise and detailed, bringing out the meaning of abiding in one's work. Include it in the record.”

Examiner Li, a School Instructor, comments: “The understanding is intimate and exact. The language is economical yet conveys the meaning fully.”

Examiner Xiang, a Professor, comments: “Concise.”

To root both the inner and the outer in sincerity alone is the work by which the gentleman advances and cultivates himself. Sincerity is the foundation of the work of becoming a sage. Could the gentleman attain flourishing virtue and achievement without sincerity? The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of tireless exertion and vigilant caution in the third nine. It explains that advancing and cultivating oneself at the proper time is the gentleman's intention, and that unifying these efforts into a single undertaking is the way of advancement and cultivation. Thus, when what is stored within becomes virtuous conduct, the gentleman certainly wishes to advance it. But could this be acquired merely by appropriating it from outside? In what governs his heart, he must preserve sincerity to establish its foundation, and overcome the self to recover its original condition. Wherever his aspirations are directed, he already gives himself fully, without falsity; whatever thoughts arise are likewise grounded in actuality and without …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
欺心蓋無不誠矣將見誠精而明義理爲之昭
融有主則虛私欲以之淨盡光輝生於篤實之
餘而日進無疆自可以上達天德矣忠信非所
以進德乎行之而爲事業君子固欲其脩矣是
豈可以强爲乎哉必其見於言者旣出而鄙悖
斯遠未發而靜專是守信立於先辭有稽而道
著誠孚於後事有實而理存辭蓋無不誠矣將
見持循旣定則立方而有恒發見當可雖處雜
而不厭居安裕於自得之後而厥脩罔覺自可
===
以優入聖域矣脩辭立誠非所以居業乎是則
進德者素豫於内所以充乎外也居業者致脩
於外所以養乎内也君子之學内外交脩如此
此九三之所以无咎也抑論聖人之學以誠敬
爲入門故曰敬義立而德不孤乾之所謂進脩
者卽學聖之功也夫子言誠而不及敬何哉蓋
因其剛健不息故專以誠而發之耳而其所謂
惕若者又豈能外乎敬耶故欲從事於進脩者
當以誠爲本而所以存誠者必以主敬爲先
punctuated:
欺，心蓋無不誠矣。將見誠精而明，義理爲之昭融；有主則虛，私欲以之淨盡。光輝生於篤實之餘，而日進無疆，自可以上達天德矣。忠信非所以進德乎？行之而爲事業，君子固欲其脩矣，是豈可以强爲乎哉？必其見於言者，旣出而鄙悖斯遠，未發而靜專是守。信立於先，辭有稽而道著；誠孚於後，事有實而理存。辭蓋無不誠矣。將見持循旣定，則立方而有恒；發見當可，雖處雜而不厭。居安裕於自得之後，而厥脩罔覺，自可以優入聖域矣。脩辭立誠非所以居業乎？是則進德者，素豫於内，所以充乎外也；居業者，致脩於外，所以養乎内也。君子之學，内外交脩如此，此九三之所以无咎也。

抑論聖人之學，以誠敬爲入門，故曰：「敬義立而德不孤。」乾之所謂進脩者，卽學聖之功也。夫子言誠而不及敬，何哉？蓋因其剛健不息，故專以誠而發之耳。而其所謂惕若者，又豈能外乎敬耶？故欲從事於進脩者，當以誠爲本，而所以存誠者，必以主敬爲先。
translation_en:
…without deception, so that nothing in the heart is insincere. Then sincerity, refined, will bring illumination, and moral principles will become radiant and clear; with a governing focus, the heart will be receptive, and selfish desires will be wholly purged. Radiance will arise from deep-rooted integrity, and daily advancement will know no bounds: one may thereby attain the virtue of Heaven above. Are loyalty and trustworthiness not the means of advancing virtue? When put into practice as undertakings, these are certainly what the gentleman wishes to cultivate. But can this be accomplished by force? In what is expressed through words, once speech issues forth, vulgarity and perversity must be kept far away; before it issues forth, stillness and concentration must be maintained. When trustworthiness is established beforehand, words have a basis and the Way becomes manifest; when sincerity is borne out afterward, affairs have substance and principle is preserved. Nothing in one’s words, then, will be insincere. Once one’s observance is settled, one will establish firm standards and maintain constancy; when its expression is fitting, one will feel no weariness even amid complex affairs. Having attained understanding for oneself, one will dwell in ease and abundance, scarcely conscious of one’s cultivation, and may thus enter with ease into the realm of sagehood. Is cultivating one’s words and establishing sincerity not the means of abiding in one’s undertakings? Thus, advancing virtue means preparing oneself inwardly so as to achieve fullness outwardly; abiding in one’s undertakings means carrying cultivation to completion outwardly so as to nourish what is within. Such is the gentleman’s learning: inward and outward cultivation sustain one another. This is why the third nine of the Qian hexagram is ‘without blame.’

Furthermore, in discussing the learning of the sages, sincerity and reverent attentiveness are the gateway. Hence the saying: ‘When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue does not stand alone.’ What the Qian hexagram calls advancement and cultivation is precisely the work of learning to become a sage. Why, then, does the Master speak of sincerity without mentioning reverence? Because the hexagram embodies unceasing strength and vigor, he expounds its meaning specifically through sincerity. Yet how could its injunction to be ‘watchfully apprehensive’ lie outside reverence? Therefore, anyone wishing to undertake advancement and cultivation must make sincerity the foundation; and to preserve sincerity, one must first make reverent attentiveness the governing principle.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也
林耀
同考試官教諭邵批講極深研幾意思明白亦學
易而有得者
同考試官教諭陳批歸重聖人作易極是
考試官學正李批辭暢理明
考試官教授向批發揮題意殆盡
大傳原易之妙用皆聖人發之也夫易聖人之
蘊也極深研幾而易之用盡矣昔大傳之意謂
===
夫惟易有以冒天下之道惟聖人有以成易之
能人知辭占象變爲易之用矣抑豈知聖人之
所爲乎是故吉凶悔吝隱於無形者深也深則
蘊奧莫測充周無窮不可以意逆矣而辭占之
至精者有以具焉夫豈辭占之自能哉聖人所
以極之也蓋其明察乎卦之情僞而小大以齊
洞見夫爻之時物而上下不一故繫之辭焉以
明失得之報斷之占焉以决趨避之方由是象
事可以知器占事可以知來而吉凶悔吝受命
punctuated:
夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。
林耀。
同考試官教諭邵批：講極深研幾意思明白，亦學易而有得者。
同考試官教諭陳批：歸重聖人作易，極是。
考試官學正李批：辭暢理明。
考試官教授向批：發揮題意殆盡。
大傳原易之妙用，皆聖人發之也。夫易，聖人之蘊也。極深研幾，而易之用盡矣。昔大傳之意謂：夫惟易有以冒天下之道，惟聖人有以成易之能。人知辭占象變爲易之用矣，抑豈知聖人之所爲乎？是故吉凶悔吝隱於無形者，深也。深則蘊奧莫測，充周無窮，不可以意逆矣，而辭占之至精者有以具焉。夫豈辭占之自能哉？聖人所以極之也。蓋其明察乎卦之情僞，而小大以齊；洞見夫爻之時物，而上下不一。故繫之辭焉，以明失得之報；斷之占焉，以决趨避之方。由是，象事可以知器，占事可以知來，而吉凶悔吝受命
translation_en:
“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient workings of things.”
Lin Yao.
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: “The meaning of ‘plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient workings of things’ is explained clearly. This, too, is someone who has gained understanding through studying the Changes.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Entirely correct to place the emphasis on the sages’ creation of the Changes.”
Examiner Li, School Director, comments: “The language flows smoothly, and the principles are clear.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “The meaning of the topic is developed almost exhaustively.”
The Great Commentary traces the wondrous functions of the Changes to their source: all were brought forth by the sages. The Changes embodies the sages’ profound understanding. By plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient workings of things, they fully realized its functions. The meaning of the Great Commentary was this: only the Changes can encompass the Way of all under Heaven, and only the sages can bring the capacities of the Changes to fulfillment. People know that statements, divination, images, and transformations constitute the functions of the Changes; but do they understand what the sages did?
Thus, good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation, concealed in what has no form, constitute the depths. Being deep, their hidden mysteries are unfathomable, their all-pervading reach limitless; they cannot be anticipated by conjecture. Yet the utmost refinement of statements and divination can encompass them. Could statements and divination have this capacity of themselves? They are the means by which the sages plumbed those depths. The sages clearly discerned the genuine and the false in the hexagrams, bringing small and great into due order; they thoroughly perceived the circumstances and things represented by the lines, with their differing positions above and below. Hence they appended statements to clarify the consequences of failure and success, and made determinations through divination to decide what course to pursue or avoid. In this way, by representing affairs through images one can understand concrete objects; by divining about affairs one can know what is to come. And concerning good fortune, misfortune, regret, and humiliation, the Changes receives the inquiry…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
如嚮矣是至精也者非聖人之所以極深乎陰
陽老少藏於無象者幾也幾則端倪未判朕兆
至微不可以力求矣而象變之至變者有以具
焉夫豈象變之自爲哉聖人所以研之也蓋其
倚數天地而妙契夫参伍錯綜效法大衍而化
裁於分揲掛扐故示之以爻以著竒偶之分定
之以象以别動靜之機由是兼六畫而成卦分
六位而成章而陰陽老少變動不居矣是至變
也者非聖人之所以研幾乎是則深幾著而易
===
理盡易理盡而民用周聖人作易之功大矣雖
然易固作於聖人然考其行事以易爲準則是
聖人爲易之用矣其何以能作耶蓋易天道也
聖人之心與天爲一故極深研幾者因易以發
其蘊而崇德廣業者用易以踐其實皆所以體
乎天也究而言之聖人與易一而已而謂聖人
爲易之用其信然哉
書
以閏月定四時成歲
punctuated:
如嚮矣。是至精也者，非聖人之所以極深乎？陰陽老少，藏於無象者，幾也。幾則端倪未判，朕兆至微，不可以力求矣，而象變之至變者有以具焉。夫豈象變之自爲哉？聖人所以研之也。蓋其倚數天地，而妙契夫参伍錯綜；效法大衍，而化裁於分揲掛扐。故示之以爻，以著竒偶之分；定之以象，以别動靜之機。由是兼六畫而成卦，分六位而成章，而陰陽老少變動不居矣。是至變也者，非聖人之所以研幾乎？是則深幾著而易理盡，易理盡而民用周，聖人作易之功大矣。雖然，易固作於聖人，然考其行事，以易爲準，則是聖人爲易之用矣，其何以能作耶？蓋易，天道也。聖人之心與天爲一，故極深研幾者，因易以發其蘊；而崇德廣業者，用易以踐其實，皆所以體乎天也。究而言之，聖人與易一而已，而謂聖人爲易之用，其信然哉？

書
以閏月定四時，成歲。
translation_en:
…like an echo. Is this utmost refinement not the means by which the sages plumbed the depths? The old and young forms of yin and yang, concealed before they take on images, are the incipient workings. At this incipient stage, their outlines are not yet distinguishable and their signs are exceedingly subtle: they cannot be sought by force. Yet the utmost capacity for transformation in the images and changes embodies them. Could the images and changes accomplish this of themselves? It was through them that the sages investigated these workings. Drawing on the numbers of Heaven and Earth, they subtly accorded with the operations of grouping in threes and fives, interweaving and combining. Taking the Great Expansion as their model, they adapted its operations through dividing the stalks, counting them off, setting one aside, and placing the remainders between the fingers. Thus they displayed these workings through the lines, making clear the distinction between odd and even, and determined them through the images, distinguishing the impulses toward movement and stillness. Hence six strokes are combined to form a hexagram, and six positions are distinguished to form an ordered pattern; the old and young forms of yin and yang change and move without remaining fixed. Is this utmost capacity for transformation not the means by which the sages investigated the incipient workings?

Thus, when the depths and incipient workings are made manifest, the principles of the Book of Changes are fully revealed; when those principles are fully revealed, the people's practical needs are comprehensively served. Great indeed was the achievement of the sages in making the Book of Changes! Nevertheless, although the Changes was indeed made by the sages, if we examine their conduct, they took the Changes as their standard. This would mean that the sages served as the practical expression of the Changes. How, then, could they have made it? The Changes is the Way of Heaven. The minds of the sages were one with Heaven. Thus, in plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient workings, they drew on the Changes to disclose its hidden content; in exalting virtue and extending their undertakings, they used the Changes to put its substance into practice. These were all means of embodying Heaven. Ultimately, the sages and the Changes are simply one. Can it truly be said, then, that the sages served as the practical expression of the Changes?

Book of Documents
“By means of an intercalary month, determine the four seasons and complete the year.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳言
同考試官教諭方批曆法以人合天而尤詳於置閏
惟此篇敷敘明白宜冠諸作
同考試官教諭夏批說置閏處精確是不苟作者
考試官學正李批敘理既明措辭亦整
考試官教授向批天道正於曆法發明得旨
聖君命官歸餘日以制曆而術不違天矣夫天
運不齊而有餘日則所以歸之而齊以曆法者
豈不有在於置閏哉昔帝堯以此命羲和若曰
===
人君順天以授人時則作曆所不容已然曆生
於數而數有不齊兹何以盡其法而成信曆哉
今夫朞之常數固必三百有六旬六日矣然曆
以十二月而爲一歲歲之全數則止於三百六
十也積日以成月而日與天會之數視歲常多
五日有奇多則歲氣不以盈乎積月以成歲而
月與日會之數視歲常少五日有奇少則月朔
不以虛乎合盈與虛之數則一歲之積得十日
焉三歲之通得一月焉於此而不立之法則盈
punctuated:
陳言

同考試官教諭方批：曆法以人合天，而尤詳於置閏，惟此篇敷敘明白，宜冠諸作。

同考試官教諭夏批：說置閏處精確，是不苟作者。

考試官學正李批：敘理既明，措辭亦整。

考試官教授向批：天道正於曆法，發明得旨。

聖君命官歸餘日以制曆，而術不違天矣。夫天運不齊而有餘日，則所以歸之而齊以曆法者，豈不有在於置閏哉？昔帝堯以此命羲和，若曰：「人君順天以授人時，則作曆所不容已。然曆生於數，而數有不齊，兹何以盡其法而成信曆哉？今夫朞之常數，固必三百有六旬六日矣。然曆以十二月而爲一歲，歲之全數則止於三百六十也。積日以成月，而日與天會之數，視歲常多五日有奇，多則歲氣不以盈乎？積月以成歲，而月與日會之數，視歲常少五日有奇，少則月朔不以虛乎？合盈與虛之數，則一歲之積得十日焉，三歲之通得一月焉。於此而不立之法，則盈
translation_en:
Chen Yan

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: Calendrical methods bring human affairs into accord with Heaven, with particular attention to intercalation. This essay alone expounds the subject clearly and should rank first among the submissions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: The explanation of intercalation is precise. This is an author who takes care with his work.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The exposition of the principles is clear, and the wording is also well ordered.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: Heaven’s course is correctly represented in calendrical methods. The exposition captures the essential meaning.

The sage ruler charged his officials with gathering the surplus days to establish the calendar, so that its procedures would not depart from Heaven’s course. Heaven’s revolutions are uneven and leave surplus days; surely the means of gathering these and bringing them into order through calendrical methods lies in intercalation? Long ago, Emperor Yao charged Xi and He with this task, as though saying:

“A ruler follows Heaven in imparting the seasons to his people, so making a calendar is indispensable. Yet a calendar arises from numerical reckoning, and the numbers do not coincide. How, then, can we fully apply its methods and produce a reliable calendar? Now the regular count of a full annual cycle must indeed be three hundred and sixty-six days. Yet the calendar takes twelve months as one year, whose total count amounts to only three hundred and sixty days. Days accumulate to form months, but the count for the sun to complete its circuit of Heaven regularly exceeds this year by five days and a fraction. Does this excess not constitute a surplus in the year’s seasonal cycle? Months accumulate to form years, but the count of the moon’s conjunctions with the sun regularly falls short of this year by five days and a fraction. Does this shortfall not constitute a deficit in the cycle of lunar months? Combining the surplus and deficit gives an accumulation of ten days in one year, and a total of one month in three years. If no method is established to address this, then the surplus …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
者何所於消虛者何所於息而歲時從瑩矣故
必察其月無中氣則置閏於是歲而多為一月
以總其餘三歲一置則再行於五歲而歷十有
九歲以成一章如是則布月以紀時而氣朔可
齊春夏秋冬之各司其令者質之天而節候不
爽矣四時有不定乎一歲之時定而千百歲之
時胥此焉矣紀時以統歲而寒暑可稽子丑寅
卯之以名其歲者視諸時而天運不乖矣歲功
有不成乎一歲之歲成而千百歲之歲胥此焉
===
矣夫是之謂信曆而以之授人庶其可乎汝羲
曁和盍亦旣厥心哉抑此乃萬世曆法之祖也
上古聖人阜成民物參贊化育蓋必有治曆明
時之政至唐堯置閏則益詳矣然後之論者以
為天運日行舒縮不同則歲宜漸差而病古曆
之簡易於是虞喜何承天諸人各以其意立為
差法然亦隨時修改迄無定說今去東晉千餘
歲而考之日月之食司曆者不愆于時意與古
亦不甚相遠也要之聖人重曆之意惟在於敬
punctuated:
者何所於消，虛者何所於息，而歲時從瑩矣。故必察其月無中氣，則置閏於是歲，而多為一月，以總其餘。三歲一置，則再行於五歲，而歷十有九歲以成一章。如是，則布月以紀時，而氣朔可齊；春夏秋冬之各司其令者，質之天而節候不爽矣。四時有不定乎？一歲之時定，而千百歲之時胥此焉矣。紀時以統歲，而寒暑可稽；子丑寅卯之以名其歲者，視諸時而天運不乖矣。歲功有不成乎？一歲之歲成，而千百歲之歲胥此焉矣。夫是之謂信曆，而以之授人，庶其可乎？汝羲曁和，盍亦旣厥心哉！

抑此乃萬世曆法之祖也。上古聖人阜成民物，參贊化育，蓋必有治曆明時之政，至唐堯置閏則益詳矣。然後之論者以為天運日行，舒縮不同，則歲宜漸差，而病古曆之簡易。於是虞喜、何承天諸人，各以其意立為差法，然亦隨時修改，迄無定說。今去東晉千餘歲，而考之日月之食，司曆者不愆于時，意與古亦不甚相遠也。要之，聖人重曆之意，惟在於敬
translation_en:
…how could the surplus be eliminated, and how could the deficit be replenished? The years and seasons would consequently become confused [?]. Thus one must identify a month containing no principal solar term and insert an intercalary month in that year, adding a month to gather up the accumulated remainder. An intercalation is made once in three years, hence twice in five years; nineteen years complete one cycle. In this way, months are arranged to mark the seasons, and solar terms and new moons can be brought into alignment. Spring, summer, autumn, and winter each exercise their proper seasonal influence; checked against Heaven, their seasonal junctures do not deviate. How could the four seasons fail to be correctly determined? Once the seasons of one year are determined, those of a thousand or a hundred years all follow from this. The seasons are marked to organize the year, and cold and heat can be verified. Years named by the earthly branches—zi, chou, yin, mao, and so forth—are checked against the seasons and do not diverge from Heaven’s motions. How could the work of the year fail to be accomplished? Once one year is brought to completion, the years of a thousand or a hundred years all follow from this. This is what is called a reliable calendar. Might it then be suitable for promulgation to the people? You, Xi and He, should you not also devote your whole hearts to this!

Indeed, this is the foundation of calendrical methods for all ages. The sages of high antiquity nurtured and brought to fulfillment the people and all things, participating in and assisting the work of transformation and growth. They must surely have had measures for regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons; by the time of Tang Yao, the insertion of intercalary months made these still more detailed. Yet later commentators held that Heaven’s motions and the sun’s course differed in their slowing and quickening, so that a discrepancy should gradually accumulate over the years; they therefore faulted the ancient calendar for its simplicity. Accordingly, Yu Xi, He Chengtian, and others each devised methods of correction according to their own views. Yet these too were revised as circumstances required, and no settled account was ever reached. Now, more than a thousand years after the Eastern Jin, when we check against solar and lunar eclipses, those responsible for the calendar do not err in their timing. Presumably their methods are not very far removed from those of antiquity either. Ultimately, the sages’ purpose in attaching importance to the calendar lay solely in reverence…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
天勤民而稽分積數之精疎則付之專官而已
帝王與天同運而民物順治者其固有道哉
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
陳南星
同考試官教諭方批立意正大措辭簡古而近
天子之光處尤見脫落
同考試官教諭夏批脫去俗套程式之文也
考試官學正李批簡當
===
考試官教授向批穩貼
君子賛敷言之妙而及其化焉夫訓化之感人
固也聖人則天以為訓而民有弗協于極者哉
箕子若曰人君納民於極曲盡勸相之方能無
孚化之應是故旣作之極也而又歌詠以長其
言旣錫之福也而又諷誦以宣其意綱維體要
不外乎民彝物則之常義理宏通自足為垂世
立教之典然衷由帝降人君代之而立言典自
天敘聖人則之而成訓是言匪私臆而理有大
punctuated:
天勤民，而稽分積數之精疎，則付之專官而已。帝王與天同運，而民物順治者，其固有道哉！
皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。
陳南星
同考試官教諭方批：立意正大，措辭簡古，而近天子之光處尤見脫落。
同考試官教諭夏批：脫去俗套，程式之文也。
考試官學正李批：簡當。
考試官教授向批：穩貼。
君子賛敷言之妙，而及其化焉。夫訓化之感人固也，聖人則天以為訓，而民有弗協于極者哉？箕子若曰：人君納民於極，曲盡勸相之方，能無孚化之應？是故旣作之極也，而又歌詠以長其言；旣錫之福也，而又諷誦以宣其意。綱維體要，不外乎民彝物則之常；義理宏通，自足為垂世立教之典。然衷由帝降，人君代之而立言；典自天敘，聖人則之而成訓。是言匪私臆，而理有大
translation_en:
…revering Heaven and diligently caring for the people; as for the precision or imprecision of reckoning fractions and accumulating numbers, he leaves that to the officials specifically charged with it. Surely there is a Way by which emperors and kings move in concert with Heaven, and the people and all things are harmoniously ordered!

“The proclaimed words of the August Ultimate are constant norms and instruction—instruction derived from the Lord on High. All the common people take the proclaimed words of the Ultimate as instruction and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven.”

Chen Nanxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The conception is upright and elevated, the diction concise and antique. The treatment of ‘drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven’ is especially free and unforced.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: “It sheds conventional clichés: a composition worthy of serving as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: “Concise and apt.”

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: “Sound and fitting.”

The gentleman praises the subtle excellence of the proclaimed words and proceeds to their transforming influence. That instruction and transformation move people is certain. When the sage models his instruction on Heaven, could any among the people fail to accord with the Ultimate?

Jizi speaks as follows: When the ruler brings the people into accord with the Ultimate and exhaustively applies every means of encouragement and assistance, how could there fail to be a response of heartfelt transformation? Thus, having established the Ultimate for them, he further sings and chants to prolong his words; having bestowed blessings upon them, he further recites to make his meaning fully known. The governing framework and essential substance extend no further than the enduring norms of human relationships and the constant principles of things. Broad and comprehensive in moral principle, these words are sufficient in themselves to serve as a canon for establishing instruction and transmitting it to later ages. Yet the inner moral standard descends from the Lord on High, and the ruler speaks on his behalf; the constant institutions are ordered by Heaven, and the sage models himself on them to formulate instruction. These words are no private conjecture, and their principle has a great…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
原君之言卽天之言矣敷言之妙如此由是庶
民蒙其樂育之敎而動其秉彞之良匪直詠歌
之已也服膺勿失而觀省以稽其成不但諷誦
之已也祗遹有聞而躬行以踐其實將見民風
丕變庶幾道義之輝順帝則以周旋而進進之
機有不能以自已者矣衆志日新親炙文明之
化仰王言而承式而烝烝於乂有莫知其所以
者矣是蓋敎有成法性有均善君子以人治人
而民之從之也宜哉大抵躬行之敎易從而勉
===
强之情難久錫福之政有窮而鼓舞之化爲不
倦也敷言本諸身有而達乎民宜其於用休之
戒九歌之勸異用同心虞周之治此其所以爲
盛與
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
石磐
同考試官敎諭祝批天澤溥施不以公私爲先後而
民心愛戴則若受公田之餘潤者比作得之
punctuated:
原。君之言卽天之言矣。敷言之妙如此，由是庶民蒙其樂育之敎，而動其秉彞之良。匪直詠歌之已也，服膺勿失，而觀省以稽其成；不但諷誦之已也，祗遹有聞，而躬行以踐其實。將見民風丕變，庶幾道義之輝，順帝則以周旋，而進進之機有不能以自已者矣；衆志日新，親炙文明之化，仰王言而承式，而烝烝於乂，有莫知其所以者矣。是蓋敎有成法，性有均善，君子以人治人，而民之從之也宜哉！大抵躬行之敎易從，而勉强之情難久；錫福之政有窮，而鼓舞之化爲不倦也。敷言本諸身有而達乎民，宜其於用休之戒、九歌之勸，異用同心。虞周之治，此其所以爲盛與！

詩
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。
石磐

同考試官敎諭祝批：天澤溥施，不以公私爲先後，而民心愛戴，則若受公田之餘潤者，比作得之。
translation_en:
…origin. The ruler’s words are thus Heaven’s words. Such is the subtle efficacy of setting forth instruction. Through it, the common people receive his teaching, which delights in nurturing them, and the goodness of their constant moral nature is stirred. They do more than sing its praises: they hold it fast in their hearts without losing it, observing and examining themselves to assess their progress. They do more than recite it: they reverently follow what they have heard and put its substance into practice through their own conduct. We shall then see the people’s customs greatly transformed. Aspiring to the splendor of the Way and righteousness, they conduct themselves according to the Supreme Lord’s standards, with an impulse toward continual improvement that they cannot themselves restrain. The aspirations of the multitude are renewed daily. Directly receiving the transforming influence of enlightened culture, they look up to the king’s words and take them as their rule, advancing steadily toward good order without knowing how this comes about. This is because teaching has established methods, and human nature possesses goodness common to all. The gentleman governs people according to their own humanity: how fitting that the people should follow him!

Generally, teaching through personal conduct is easy to follow, whereas an attitude maintained by forced effort is difficult to sustain. Government that bestows blessings has its limits, whereas transformation through inspiration never tires. Instruction set forth in words rests upon what the ruler himself possesses and extends to the people. It fittingly shares the purpose of the admonition to encourage through praise and the exhortations of the Nine Songs, though their applications differ. Surely this is what made the governments of Yu and Zhou so flourishing!

Book of Odes
“Thickly gather the clouds;
Abundantly falls the rain.
Rain upon our public fields,
Then reach our private fields as well.”
Shi Pan

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: Heaven’s rain is bestowed everywhere, without giving precedence to public fields over private ones. Yet the people’s loving devotion makes them feel as though they receive the moisture left over from the public fields. This composition [?] captures that meaning.
