title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
以閏月定四時成歲
惟說式克欽承旁招俊乂列于庶位
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
惟爾令德孝恭惟孝友于兄弟克施有政
命汝尹茲東郊敬哉昔周公師保萬民
民懷其德往慎乃司茲率厥常懋昭周
公之訓惟民其乂
詩
===
采采芣苢薄言采之采采芣苢薄言有之
采采芣苢薄言掇之采采芣苢薄言捋
之采采芣苢薄言袺之采采芣苢薄言
襭之
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
申伯之德柔惠且直揉此萬邦聞于四國
吉甫作誦其詩孔碩其風肆好以贈申
伯
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
punctuated:
以閏月定四時，成歲。
惟說式克欽承，旁招俊乂，列于庶位。
皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。
惟爾令德孝恭，惟孝友于兄弟，克施有政。命汝尹茲東郊，敬哉！昔周公師保萬民，民懷其德。往，慎乃司，茲率厥常，懋昭周公之訓，惟民其乂。

詩

采采芣苢，薄言采之。采采芣苢，薄言有之。采采芣苢，薄言掇之。采采芣苢，薄言捋之。采采芣苢，薄言袺之。采采芣苢，薄言襭之。
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。
申伯之德，柔惠且直。揉此萬邦，聞于四國。吉甫作誦，其詩孔碩，其風肆好，以贈申伯。
有飶其香，邦家之光。有椒其馨，胡考之寧。
translation_en:
…By means of intercalary months, determine the four seasons and complete the year.

Yue reverently carried out these commands, widely recruiting men of outstanding talent and placing them in the various offices.

The pronouncements setting forth the August Standard are enduring norms and instructions; they are the teachings of the Supreme Lord. Let all the common people take the pronouncements of the Standard as their instruction and put them into practice, thereby drawing near to the radiance of the Son of Heaven.

Your excellent virtues are filial devotion and reverence. Filial toward your parents and loving toward your brothers, you can extend these qualities to government. I appoint you to govern this eastern suburb. Be reverent! Formerly, the Duke of Zhou taught and protected the myriad people, and the people cherished his virtue. Go, attend carefully to your charge, follow his constant principles, and diligently make manifest the Duke of Zhou’s instructions. Then the people will be well governed.

Book of Odes

We gather, gather the plantain; let us pluck it.
We gather, gather the plantain; let us keep it.
We gather, gather the plantain; let us pick it up.
We gather, gather the plantain; let us strip it by the handful.
We gather, gather the plantain; let us hold it in our lifted skirts.
We gather, gather the plantain; let us tuck our skirts into our belts to carry it.

Dense gather the clouds; abundant falls the rain. Rain upon our public fields, and then reach our private fields as well.

The virtue of the Earl of Shen is gentle, generous, and upright. He brings harmony to the myriad states; his fame is heard throughout the lands in all four directions. Jifu composed this song: its verses are most grand, its airs expansive and fine, to present to the Earl of Shen.

Fragrant is the aroma of the offerings—the glory of the state and its ruling house. Pepper-sweet is their scent—the peace of a long and venerable life.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
春秋
夏公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭伯許男
曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕吳子使札來聘
〔襄公二十有九年〕
丁亥楚子入陳〔宣公十有一年〕晉人宋人
衛人曹人同盟于清丘宋師伐陳衛
人救陳〔俱宣公十有二年〕
公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子
杞伯救鄭〔成公七年〕
===
秋季孫意如會晉韓起齊國弱宋華亥衛
北宮佗鄭罕虎曹人杞人于厥憖〔昭公
十有一年〕三月公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡
侯衛侯陳子鄭伯許男曹伯莒子邾子
頓子胡子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國
夏于召陵侵楚〔定公四年〕
禮記
君子察於此三者可以有志於學矣
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
punctuated:
春秋

夏，公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘。〔僖公九年〕吳子使札來聘。〔襄公二十有九年〕

丁亥，楚子入陳。〔宣公十有一年〕晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人同盟于清丘。宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔俱宣公十有二年〕

公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、杞伯救鄭。〔成公七年〕

秋，季孫意如會晉韓起、齊國弱、宋華亥、衛北宮佗、鄭罕虎、曹人、杞人于厥憖。〔昭公十有一年〕三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕

禮記

君子察於此三者，可以有志於學矣。

春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，
translation_en:
Spring and Autumn Annals

In summer, the Duke of Lu met at Kuiqiu with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the Viscount of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Viscount of Wu sent Zha on a diplomatic visit to Lu. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xiang.〕

On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.〕 Representatives of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao concluded a joint covenant at Qingqiu. The army of Song attacked Chen, and men of Wei came to Chen’s aid. 〔Both entries are from the twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕

The Duke of Lu joined the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, and the Earl of Qi to relieve Zheng. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng.〕

In autumn, Jisun Yiru met at Jueyin with Han Qi of Jin, Guo Ruo of Qi, Hua Hai of Song, Beigong Tuo of Wei, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Cao and Qi. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.〕 In the third month, the Duke of Lu met at Shaoling with the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi, and invaded Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding.〕

Book of Rites

When the gentleman understands these three things, he can set his heart on learning.

Bringing forth in spring and nurturing growth in summer constitute benevolence; gathering in autumn and storing in winter constitute righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
義近於禮
所以治愛人禮爲大所以治禮敬爲大
溫良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也
第貳塲
論
天地之所以爲大
===
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以戶部侍郎裴垍爲中書侍郎同平
章事誥〔元和三年〕
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士
謝表〔景德二年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
轉解官物
punctuated:
義近於禮。
所以治愛人，禮爲大；所以治禮，敬爲大。
溫良者，仁之本也；敬慎者，仁之地也；寬裕者，仁之作也；孫接者，仁之能也；禮節者，仁之貌也；言談者，仁之文也；歌樂者，仁之和也；分散者，仁之施也。
第貳塲
論
天地之所以爲大。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜民今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬唐以戶部侍郎裴垍爲中書侍郎、同平章事誥〔元和三年〕。
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士謝表〔景德二年〕。
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由。
轉解官物。
translation_en:
…Righteousness is akin to ritual propriety.
For regulating love for others, ritual propriety is paramount; for regulating ritual propriety, reverence is paramount.
Gentleness and kindness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are its ground; generosity and magnanimity are its expression in action; deference in dealing with others is its capacity; ritual observances are its outward appearance; speech and conversation are its refinement; singing and music are its harmony; distributing possessions is its bestowal.
Second Session
Discourse
What makes Heaven and Earth great.
Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic from among these categories [?].〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty remitting half of the people's land tax for the current year. 〔Second year of Emperor Wen's reign.〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Pei Ji, Vice Minister of Revenue, as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery. 〔Third year of Yuanhe.〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for Yang Yi's appointment as a Hanlin Academician. 〔Second year of Jingde.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕
Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks.
Forwarding government property.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
禁止迎送
遞送公文
侵占街道
第叁塲
策五道
問帝王之治必本於德而其爲政也必先
於教古今言治者必曰唐虞而稱聖德
者必曰堯舜雖功格於放勳而化成於
無虞然精一執中之教實開萬世心學
===
之源豈非推行有本而功化之極固不
待外求也我
太祖高皇帝
謨訓功烈度越百世今
聖政記
大明日曆之紀載煥如日星其於精一之傳若
合符節有可舉而言之與我
皇上懋德建中政化之成四達不悖是故
敬一有箴
punctuated:
禁止迎送。
遞送公文。
侵占街道。

第叁塲
策五道

問：帝王之治必本於德，而其爲政也必先於教。古今言治者必曰唐虞，而稱聖德者必曰堯舜。雖功格於放勳，而化成於無虞，然精一執中之教，實開萬世心學之源。豈非推行有本，而功化之極固不待外求也？我太祖高皇帝謨訓功烈，度越百世。今《聖政記》《大明日曆》之紀載，煥如日星，其於精一之傳，若合符節，有可舉而言之與？我皇上懋德建中，政化之成，四達不悖。是故敬一有箴，
translation_en:
Prohibiting ceremonial welcomes and send-offs.
Forwarding official documents.
Encroaching upon streets.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The governance of emperors and kings must be rooted in virtue, and in administering government they must give priority to moral instruction. From antiquity to the present, those who discuss good governance invariably cite Tang and Yu, and those who praise sagely virtue invariably cite Yao and Shun. Although achievement reached its height in Fangxun (Yao), and moral transformation was perfected under Wuyu [?; apparently referring to Shun], it was their teaching of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean that truly opened the wellspring of the learning of the mind for all ages. Was this not because their implementation had a foundation, so that the highest achievements in government and moral transformation assuredly required no seeking outside it?

Our Emperor Taizu Gao’s plans, instructions, and glorious achievements surpassed those of a hundred generations. The accounts now recorded in the Record of Sagely Governance and the Daily Record of the Great Ming shine like the sun and stars. Their correspondence with the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness is like the matching halves of a tally. Can you cite and discuss examples?

Our reigning Emperor diligently cultivates virtue and establishes the mean; the accomplishments of his government and moral transformation extend in all directions without discord. Thus, for reverent single-mindedness there is an admonition …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
視聽言動心箴有註
微詞奧旨妙契往聖爾諸士服膺有年矣其
有能賛揚萬一以光昭
盛美者乎夫商周有頌詩人所以歌上德也
彰
盛實而宣
鴻休非士者職分事哉不然則與擊壤之夫
莫知帝力者等也
問先儒謂文以載道則道以文而明文以
===
道而傳者也六經之聖無心於文而至
道存焉不可尚矣嗣是則孔孟筆削於
春秋問答於門第固將以存志也而他
日無言之教不得已之辨蓋嘗屢致其
意焉豈道固不貴於有文耶漢之遷固
名山金匱之藏不可謂非一代之典也
而核直贍詳之文終愧六經豈其果無
所發明於道耶魏晋無文昔人所鄙浮
華纖麗之習誠不足以昭物而章軌也
punctuated:
視聽言動心箴有註，微詞奧旨，妙契往聖。爾諸士服膺有年矣，其有能賛揚萬一，以光昭盛美者乎？夫商周有頌，詩人所以歌上德也。彰盛實而宣鴻休，非士者職分事哉？不然，則與擊壤之夫莫知帝力者等也。

問：先儒謂文以載道，則道以文而明，文以道而傳者也。六經之聖，無心於文，而至道存焉，不可尚矣。嗣是，則孔孟筆削於《春秋》，問答於門第，固將以存志也。而他日無言之教、不得已之辨，蓋嘗屢致其意焉。豈道固不貴於有文耶？漢之遷固，名山金匱之藏，不可謂非一代之典也。而核直贍詳之文，終愧六經，豈其果無所發明於道耶？魏晋無文，昔人所鄙。浮華纖麗之習，誠不足以昭物而章軌也。
translation_en:
…and the Admonitions on Seeing, Hearing, Speaking, Acting, and the Mind have commentaries. Their subtle expressions and profound meanings accord wondrously with the sages of old. You scholars have cherished these teachings for years. Is there anyone among you who can extol even a ten-thousandth part of them, thereby making this glorious excellence shine forth? Shang and Zhou had their hymns, through which poets celebrated the virtue of their rulers. Is it not the scholar’s proper duty to display these abundant accomplishments and proclaim these great blessings? Otherwise, you would be no different from the man who played at striking the ground, unaware of the emperor’s contribution to his life.

Question: Earlier Confucian scholars said that writing conveys the Way. Thus the Way is made clear through writing, and writing is transmitted through the Way. The sages responsible for the Six Classics had no deliberate concern for literary composition, yet the supreme Way resides in their works: nothing can surpass them. Subsequently, Confucius and Mencius wielded the brush to include and excise in the Spring and Autumn Annals and engaged in questions and answers within their schools [?], surely intending thereby to preserve their aspirations. Yet on other occasions they repeatedly expressed their thoughts about teaching without words and disputing only when compelled to do so. Could it be that the Way does not inherently value written expression? The works of Sima Qian and Ban Gu of the Han, preserved in famous mountains and metal caskets, cannot be denied the status of authoritative records of their age. Yet their writing, accurate and forthright, ample and detailed, ultimately falls short of the Six Classics. Can it really have done nothing to elucidate the Way? That Wei and Jin had no literature was a reproach voiced by men of former times. Their habits of superficial ornament and delicate elegance were indeed insufficient to illuminate things and make guiding norms manifest.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
其後言唐文者必歸韓柳而因文見道
之稱柳子不與焉其於昌黎何取言宋
文者惟美歐蘇而宋有文字四篇二子
無取焉其於歐蘇何病原道之作卓乎
有見矣而其時智如子房才如賈誼而
文足以經國制變者視韓子為孰優太
極圖西銘諸作筆力高古矣而其時接
正傳於濂洛集大成於諸子者論其文
夫豈劣夫篤實而藝書美愛而久傳先
===
儒固有定說矣諸士子抱藝而來將必
有所發明而不徒事於文者幸究言之
以觀所蘊
問周禮周公治周之成書而貽世之典則
也後之言政者稽焉然是非頗謬而疑
信未協雖更以程朱蘇胡諸大儒之論
莫之取衷其詳可得而言與夫政莫重
於建官而法必先於出令唐虞惟百夏
商用倍周俗繁簡不應遽爾異也今五
punctuated:
其後言唐文者必歸韓柳，而因文見道之稱，柳子不與焉，其於昌黎何取？言宋文者惟美歐蘇，而宋有文字四篇，二子無取焉，其於歐蘇何病？原道之作，卓乎有見矣，而其時智如子房、才如賈誼，而文足以經國制變者，視韓子為孰優？太極圖、西銘諸作，筆力高古矣，而其時接正傳於濂洛、集大成於諸子者，論其文，夫豈劣？夫篤實而藝，書美愛而久傳，先儒固有定說矣。諸士子抱藝而來，將必有所發明而不徒事於文者，幸究言之，以觀所蘊。
問：周禮，周公治周之成書，而貽世之典則也，後之言政者稽焉。然是非頗謬，而疑信未協，雖更以程朱蘇胡諸大儒之論，莫之取衷，其詳可得而言與？夫政莫重於建官，而法必先於出令。唐虞惟百，夏商用倍，周俗繁簡不應遽爾異也。今五
translation_en:
…Thereafter, those who discuss Tang prose invariably turn to Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan. Yet Liu is not included in the praise accorded to those whose writing reveals the Way. What is it in Han Yu of Changli that merits this distinction? Those who discuss Song prose praise only Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. Yet among the four exemplary pieces of Song writing, nothing by these two is selected. What shortcoming does this imply in Ouyang and Su? The essay Inquiry into the Way displays outstanding insight. Yet in Han Yu’s time there were men with wisdom like that of Zifang and talent like that of Jia Yi, whose writing could order the state and manage changing circumstances. Compared with Master Han, who was superior? Works such as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate and the Western Inscription possess an elevated, antique literary force. Yet among those of that age who received the orthodox transmission from the masters of Lian and Luo and brought together the achievements of the various masters, how could their writing be judged inferior? As for being substantial and accomplished, and writings being beautiful, cherished, and enduringly transmitted [?], earlier Confucian scholars have already offered settled judgments. You candidates have come bearing your literary accomplishments; surely you have insights to elucidate beyond merely attending to literary form. Please discuss these matters fully, so that we may see what you have within you.
Question: The Rites of Zhou is the completed account of the Duke of Zhou’s governance of Zhou and a body of authoritative standards bequeathed to later ages. Those who subsequently discuss government consult it. Yet judgments of its merits and faults diverge considerably, and doubt and belief remain unreconciled. Even after examining the arguments of such great Confucian scholars as Cheng, Zhu, Su, and Hu, no balanced conclusion has been reached. Can the details be set forth? In government, nothing is more important than establishing offices, and in instituting laws, issuing commands must come first. Under Tang and Yu there were only a hundred officials; Xia and Shang employed twice that number. The complexity or simplicity of Zhou customs should not have differed so abruptly. Now, the five…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
官之屬自內史宮正以至鄉卿甸帥胥
廛封牧藁校饔薙之類衆至數萬而比
閭卒伍之長不與焉不知畿甸千里之
內為田幾井而又有王官公族食采四
地之一此等將仰給於公抑自食其力
耶古者為而不有應而不求百姓日遷
善而不知周去古未遠也今歲朔孟仲
考藝讀法詢事振旅凡大聚會月必屢
至而飲射酺蜡之類不與焉不知一月
===
之內為日幾何而又有供給徵召蒐獼
田狩之役此等豈在官之庶人抑南畝
之耕夫耶夫選用既衆理難必其皆賢
徵會不時勢不能於無擾况代耕不足
而妨業尤多豈古今政俗若是不同耶
昔人謂如有用我者執此以往講求不
素則推行必悖爾諸士固豫養以待用
者其有以告我
問天地之氣下為河嶽上則列星經緯昭
punctuated:
官之屬，自內史、宮正以至鄉卿、甸帥、胥、廛、封、牧、藁、校、饔、薙之類，衆至數萬，而比、閭、卒、伍之長不與焉。不知畿甸千里之內，為田幾井，而又有王官、公族食采四地之一，此等將仰給於公，抑自食其力耶？古者為而不有，應而不求，百姓日遷善而不知。周去古未遠也，今歲朔孟仲，考藝、讀法、詢事、振旅，凡大聚會，月必屢至，而飲、射、酺、蜡之類不與焉。不知一月之內，為日幾何，而又有供給、徵召、蒐獼、田狩之役，此等豈在官之庶人，抑南畝之耕夫耶？夫選用既衆，理難必其皆賢；徵會不時，勢不能於無擾。况代耕不足，而妨業尤多，豈古今政俗若是不同耶？昔人謂：「如有用我者，執此以往。」講求不素，則推行必悖。爾諸士固豫養以待用者，其有以告我。

問：天地之氣，下為河嶽，上則列星，經緯昭
translation_en:
…the subordinate offices, from the Interior Secretary and Palace Director down to the district ministers, directors of the royal domains, and officials responsible for assistants, market premises, boundaries, pastures, fodder, horses, cooked provisions, and clearing vegetation [?], number in the tens of thousands. This does not even include the heads of neighborhood and military units. Within the royal domain extending a thousand li, how many well-field units of farmland could there be? Moreover, royal officials and members of the ruling lineage draw revenues from one-quarter of the land. Are all these people to depend on public support, or to support themselves through their own labor?

In antiquity, rulers acted without claiming possession and responded without making demands; the common people advanced daily toward goodness without knowing it. The Zhou was not far removed from antiquity. Yet here, at the beginnings of years and months and in the first and second months of the seasons, there were examinations of skills, readings of laws, inquiries into affairs, and military reviews. Major assemblies necessarily occurred several times each month, even without counting the communal drinking and archery ceremonies, the communal feasts, and the year-end agricultural sacrifices. How many days could there be in a single month? There were also duties involving the provision of supplies, official summonses, seasonal hunts [?], and hunting expeditions. Were those performing these duties commoners employed in government service, or farmers tilling the southern fields?

With so many people selected for employment, it would scarcely be possible to ensure that all were worthy. With summonses to assemblies issued at irregular times, disturbance would inevitably follow. Moreover, the support provided in lieu of farming was insufficient, while interference with people's occupations was especially frequent. Could government and customs in antiquity and in later ages really have differed so greatly? A man of former times said: “If someone were to employ me, I would take this with me and proceed.” Without sustained prior study, putting it into practice would surely go awry. You scholars have indeed been cultivating yourselves in preparation for service; tell me what you have to say about this.

Question: The vital energy of Heaven and Earth forms rivers and mountains below, and the arrayed stars above, whose longitudinal and latitudinal patterns shine…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
回以垂天象匯流盤峙以奠地宜莫不
有理焉古昔聖王知其然故立司天司
地之官而星官堪輿之說昉於史傳矣
粤嘗稽之黃帝羲和之命車區之占唐
虞鳥火之識璣衡之在何當時以為急
務而後世之業其官者乃反有不知與
星象之書古凡幾家誰為最著今其所
傳者可得而聞其要與漢唐而下精於
其術者代不乏人亦可舉而言其優劣
===
與若堪輿之書今則無傳矣僅見於周
禮者有辨方正位之辭而求其制則惟
土圭測景而已其作用之遺意猶有可
考者與冬官土宜之辨以相民宅歷代
形勝之據以建國都蓋必有所見也其
亦可得而言與或者又謂懸象在天其
本在地於是又有分野之說而論者疑
其星野之不相值是果然與昔之人有
能推古聖人敬天理地之意而著為定
punctuated: 回以垂天象，匯流盤峙以奠地宜，莫不有理焉。古昔聖王知其然，故立司天司地之官，而星官堪輿之說昉於史傳矣。粤嘗稽之，黃帝羲和之命、車區之占，唐虞鳥火之識、璣衡之在，何當時以為急務，而後世之業其官者乃反有不知與？星象之書，古凡幾家？誰為最著？今其所傳者，可得而聞其要與？漢唐而下，精於其術者代不乏人，亦可舉而言其優劣與？若堪輿之書，今則無傳矣。僅見於周禮者，有辨方正位之辭，而求其制，則惟土圭測景而已。其作用之遺意，猶有可考者與？冬官土宜之辨，以相民宅；歷代形勝之據，以建國都，蓋必有所見也。其亦可得而言與？或者又謂，懸象在天，其本在地，於是又有分野之說，而論者疑其星野之不相值，是果然與？昔之人有能推古聖人敬天理地之意，而著為定
translation_en:
…revolving to display the celestial configurations, while converging streams and firmly standing mountains establish the proper dispositions of the earth: all have their underlying principles. The sage kings of antiquity understood this, and therefore established officials charged with heaven and officials charged with earth. Accounts of the celestial offices and geomancy thus first appeared in historical writings. Examining antiquity, we find the Yellow Emperor’s appointment of Xi and He, the divinations of Chequ [?], and, under Tang Yao and Yu Shun, the identification of the Bird and Fire stars and the examination of the jade astronomical instruments. Why were these considered urgent tasks at the time, whereas some later occupants of these offices actually knew nothing of them?

How many schools of writings on celestial configurations were there in antiquity? Which were the most distinguished? Can we hear the essentials of those transmitted to the present? From the Han and Tang onward, every age had people proficient in these arts. Can you also name them and discuss their relative merits?

As for books on geomancy, none are now transmitted. What little appears in the Rites of Zhou includes statements about distinguishing directions and correctly establishing positions; yet, when we seek the actual procedures, there is only the measurement of shadows with an earth gnomon. Can any surviving intentions behind its practical application still be investigated? The distinctions among suitable soils made by the winter officials served to select dwelling sites for the people; successive dynasties relied on advantageous terrain to establish their capitals. Surely these practices rested on some understanding. Can that understanding also be explained?

Some further maintain that the configurations suspended in heaven have their roots on earth. Hence there is also the theory of astral-terrestrial correspondences. Yet commentators doubt whether the stars and their corresponding terrestrial regions actually match. Is this indeed so? Among people of former times, were there any who could develop the ancient sages’ intention of revering heaven and ordering the earth, and set it down as a definitive…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
論者君子取之若然則義非高遠道存
民用是亦學者之所當講也諸生宜毋
諉之術數之學
問經國致治莫切於利用而用之利者莫
喻於錢幣所以通貨源而資民生也粵
稽之古有謂之泉有謂之布者其義何
居有鑄於歷山有鑄於莊山者其意安
在漢之莢錢八銖四銖五銖名亦多矣
何為而五銖獨用唐之開元天寶乾元
===
制亦善矣何為而開元可行迨至宋元
更造不一惟我
國家因時酌宜設局鼓鑄兼用前代行之四
方而大江以南壤地千里錢不為市何
耶或謂南北異俗不可强同然嶺海之
間以之貿遷豈通於彼而獨塞於此乎
玆欲使錢幣大行而民情俱協抑何道
可以致之古有外府泉府邦布邦市之
法不知可倣而行之否乎夫稽實致用
punctuated:
論者，君子取之。若然，則義非高遠，道存民用，是亦學者之所當講也。諸生宜毋諉之術數之學。

問：經國致治，莫切於利用，而用之利者，莫喻於錢幣，所以通貨源而資民生也。粵稽之古，有謂之泉、有謂之布者，其義何居？有鑄於歷山、有鑄於莊山者，其意安在？漢之莢錢、八銖、四銖、五銖，名亦多矣，何為而五銖獨用？唐之開元、天寶、乾元，制亦善矣，何為而開元可行？迨至宋元，更造不一。惟我國家因時酌宜，設局鼓鑄，兼用前代，行之四方。而大江以南，壤地千里，錢不為市，何耶？或謂南北異俗，不可强同。然嶺海之間，以之貿遷，豈通於彼而獨塞於此乎？玆欲使錢幣大行，而民情俱協，抑何道可以致之？古有外府、泉府、邦布、邦市之法，不知可倣而行之否乎？夫稽實致用
translation_en:
…judgments that gentlemen have accepted. If so, their meaning is neither lofty nor remote: the Way resides in what serves the people’s needs. This too is something scholars ought to discuss. You candidates should not dismiss it as the study of technical arts and numerical methods.

Question: In ordering the state and bringing about good government, nothing is more pressing than facilitating practical use; and nothing illustrates such utility more clearly than coinage, which circulates supplies of goods and sustains the people’s livelihood. Looking back to antiquity, some called money quan, “springs,” and others bu, “cloth.” What did these terms mean? Some cast coins at Mount Li and others at Mount Zhuang: what was the intention behind this? The Han had many names for its coins—pod money, eight-zhu, four-zhu, and five-zhu coins. Why did the five-zhu alone remain in use? The Tang’s Kaiyuan, Tianbao, and Qianyuan coinages were also well designed. Why was it the Kaiyuan that proved practicable? By the Song and Yuan, new issues were produced repeatedly. Our own dynasty, weighing what is appropriate to the times, has established bureaus to cast coins and has put them into circulation throughout the realm alongside coins of earlier dynasties. Yet south of the great Yangzi River, over a territory extending a thousand li, coins are not used in market transactions. Why is this? Some say that northern and southern customs differ and cannot be forcibly made uniform. Yet in the region between the mountain ranges and the sea, coins are used in trade. How can they circulate there but be obstructed here alone? If we now wish to bring coinage into widespread circulation while accommodating the dispositions of all the people, by what means can this be achieved? In antiquity there were regulations concerning the Outer Treasury, the Treasury for Markets, state currency, and state markets. Could these be imitated and put into practice? As for investigating actual conditions and achieving practical utility…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
通變宜民亦士之所當究願著于篇以
觀所學
punctuated: 通變宜民，亦士之所當究。願著于篇，以觀所學。
translation_en: …adapting to change for the benefit of the people is also something scholars ought to investigate thoroughly. Please set forth your views in writing, so that we may assess your learning.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯子出
門人問曰何謂也曾子曰夫子之道忠
恕而已矣
洪世遷
考試官學正李批詞不費而意義自見蓋聞聖
敬而有得者
考試官教授向批一貫之旨發於忠恕意融辭
===
達僅見此作
大賢聞聖道而有得而因以發之也夫道一而
已大賢唯於有聞而發於所問聖門授受之妙
可知矣昔曾子造深於真積而功竭於末由夫
子知其有得也故呼其名而告之以為道惟一
本而物有殊致渾然在中者實涵萬化之原寂
然不動者自妙順應之感蓋守之至約則裕用
而不窮而操之有要則多學非所事也曾子聞
言而悟應聲而唯不必擬議於言語之間而真
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」子出，門人問曰：「何謂也？」曾子曰：「夫子之道，忠恕而已矣。」

洪世遷

考試官學正李批：「詞不費而意義自見，蓋聞聖敬而有得者。」

考試官教授向批：「一貫之旨發於忠恕，意融辭達，僅見此作。」

大賢聞聖道而有得，而因以發之也。夫道一而已，大賢唯於有聞，而發於所問，聖門授受之妙可知矣。昔曾子造深於真積，而功竭於末由。夫子知其有得也，故呼其名而告之，以為道惟一本，而物有殊致；渾然在中者，實涵萬化之原；寂然不動者，自妙順應之感。蓋守之至約，則裕用而不窮；而操之有要，則多學非所事也。曾子聞言而悟，應聲而唯，不必擬議於言語之間，而真
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, “Shen! My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Master Zeng replied, “Yes.” When the Master had gone out, the disciples asked, “What did he mean?” Master Zeng said, “The Master’s Way consists simply of loyalty and reciprocity.”

Hong Shiqian

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “The wording is economical, yet the meaning reveals itself. This seems the work of someone who has heard the sage’s reverence [?] and gained understanding.”

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: “The meaning of the single unifying principle is brought out through loyalty and reciprocity. The ideas are integrated and the language expressive: only in this composition have I seen this achieved.”

The great worthy heard the sage’s Way and gained understanding, and then took the occasion to elucidate it. The Way is but one. The great worthy assented upon hearing it and elucidated it when questioned: herein we can perceive the subtlety of transmitting and receiving instruction in the sage’s school. Formerly, Master Zeng attained profound understanding through the steady accumulation of genuine effort, and exerted himself to the utmost until there seemed no further path to follow. The Master knew that he had gained understanding, and therefore called him by name and instructed him: the Way has but one root, although things have diverse manifestations. What abides within as an undivided whole contains the source of all transformations; what is still and unmoving responds with spontaneous subtlety to whatever calls it forth. For when what one holds to is supremely simple, its application is abundant and inexhaustible; when one grasps the essential, extensive learning is no longer one’s pursuit. Master Zeng heard these words and awakened to their meaning, immediately answering, “Yes.” He had no need to deliberate over words, but truly …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
有得於口耳之外者矣然道不可以易聞而學
不容以頓悟此門人何謂之問所以發於夫子
旣出之後也曾子曉之以為至道難言而近取
自足故四敎無隱不聞所謂忠乎盡己不欺而
恕之體以立一言可行不聞所謂恕乎推心及
物而忠之用以行下學之成功即上達之心法
不可以殊觀也聖人之能事亦學問之極功初
非有二致也是則道有真見則言無費辭觀於
忠恕之喻而一貫之唯夫豈徒聞也哉大抵聖
===
敎無隱而至道難聞一貫之旨固門人所共承
而曾子所獨唯豈非時雨之化溥物均施而生
息之機隨分各足者哉是故四勿請事惟顏氏
子直任而不辭而方信忽疑雖穎悟如子貢而
猶有所未達也故曰參也竟以魯得之
極高明而道中庸
周欽
同考試官敎諭邵批〔講高明中庸處詞理精到〕
〔獨異諸作錄之〕
punctuated:
有得於口耳之外者矣。然道不可以易聞，而學不容以頓悟，此門人何謂之問所以發於夫子旣出之後也。曾子曉之，以為至道難言，而近取自足。故四敎無隱，不聞所謂忠乎？盡己不欺，而恕之體以立。一言可行，不聞所謂恕乎？推心及物，而忠之用以行。下學之成功，即上達之心法，不可以殊觀也。聖人之能事，亦學問之極功，初非有二致也。是則道有真見，則言無費辭。觀於忠恕之喻，而一貫之唯，夫豈徒聞也哉？大抵聖敎無隱，而至道難聞。一貫之旨，固門人所共承，而曾子所獨唯，豈非時雨之化，溥物均施，而生息之機，隨分各足者哉？是故四勿請事，惟顏氏子直任而不辭；而方信忽疑，雖穎悟如子貢，而猶有所未達也。故曰：「參也竟以魯得之。」

極高明而道中庸

周欽

同考試官敎諭邵批〔講高明中庸處，詞理精到。〕〔獨異諸作，錄之。〕
translation_en:
…and truly attained an understanding beyond mere speaking and hearing. Yet the Way cannot readily be apprehended through hearing, nor does learning admit of sudden enlightenment. This is why the disciples asked what the Master meant only after he had gone out. Zengzi explained to them that the ultimate Way is difficult to express, but that drawing upon what is close at hand is sufficient. Thus, nothing was concealed in the four teachings: had they not heard of what is called conscientiousness? By fully exerting oneself without deception, one establishes the substance of reciprocity. As for the single word that can guide one’s conduct, had they not heard of what is called reciprocity? By extending one’s own heart to others and things, one puts conscientiousness into practice. The achievement of learning below is precisely the method of the heart by which one reaches understanding above; these cannot be regarded as separate. What the sage can accomplish is also the ultimate achievement of learning: from the outset, these have never been two different things. Thus, when one truly perceives the Way, one’s words contain nothing superfluous. Considering Zengzi’s explanation through conscientiousness and reciprocity, and his assent to the single thread running through the Way, could his understanding have come merely from hearing? In general, the sage’s teachings conceal nothing, yet the ultimate Way is difficult to apprehend through hearing. All the disciples received the teaching concerning the single thread, but Zengzi alone assented to it. Is this not like the transforming influence of timely rain, spread impartially over all things, while each receives, according to its capacity, enough of the impulse to grow and flourish? Thus, it was Yan Hui alone who asked to put the four prohibitions into practice, directly accepting the responsibility without declining it. By contrast, even someone as perceptive as Zigong would move from confidence to sudden doubt, and still had points he had not understood. Hence the saying: “Shen ultimately attained it through his dullness.”

Reach the Utmost Loftiness and Brilliance, Yet Follow the Mean in Ordinary Practice

Zhou Qin

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: 〔In explaining loftiness and brilliance and the Mean in ordinary practice, both the wording and the reasoning are refined and exact.〕〔Distinctive among all the compositions; selected for inclusion.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭陳批說理明白而辭意渾融中庸
義當如此可式
考試官學正李批簡潔明當蓋精於中庸之理者
考試官教授向批辭不費而理自足
心復其體而事循其則君子修凝之功也蓋高
明者心之體而中庸者事之則也君子復之循
之而所以存心致知者於是盡矣中庸之意謂
夫天下之道統於吾心而散於事理心不復其
本然則無以爲致用之體事不究其當然則無
===
以周全體之用非所以合内外也君子之學何
如哉是故至虛之浡而清通無際至靈之瑩而
旁燭無疆吾心之體本高明也而累之於欲則
卑暗矣其必務崇有功而使其高者不少屈於
狥物渾然天啓之衷與太虛同其象焉緝熈有
學而使其明者不少昏於外誘洞然神發之知
於萬物無不照焉如是則心之體以立矣然豈
可徒狥于内而無所用乎彼物齊於正道而體
無所偏行本於定理而人不可易萬事之則有
punctuated:
同考試官教諭陳批：說理明白，而辭意渾融，中庸義當如此，可式。
考試官學正李批：簡潔明當，蓋精於中庸之理者。
考試官教授向批：辭不費而理自足。
心復其體而事循其則，君子修凝之功也。蓋高明者，心之體；而中庸者，事之則也。君子復之循之，而所以存心致知者於是盡矣。中庸之意謂：夫天下之道，統於吾心而散於事理。心不復其本然，則無以爲致用之體；事不究其當然，則無以周全體之用，非所以合内外也。君子之學何如哉？是故至虛之浡，而清通無際；至靈之瑩，而旁燭無疆。吾心之體本高明也，而累之於欲，則卑暗矣。其必務崇有功，而使其高者不少屈於狥物，渾然天啓之衷，與太虛同其象焉；緝熈有學，而使其明者不少昏於外誘，洞然神發之知，於萬物無不照焉。如是則心之體以立矣，然豈可徒狥于内而無所用乎？彼物齊於正道而體無所偏，行本於定理而人不可易，萬事之則有
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear, and the language and meaning are thoroughly integrated. This is how the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean should be expounded. It can serve as a model.”
Examiner Li, School Director, comments: “Concise, clear, and apt: surely the work of someone deeply versed in the principles of the Doctrine of the Mean.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “The language is economical, yet the reasoning is complete.”
For the mind to recover its fundamental substance and for affairs to follow their proper standards is the achievement of the gentleman’s cultivation and consolidation. Loftiness and illumination are the substance of the mind; centrality and constancy are the standards governing affairs. The gentleman recovers the former and follows the latter, thereby fully accomplishing the preservation of the mind and the extension of knowledge. The meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean is this: the Way of all under Heaven is united in my mind and distributed among the principles of affairs. Unless the mind recovers its original condition, there is no substance from which to put it into practice; unless one investigates what is proper in affairs, there is no way to encompass the functioning of that substance in its entirety. This would fail to unite the inner and the outer. What, then, is the gentleman’s learning like?
Thus, in the surging fullness of utter emptiness [?], it is clear and unobstructed, without limit; in the brilliance of utmost spiritual responsiveness, it illuminates every direction without bound. The substance of my mind is originally lofty and illuminated, but when burdened by desires it becomes low and dark. One must therefore strive for elevation with effective effort, ensuring that its loftiness is not diminished in the slightest by yielding to external things. Then the undivided inner nature disclosed by Heaven shares the character of the Great Void. Through learning that continually sustains illumination, one must ensure that its brightness is not dimmed in the slightest by external enticements. Then the penetrating awareness arising from its spiritual responsiveness leaves none of the myriad things unilluminated. In this way the substance of the mind is established. Yet how could one attend solely to the inner and make no practical use of it?
Things are brought into accord with the correct Way, so that their constitution is without deviation; conduct is grounded in settled principles, which people cannot alter. The standards governing the myriad affairs possess…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
中庸也而動之以私則差謬矣又必精裁度於
物來之應而用中善天下之則理有至當吾不
敢以高明之資而過於範圍也詳擬議於制事
之宜而庸行會天下之趨道有共由吾不敢以
偏陂之私而舍其正路也如是則道之用以行
矣夫體立而心存用行而知致內外交養所以
脩德也而道不於是凝哉抑觀子思上言君子
致廣大盡精微矣此復言其極高明而道中庸
夫廣大若蕩高明若虛也然道體之大非高廣
===
則無以容之而且精微之盡中庸之道則行之
而有常析之而不亂矣此君子之所以道會小
大而作聖之功於是為盡後之儒者乃主其一
偏而滋學者之惑噫其何以與於斯
以友天下之善士為未足又尚論古之人
頌其詩讀其書不知其人可乎是以論
其世也是尚友也
陳南星
同考試官教諭夏批講頌詩讀書作平日工夫
punctuated:
中庸也，而動之以私則差謬矣。又必精裁度於物來之應，而用中善天下之則。理有至當，吾不敢以高明之資而過於範圍也；詳擬議於制事之宜，而庸行會天下之趨。道有共由，吾不敢以偏陂之私而舍其正路也。如是則道之用以行矣。夫體立而心存，用行而知致，內外交養，所以脩德也，而道不於是凝哉？抑觀子思上言君子致廣大、盡精微矣，此復言其極高明而道中庸。夫廣大若蕩，高明若虛也，然道體之大，非高廣則無以容之。而且精微之盡、中庸之道，則行之而有常，析之而不亂矣。此君子之所以道會小大，而作聖之功於是為盡。後之儒者乃主其一偏，而滋學者之惑。噫，其何以與於斯？
以友天下之善士為未足，又尚論古之人。頌其詩，讀其書，不知其人可乎？是以論其世也，是尚友也。
陳南星
同考試官教諭夏批：講頌詩讀書作平日工夫
translation_en:
…the constant mean; but when selfishness sets things in motion, deviation and error result. One must also judge and weigh precisely how to respond to things as they arise, applying the mean to perfect the standards of the world. Principle has its supremely fitting measure; I dare not use my capacity for loftiness and illumination to exceed its bounds. One must deliberate carefully upon what is appropriate in managing affairs, bringing the world's pursuits together through constant practice. The Way has a path shared by all; I dare not abandon its proper course through selfish partiality. In this manner, the functioning of the Way is put into practice. When the substance is established, the mind is preserved; when its functioning is carried out, knowledge is fully extended. Nourishing the inner and outer together is how one cultivates virtue. Would the Way not thereby become firmly established?
Consider, moreover, how Zisi says above that the gentleman extends himself to breadth and greatness and exhaustively investigates the subtle and minute. Here he again speaks of reaching the utmost loftiness and illumination while following the constant mean. Breadth and greatness may seem unbounded, and loftiness and illumination may seem empty. Yet the greatness of the Way's substance cannot be accommodated without loftiness and breadth. Moreover, through exhaustive investigation of the subtle and minute and the practice of the constant mean, its enactment has constancy and its analysis remains orderly. This is how the gentleman brings together the small and the great in the Way, thereby completing the work of becoming a sage. Later Confucian scholars instead championed one partial aspect, increasing the perplexity of learners. Alas, how could they participate in this achievement?
“Considering friendship with the good men of the world insufficient, one goes further and discusses the people of antiquity. Reciting their poems and reading their writings, can one fail to know what sort of people they were? Thus one examines their age. This is reaching back to befriend the ancients.”
Chen Nanxing
Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: His treatment of reciting poems and reading writings as the work of daily cultivation…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
最爲有見他作未及此也
同考試官教諭方批順理發揮得孟子立言之意而
結末歸之立志可占所養
考試官學正李批說尚友處得旨
考試官教授向批辭意精雅
大賢言士能進友古人則取善遠矣夫進善無
止法也友盡天下而復求古人斯其爲善進也
哉昔孟子告萬章取友至此若謂士之取善以
言乎廣則天下以爲量以言乎遠則千古以爲
===
徒今夫天下之善士吾旣得而友之矣然善士
之成名不可多見於斯世而其人之純德懿行
容有未備於所友者乎是未可以遽自足也君
子之取友不必盡出於一時而古人之令聞百
世孰非吾所當論交者乎是不可以弗之考也
是何也蓋古人往矣而其道在詩書吾旣嘗誦
其詩矣曰是古人之和聲述志者也然詩其聲
也其人不在是也習其聲而不知其人君子有
弗取焉又嘗讀其書矣曰是古人之立言道事
punctuated:
最爲有見，他作未及此也。
同考試官教諭方批：順理發揮，得孟子立言之意，而結末歸之立志，可占所養。
考試官學正李批：說尚友處得旨。
考試官教授向批：辭意精雅。
大賢言士能進友古人，則取善遠矣。夫進善無止法也，友盡天下而復求古人，斯其爲善進也哉！昔孟子告萬章取友至此，若謂士之取善，以言乎廣，則天下以爲量；以言乎遠，則千古以爲徒。今夫天下之善士，吾旣得而友之矣。然善士之成名，不可多見於斯世，而其人之純德懿行，容有未備於所友者乎？是未可以遽自足也。君子之取友，不必盡出於一時，而古人之令聞百世，孰非吾所當論交者乎？是不可以弗之考也。是何也？蓋古人往矣，而其道在詩書。吾旣嘗誦其詩矣，曰：是古人之和聲述志者也。然詩其聲也，其人不在是也。習其聲而不知其人，君子有弗取焉。又嘗讀其書矣，曰：是古人之立言道事
translation_en:
…is especially perceptive; the other compositions do not measure up to this.
Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “The exposition follows the argument coherently and captures Mencius’s intent in these words. Its conclusion returns to establishing one’s resolve, allowing us to gauge the writer’s self-cultivation.”
Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The discussion of befriending the ancients captures the essential meaning.”
Examiner Xiang, Instructor, comments: “The wording and ideas are refined and elegant.”
The great worthy says that if a scholar can advance to befriending the ancients, his pursuit of goodness will reach far indeed. Advancing in goodness admits of no stopping point. Having befriended all under Heaven, he then seeks out the ancients: how well he advances! When Mencius spoke to Wan Zhang about choosing friends, he carried the matter this far, as though to say that, in seeking goodness, a scholar takes all under Heaven as his measure of breadth and the people of a thousand ages as his companions across time.
Now I have already found and befriended the good scholars of the world. Yet good scholars who achieve renown are not often encountered in this age. Might there be aspects of pure virtue and admirable conduct that are not fully represented among those I have befriended? Thus I cannot hastily rest content. The gentleman need not choose all his friends from a single age. Among the ancients whose fine reputations endure for a hundred generations, who is not someone with whom I ought to consider forming a friendship? Thus I cannot fail to examine them.
Why is this? The ancients have passed away, but their Way remains in their poems and writings. I have recited their poems, saying: these are how the ancients harmonized sounds and expressed their aspirations. Yet poems are their voices; the people themselves are not contained therein. To become familiar with their voices without knowing the people is something the gentleman will not accept. I have also read their writings, saying: these are how the ancients set forth their words and recounted affairs…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
者也然書其言也其人則其行也得其言而弗
求其行吾不知其可焉故必稽載籍之所傳徵
往哲之遺行而其動爲世道於當時者吾將麗
其澤以自益卽詩書之陳言考古人之實事而
其行爲世法於平生者吾將通其志而定交如
是則其於取友也不亦尚矣哉蓋友以天下特
兼善天下耳而復能求之古人則其取善以自
淑者當必與終古而俱遠矣夫何有窮已耶友
盡一世特一世之士耳而至於取友前世則其
===
觀人以成已者方且等百世而上之矣夫何可
限量耶取友之道於是爲盡而士之爲士蓋將
終其身而不能以一日無友矣章也其知此義
哉大抵士生天地間欲爲千百世之名則當有
千百世之志故伊尹之慕道堯舜孟子之願學
孔子皆志定也厥後一德相湯以成聖業七篇
傳道以詔萬世而伊孟之名卒與堯舜孔子竝
傳使其在當時訑訑然曰我旣爲天下善士矣
則考德其時信莫有過之而未必有後世之名
punctuated:
者也。然書其言也，其人則其行也。得其言而弗求其行，吾不知其可焉。故必稽載籍之所傳，徵往哲之遺行，而其動爲世道於當時者，吾將麗其澤以自益；卽詩書之陳言，考古人之實事，而其行爲世法於平生者，吾將通其志而定交。如是，則其於取友也，不亦尚矣哉！蓋友以天下，特兼善天下耳；而復能求之古人，則其取善以自淑者，當必與終古而俱遠矣，夫何有窮已耶？友盡一世，特一世之士耳；而至於取友前世，則其觀人以成已者，方且等百世而上之矣，夫何可限量耶？取友之道於是爲盡，而士之爲士，蓋將終其身而不能以一日無友矣。章也，其知此義哉！

大抵士生天地間，欲爲千百世之名，則當有千百世之志。故伊尹之慕道堯舜，孟子之願學孔子，皆志定也。厥後，一德相湯以成聖業，七篇傳道以詔萬世，而伊孟之名卒與堯舜孔子竝傳。使其在當時訑訑然曰：「我旣爲天下善士矣！」則考德其時，信莫有過之，而未必有後世之名
translation_en:
…were the means by which they did so. Yet writings are their words, whereas the men themselves are revealed in their conduct. To grasp their words without seeking to understand their conduct—I do not see how this could be acceptable. Thus one must investigate what the records transmit and examine the surviving accounts of earlier worthies’ conduct. Where their actions served the Way in their own age, I shall draw upon their beneficent influence to improve myself. Through the words preserved in the Odes and Documents, I shall examine the actual deeds of the ancients. Where their lifelong conduct provided a model for the world, I shall comprehend their aspirations and establish friendship with them. Is this not an exalted way of choosing friends? For making friends throughout the world merely extends the pursuit of goodness throughout the world. If one can also seek friends among the ancients, then drawing upon goodness to improve oneself must reach as far as antiquity itself. How could it ever come to an end? Even if one befriends everyone in an age, they are still only the scholars of that single age. But when one comes to seek friends in earlier ages, learning from others to perfect oneself reaches back through a hundred generations and beyond. How could its extent be measured? Here the way of choosing friends finds its fullest expression. A scholar, in fulfilling his calling, will throughout his life be unable to pass even a single day without friends. Zhang, may you understand this meaning!

In general, a scholar born between Heaven and Earth who wishes to win renown lasting hundreds or thousands of generations must possess aspirations extending across hundreds or thousands of generations. Thus Yi Yin’s yearning for the Way of Yao and Shun, and Mengzi’s wish to learn from Kongzi, both arose from firmly settled aspirations. Thereafter, Yi Yin assisted Tang with single-minded virtue to accomplish the work of a sage, while Mengzi transmitted the Way in seven books to instruct all subsequent generations. Their names were ultimately handed down alongside those of Yao, Shun, and Kongzi. Had they complacently declared in their own day, “I am already a good scholar of the world!” then, judging their virtue against that of their contemporaries, surely no one would have surpassed them; yet they might not have attained renown in later ages…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
如此也矣孟子之告萬章即其所自爲志者而
惜乎章之不足以語此
易
忠信所以進德也修辭立其誠所以居業
也
周欽
同考試官教諭邵批進德居業不外乎誠此作發
揮明白而於居業處尤善體貼殆知學者
同考試官教諭陳批發得脩辭居業意出錄之
考試官學正李批體認親切語不煩而意盡
考試官教授向批簡潔
内外一本於誠君子進脩之功也夫誠者聖功
之本也君子德業之盛非誠而能之乎文言申
九三乾乾惕若之意謂夫及時進脩者君子之
心合一爲功者進脩之道是故蘊之而爲德行
君子固欲其進矣是豈可以襲取乎哉必其主
於心者存誠以立其體克已以復其初志意之
所在旣盡已而無僞念慮之所發復以實而不
punctuated:
如此也矣。孟子之告萬章，即其所自爲志者，而惜乎章之不足以語此！

易

忠信所以進德也，修辭立其誠，所以居業也。

周欽

同考試官教諭邵批：進德居業，不外乎誠。此作發揮明白，而於居業處尤善體貼，殆知學者。

同考試官教諭陳批：發得脩辭居業意出，錄之。

考試官學正李批：體認親切，語不煩而意盡。

考試官教授向批：簡潔。

内外一本於誠，君子進脩之功也。夫誠者，聖功之本也。君子德業之盛，非誠而能之乎？文言申九三乾乾惕若之意，謂夫及時進脩者，君子之心；合一爲功者，進脩之道。是故蘊之而爲德行，君子固欲其進矣，是豈可以襲取乎哉？必其主於心者，存誠以立其體，克已以復其初。志意之所在，旣盡已而無僞；念慮之所發，復以實而不
translation_en:
…such as this. What Mengzi told Wan Zhang was precisely what he himself had made his aspiration. Yet alas, Wan Zhang was not equal to discussing this!

Book of Changes

“Loyalty and trustworthiness are the means of advancing virtue; refining one's words and establishing one's sincerity are the means of abiding in one's work.”

Zhou Qin

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: Advancing virtue and abiding in one's work go no further than sincerity. This composition develops the meaning clearly, and its treatment of abiding in one's work shows especially fine understanding. Its author is surely someone who understands learning.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: It brings out the meaning of refining one's words and abiding in one's work. Select it.

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: The understanding is intimate and exact; the language is economical yet conveys the meaning fully.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: Concise and clear.

That the inward and the outward alike are rooted in sincerity is the achievement of the gentleman's advancement and cultivation. Sincerity is the foundation of the work of becoming a sage. Could the gentleman attain flourishing virtue and accomplishment without sincerity? The Commentary on the Words of the Text elaborates the meaning of the third yang line's “unceasing diligence” and “vigilant caution.” It means that advancing and cultivating oneself at the proper time is the gentleman's intention, and that uniting these in a single endeavor is the way of advancement and cultivation. Thus, when what is stored within becomes virtuous conduct, the gentleman naturally wishes to advance it. But can this be acquired merely by appropriating outward forms? What governs his heart must preserve sincerity to establish its foundation and overcome the self to restore its original state. In the direction of his purpose and intentions, he already gives himself fully, without falsity; in the arising of his thoughts and reflections, he likewise proceeds with truthfulness and does not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
欺心蓋無不誠矣將見誠精而明義理爲之昭
融有主則虛私欲以之淨盡光輝生於篤實之
餘而日進無疆自可以上達天德矣忠信非所
以進德乎行之而爲事業君子固欲其脩矣是
豈可以强爲乎哉必其見於言者旣出而鄙悖
斯遠未發而靜專是守信立於先辭有稽而道
著誠孚於後事有實而理存辭蓋無不誠矣將
見持循旣定則立方而有恒發見當可雖處雜
而不厭居安裕於自得之後而厥脩罔覺自可
===
===
以優入聖域矣脩辭立誠非所以居業乎是則
進德者素豫於内所以充乎外也居業者致脩
於外所以養乎内也君子之學内外交脩如此
此九三之所以无咎也抑論聖人之學以誠敬
爲入門故曰敬義立而德不孤乾之所謂進脩
者卽學聖之功也夫子言誠而不及敬何哉蓋
因其剛健不息故專以誠而發之耳而其所謂
惕若者又豈能外乎敬耶故欲從事於進脩者
當以誠爲本而所以存誠者必以主敬爲先
punctuated:
欺，心蓋無不誠矣。將見誠精而明，義理爲之昭融；有主則虛，私欲以之淨盡。光輝生於篤實之餘，而日進無疆，自可以上達天德矣。忠信非所以進德乎？行之而爲事業，君子固欲其脩矣，是豈可以强爲乎哉？必其見於言者，旣出而鄙悖斯遠，未發而靜專是守。信立於先，辭有稽而道著；誠孚於後，事有實而理存。辭蓋無不誠矣。將見持循旣定，則立方而有恒；發見當可，雖處雜而不厭。居安裕於自得之後，而厥脩罔覺，自可以優入聖域矣。脩辭立誠非所以居業乎？

是則進德者，素豫於内，所以充乎外也；居業者，致脩於外，所以養乎内也。君子之學，内外交脩如此，此九三之所以无咎也。

抑論聖人之學，以誠敬爲入門，故曰：「敬義立而德不孤。」乾之所謂進脩者，卽學聖之功也。夫子言誠而不及敬，何哉？蓋因其剛健不息，故專以誠而發之耳。而其所謂惕若者，又豈能外乎敬耶？故欲從事於進脩者，當以誠爲本，而所以存誠者，必以主敬爲先。
translation_en:
…deceit; the heart is thus sincere in every respect. Then sincerity will become pure and luminous, and moral principles will thereby shine forth in clarity and harmony. With a governing principle, the heart becomes open, and selfish desires are thereby entirely cleared away. Radiance arises from deep integrity, and daily advancement knows no bounds: one can naturally attain the virtue of Heaven above. Are loyalty and trustworthiness not the means of advancing virtue? When put into practice as undertakings, these are certainly what the gentleman wishes to cultivate. But can this be achieved by forcing it? In what finds expression in words, once speech issues forth, vulgarity and perversity must be kept far away; before it issues forth, stillness and concentration must be maintained. Trustworthiness is established beforehand: words have a basis, and the Way becomes manifest. Sincerity is borne out afterward: deeds have substance, and principle abides in them. One’s words are thus sincere in every respect. Then, once what one holds to and follows is settled, one establishes upright standards and remains constant. When their expression is fitting, one does not weary even amid complicated affairs. Having attained understanding for oneself, one dwells in ease and ample composure, cultivating oneself without being conscious of the effort; one can naturally enter with ease into the realm of sagehood. Is refining one’s words and establishing sincerity not the means of abiding in one’s work?

Thus, advancing virtue means preparing oneself inwardly beforehand, so as to give fullness to one’s outward conduct; abiding in one’s work means carrying cultivation to completion outwardly, so as to nourish oneself inwardly. In the gentleman’s learning, the inner and outer are cultivated together in this way. This is why the Nine in the Third Place is without blame.

Moreover, in discussing the learning of the sages, sincerity and reverence are its gateway. Thus it is said: “When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue is not isolated.” What the Qian hexagram calls advancing virtue and cultivating one’s work is precisely the effort of learning to become a sage. Why, then, does the Master speak of sincerity without mentioning reverence? Because the hexagram embodies unceasing strength and vigor, he expounds its meaning specifically through sincerity. Yet how could its injunction to remain watchfully apprehensive lie outside reverence? Therefore, those who wish to undertake the advancement of virtue and the cultivation of their work should take sincerity as their foundation; and to preserve sincerity, they must first make reverence their governing principle.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
夫易聖人之所以極深而研幾也
林耀
同考試官教諭邵批講極深研幾意思明白亦學
易而有得者
同考試官教諭陳批歸重聖人作易極是
考試官學正李批辭暢理明
考試官教授向批發揮題意殆盡
大傳原易之妙用皆聖人發之也夫易聖人之
蘊也極深研幾而易之用盡矣昔大傳之意謂
===
夫惟易有以冒天下之道惟聖人有以成易之
能人知辭占象變爲易之用矣抑豈知聖人之
所爲乎是故吉凶悔吝隱於無形者深也深則
蘊奧莫測充周無窮不可以意逆矣而辭占之
至精者有以具焉夫豈辭占之自能哉聖人所
以極之也蓋其明察乎卦之情僞而小大以齊
洞見夫爻之時物而上下不一故繫之辭焉以
明失得之報斷之占焉以决趨避之方由是象
事可以知器占事可以知來而吉凶悔吝受命
punctuated:
夫易，聖人之所以極深而研幾也。
林耀
同考試官教諭邵批：講極深研幾意思明白，亦學易而有得者。
同考試官教諭陳批：歸重聖人作易，極是。
考試官學正李批：辭暢理明。
考試官教授向批：發揮題意殆盡。
大傳原易之妙用，皆聖人發之也。夫易，聖人之蘊也。極深研幾，而易之用盡矣。昔大傳之意謂：夫惟易有以冒天下之道，惟聖人有以成易之能。人知辭占象變爲易之用矣，抑豈知聖人之所爲乎？是故吉凶悔吝隱於無形者，深也。深則蘊奧莫測，充周無窮，不可以意逆矣，而辭占之至精者有以具焉。夫豈辭占之自能哉？聖人所以極之也。蓋其明察乎卦之情僞，而小大以齊；洞見夫爻之時物，而上下不一。故繫之辭焉，以明失得之報；斷之占焉，以决趨避之方。由是象事可以知器，占事可以知來，而吉凶悔吝受命
translation_en:
“The Changes is that by which the sages plumb the depths and investigate the incipient.”
Lin Yao
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient is clear in meaning. This, too, is someone who has gained understanding through studying the Changes.”
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Placing the emphasis on the sages’ creation of the Changes is entirely correct.”
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “The language flows freely, and the principles are clear.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “The meaning of the topic is developed almost exhaustively.”
The Great Commentary traces the marvelous functions of the Changes to their source: all were brought forth by the sages. The Changes embodies the sages’ profound understanding. By plumbing the depths and investigating the incipient, they brought the functions of the Changes to their fullest realization. The meaning of the Great Commentary was this: only the Changes can encompass the Way of all under Heaven, and only the sages can fully realize the capacities of the Changes. People know that statements, prognostications, images, and transformations constitute the functions of the Changes; but do they understand what the sages accomplished?
Thus, auspiciousness, misfortune, regret, and humiliation, concealed in the formless, constitute the depths. Being deep, their hidden mysteries are unfathomable; they pervade everything without limit and cannot be anticipated by conjecture. Yet the utmost refinement of the statements and prognostications can encompass them. Could the statements and prognostications accomplish this by themselves? They are the means by which the sages plumbed the depths. For the sages clearly discerned the genuine and false circumstances of the hexagrams, bringing the small and the great into due order; they penetrated the times and things represented by the lines, whose upper and lower positions differ. Therefore they appended statements to illuminate the consequences of failure and success, and made determinations through prognostication to decide what to pursue and what to avoid. In this way, by representing affairs through images one can understand concrete implements, and by divining about affairs one can know what is to come; auspiciousness, misfortune, regret, and humiliation receive the inquiry …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
如嚮矣是至精也者非聖人之所以極深乎陰
陽老少藏於無象者幾也幾則端倪未判朕兆
至微不可以力求矣而象變之至變者有以具
焉夫豈象變之自爲哉聖人所以研之也蓋其
倚數天地而妙契夫參伍錯綜效法大衍而化
裁於分揲掛扐故示之以爻以著竒偶之分定
之以象以别動靜之機由是兼六畫而成卦分
六位而成章而陰陽老少變動不居矣是至變
也者非聖人之所以研幾乎是則深幾著而易
===
理盡易理盡而民用周聖人作易之功大矣雖
然易固作於聖人然考其行事以易爲準則是
聖人爲易之用矣其何以能作耶蓋易天道也
聖人之心與天爲一故極深研幾者因易以發
其蘊而崇德廣業者用易以踐其實皆所以體
乎天也究而言之聖人與易一而已而謂聖人
爲易之用其信然哉
書
以閏月定四時成歲
punctuated:
如嚮矣。是至精也者，非聖人之所以極深乎？陰陽老少藏於無象者，幾也。幾則端倪未判，朕兆至微，不可以力求矣，而象變之至變者有以具焉。夫豈象變之自爲哉？聖人所以研之也。蓋其倚數天地，而妙契夫參伍錯綜；效法大衍，而化裁於分揲掛扐。故示之以爻，以著竒偶之分；定之以象，以别動靜之機。由是兼六畫而成卦，分六位而成章，而陰陽老少變動不居矣。是至變也者，非聖人之所以研幾乎？是則深幾著而易理盡，易理盡而民用周。聖人作易之功大矣！雖然，易固作於聖人，然考其行事，以易爲準，則是聖人爲易之用矣，其何以能作耶？蓋易，天道也。聖人之心與天爲一，故極深研幾者，因易以發其蘊；而崇德廣業者，用易以踐其實，皆所以體乎天也。究而言之，聖人與易一而已，而謂聖人爲易之用，其信然哉？

書

以閏月定四時成歲。
translation_en:
…like an echo. Is this utmost refinement not the means by which the sages plumbed the depths? The incipient workings are yin and yang, old and young, concealed before they take perceptible form. At this incipient stage, beginnings are not yet distinguishable, and the signs are exceedingly subtle: they cannot be sought by force. Yet the utmost capacity for change embodied in images and transformations encompasses them. Could images and transformations accomplish this by themselves? It was through them that the sages investigated these incipient workings. Drawing upon the numbers of Heaven and Earth, they wondrously accorded with their interweaving and cross-combination in threes and fives. Taking the Great Expansion procedure as their model, they adapted its operations of dividing the stalks, counting them off, setting one aside, and holding the remainders between the fingers. Thus they displayed these workings through the lines, making clear the distinction between odd and even; they established them through the images, distinguishing the impulses toward movement and stillness. In this way, six lines were combined to form a hexagram, and six positions were distinguished to form its pattern; yin and yang, old and young, changed and moved without remaining fixed. Is this utmost capacity for change not the means by which the sages investigated incipient workings? Thus the depths and incipient workings become manifest, and the principles of the Changes are fully revealed; when these principles are fully revealed, the practical needs of the people are comprehensively met. Great indeed was the achievement of the sages in making the Changes!

Nevertheless, although the Changes was indeed made by the sages, if we examine their conduct, they took the Changes as their standard. This would mean that the sages served as the instrument of the Changes. How, then, could they have made it? The Changes is the Way of Heaven. The minds of the sages were one with Heaven. Thus, in plumbing the depths and investigating incipient workings, they drew upon the Changes to disclose its hidden meanings; in exalting virtue and extending their accomplishments, they employed the Changes to put its truths into practice. All these were means of embodying Heaven. Examined to the utmost, the sages and the Changes are simply one. Can it really be true, then, to say that the sages served as the instrument of the Changes?

Book of Documents

“By means of the intercalary month, determine the four seasons and complete the year.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳言
同考試官教諭方批曆法以人合天而尤詳於置閏
惟此篇敷敘明白宜冠諸作
同考試官教諭夏批說置閏處精確是不苟作者
考試官學正李批敘理既明措辭亦整
考試官教授向批天道正於曆法發明得旨
聖君命官歸餘日以制曆而術不違天矣夫天
運不齊而有餘日則所以歸之而齊以曆法者
豈不有在於置閏哉昔帝堯以此命羲和若曰
===
人君順天以授人時則作曆所不容已然曆生
於數而數有不齊茲何以盡其法而成信曆哉
今夫朞之常數固必三百有六旬六日矣然曆
以十二月而爲一歲歲之全數則止於三百六
十也積日以成月而日與天會之數視歲常多
五日有奇多則歲氣不以盈乎積月以成歲而
月與日會之數視歲常少五日有奇少則月朔
不以虛乎合盈與虛之數則一歲之積得十日
焉三歲之通得一月焉於此而不立之法則盈
punctuated:
陳言

同考試官教諭方批：曆法以人合天，而尤詳於置閏。惟此篇敷敘明白，宜冠諸作。

同考試官教諭夏批：說置閏處精確，是不苟作者。

考試官學正李批：敘理既明，措辭亦整。

考試官教授向批：天道正於曆法，發明得旨。

聖君命官歸餘日以制曆，而術不違天矣。夫天運不齊而有餘日，則所以歸之而齊以曆法者，豈不有在於置閏哉？昔帝堯以此命羲和，若曰：「人君順天以授人時，則作曆所不容已。然曆生於數，而數有不齊，茲何以盡其法而成信曆哉？今夫朞之常數，固必三百有六旬六日矣。然曆以十二月而爲一歲，歲之全數則止於三百六十也。積日以成月，而日與天會之數，視歲常多五日有奇，多則歲氣不以盈乎？積月以成歲，而月與日會之數，視歲常少五日有奇，少則月朔不以虛乎？合盈與虛之數，則一歲之積得十日焉，三歲之通得一月焉。於此而不立之法，則盈
translation_en:
Chen Yan

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: Calendrical methods bring human affairs into accord with Heaven, with particular attention to the insertion of intercalary months. This essay alone expounds the matter clearly and deserves to rank first among the compositions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: The discussion of inserting intercalary months is precise. This is the work of a conscientious writer.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The exposition of the principles is clear, and the wording is orderly as well.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: Heaven’s course is correctly represented through calendrical methods; the exposition grasps the essential meaning.

The sage ruler commanded his officials to gather the surplus days to construct the calendar, so that its methods would not depart from Heaven. The movements of Heaven are uneven and produce surplus days. Does not the means of gathering these days and bringing them into order through calendrical methods lie in inserting intercalary months? In former times, Emperor Yao instructed Xi and He on this matter, as though saying:

“A ruler follows Heaven in granting the people the seasons for their activities; thus, making a calendar is indispensable. Yet the calendar arises from numerical reckoning, and these numbers do not agree. How, then, can its methods be fully applied to produce a reliable calendar? Now, the standard number of days in a complete annual cycle must indeed be three hundred and sixty-six. Yet the calendar takes twelve months as one year, and the full count of days in such a year amounts to only three hundred and sixty. Days accumulate to form months, but the count for the sun to return to the same position relative to the heavens regularly exceeds this year by five days and a fraction. With this excess, is there not a surplus in the annual cycle of seasonal qi? Months accumulate to form years, but the count for the moon’s conjunctions with the sun regularly falls short of this year by five days and a fraction. With this shortage, is there not a deficit in the cycle of lunar beginnings? Combining the amounts of surplus and deficit yields an accumulation of ten days in one year; over three years, the total amounts to one month. If no method is established to deal with this, then the surplus …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
者何所於消虛者何所於息而歲時從差矣故
必察其月無中氣則置閏於是歲而多爲一月
以總其餘三歲一置則再行於五歲而歷十有
九歲以成一章如是則布月以紀時而氣朔可
齊春夏秋冬之各司其令者質之天而節候不
爽矣四時有不定乎一歲之時定而千百歲之
時胥此焉矣紀時以統歲而寒暑可稽子丑寅
卯之以名其歲者視諸時而天運不乖矣歲功
有不成乎一歲之歲成而千百歲之歲胥此焉
===
矣夫是之謂信曆而以之授人庶其可乎汝羲
曁和盍亦旣厥心哉抑此乃萬世曆法之祖也
上古聖人阜成民物參賛化育蓋必有治曆明
時之政至唐堯置閏則益詳矣然後之論者以
爲天運日行舒縮不同則歲宜漸差而病古曆
之簡易於是虞喜何承天諸人各以其意立爲
差法然亦隨時修改迄無定說今去東晉千餘
歲而考之日月之食司曆者不愆于時意與古
亦不甚相遠也要之聖人重曆之意惟在於敬
punctuated:
者何所於消，虛者何所於息，而歲時從差矣。故必察其月無中氣，則置閏於是歲，而多爲一月，以總其餘。三歲一置，則再行於五歲，而歷十有九歲以成一章。如是，則布月以紀時，而氣朔可齊；春夏秋冬之各司其令者，質之天而節候不爽矣。四時有不定乎？一歲之時定，而千百歲之時胥此焉矣。紀時以統歲，而寒暑可稽；子丑寅卯之以名其歲者，視諸時而天運不乖矣。歲功有不成乎？一歲之歲成，而千百歲之歲胥此焉矣。夫是之謂信曆，而以之授人，庶其可乎？汝羲曁和，盍亦旣厥心哉！
抑此乃萬世曆法之祖也。上古聖人阜成民物，參賛化育，蓋必有治曆明時之政，至唐堯置閏則益詳矣。然後之論者，以爲天運日行舒縮不同，則歲宜漸差，而病古曆之簡易。於是虞喜、何承天諸人，各以其意立爲差法，然亦隨時修改，迄無定說。今去東晉千餘歲，而考之日月之食，司曆者不愆于時，意與古亦不甚相遠也。要之，聖人重曆之意，惟在於敬
translation_en:
…by what means would the surplus be eliminated, and by what means would the deficit be replenished? The years and seasons would consequently fall out of alignment. Thus one must identify a month without a principal solar term and insert an intercalary month in that year, adding a month to account for the accumulated remainder. An intercalation is made once in three years, twice in five years, and a cycle is completed over nineteen years. In this way, months are arranged to mark the seasons, and solar terms and new moons can be brought into alignment. Spring, summer, autumn, and winter each exercise their proper seasonal authority; checked against Heaven, their seasonal signs do not deviate. Could the four seasons then fail to be fixed? Once the seasons of a single year are fixed, those of hundreds and thousands of years all follow from this. The seasons are recorded to organize the years, and cold and heat can be verified. Years named by the earthly branches zi, chou, yin, mao, and so forth, when checked against the seasons, do not diverge from Heaven’s movements. Could the work of the year then fail to be completed? Once a single year is duly completed, the years of hundreds and thousands of years all follow from this. This is what is called a reliable calendar. Would it not then be suitable to issue it to the people? You, Xi and He, why do you not also devote your minds fully to this!
Indeed, this is the foundation of calendrical methods for all ages. The sages of high antiquity nurtured and perfected the people and all things, participating in and assisting the transforming and nourishing work of Heaven and Earth. They surely had measures for regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons. By the time of Yao of Tang, the insertion of intercalary months made these still more precise. Yet later commentators held that Heaven’s movements and the sun’s course differed in their slowing and quickening, so that the years must gradually fall out of alignment; they therefore criticized the simplicity of ancient calendars. Accordingly, Yu Xi, He Chengtian, and others each devised methods of correction according to their own views. Yet these too were revised as circumstances required, and no settled account was ever reached. Now, more than a thousand years after the Eastern Jin, when we check against solar and lunar eclipses, those responsible for the calendar do not err in their timing. I suppose that their methods are not very far removed from those of antiquity either. In essence, the sages’ intention in attaching importance to the calendar lay solely in reverently…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
天勤民而稽分積數之精疎則付之專官而已
帝王與天同運而民物順治者其固有道哉
皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥庶
民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之光
陳南星
同考試官教諭方批立意正大措辭簡古而近
天子之光處尤見脫落
同考試官教諭夏批脫去俗套程式之文也
考試官學正李批簡當
===
考試官教授向批穩貼
君子贊敷言之妙而及其化焉夫訓化之感人
固也聖人則天以爲訓而民有弗協于極者哉
箕子若曰人君納民於極曲盡勸相之方能無
孚化之應是故旣作之極也而又歌詠以長其
言旣錫之福也而又諷誦以宣其意綱維體要
不外乎民彝物則之常義理宏通自足爲垂世
立教之典然衷由帝降人君代之而立言典自
天敘聖人則之而成訓是言匪私臆而理有大
punctuated:
天勤民，而稽分積數之精疎，則付之專官而已。帝王與天同運，而民物順治者，其固有道哉！

「皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光。」
陳南星

同考試官教諭方批：立意正大，措辭簡古，而近天子之光處，尤見脫落。
同考試官教諭夏批：脫去俗套，程式之文也。
考試官學正李批：簡當。
考試官教授向批：穩貼。

君子贊敷言之妙，而及其化焉。夫訓化之感人，固也。聖人則天以爲訓，而民有弗協于極者哉？箕子若曰：人君納民於極，曲盡勸相之方，能無孚化之應？是故旣作之極也，而又歌詠以長其言；旣錫之福也，而又諷誦以宣其意。綱維體要，不外乎民彝物則之常；義理宏通，自足爲垂世立教之典。然衷由帝降，人君代之而立言；典自天敘，聖人則之而成訓。是言匪私臆，而理有大
translation_en:
…revering Heaven and caring diligently for the people; as for the precision or imprecision of examining fractions and accumulating numbers, these matters are simply entrusted to specialist officials. Surely there is a Way by which emperors and kings move in concert with Heaven, and the people and all things are harmoniously governed!

“The extended exposition of the August Ultimate provides constant norms and instruction: its instruction comes from the Lord on High. All the common people take this extended exposition of the Ultimate as their instruction and put it into practice, thereby drawing near to the brilliance of the Son of Heaven.”
Chen Nanxing

Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor of a county Confucian school, comments: “The conception is upright and lofty, and the wording concise and antique. The treatment of ‘drawing near to the brilliance of the Son of Heaven’ is especially free of constraint.”
Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor of a county Confucian school, comments: “Free of conventional clichés, this is an essay worthy of serving as a model.”
Examiner Li, Instructor of a subprefectural Confucian school, comments: “Concise and apt.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor of a prefectural Confucian school, comments: “Sound and fitting.”

The gentleman praises the excellence of the extended exposition and proceeds to discuss its transforming influence. That instruction and transformation move people is certain. When the sage takes Heaven as his model in establishing instruction, can any among the people fail to accord with the Ultimate? Jizi seems to say: When the ruler brings the people within the Ultimate and exhausts every means of encouraging and assisting them, how could there fail to be a response of sincere transformation? Thus, having established the Ultimate for them, he further sings and chants to prolong his words; having bestowed blessings upon them, he further recites to make his meaning known. The guiding principles and essential substance extend no further than the enduring norms of human conduct and the laws of things. Their moral principles are comprehensive and penetrating, sufficient in themselves to serve as a canon for establishing instruction and transmitting it to later ages. Yet the moral mean is bestowed by the Lord on High, and the ruler speaks on his behalf; the constant standards are ordered by Heaven, and the sage models himself upon them to formulate instruction. These words are no private conjecture, and their principles have a great …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
原君之言卽天之言矣敷言之妙如此由是庶
民蒙其樂育之敎而動其秉彝之良匪直詠歌
之巳也服膺勿失而觀省以稽其成不但諷誦
之巳也祗遹有聞而躬行以踐其實將見民風
丕變庶幾道義之輝順帝則以周旋而進進之
機有不能以自已者矣衆志日新親炙文明之
化仰王言而承式而烝烝於乂有莫知其所以
者矣是蓋敎有成法性有均善君子以人治人
而民之從之也宜哉大抵躬行之敎易從而勉
强之情難久錫福之政有窮而鼓舞之化爲不
倦也敷言本諸身有而達乎民宜其於用休之
戒九歌之勸異用同心虞周之治此其所以爲
盛與
詩
有渰萋萋興雨祁祁雨我公田遂及我私
石磐
同考試官敎諭祝批〔天澤溥施不以公私爲先後而民心愛戴則若受公田之餘潤者此作得之〕
punctuated:
原，君之言卽天之言矣。敷言之妙如此，由是庶民蒙其樂育之敎，而動其秉彝之良。匪直詠歌之巳也，服膺勿失，而觀省以稽其成；不但諷誦之巳也，祗遹有聞，而躬行以踐其實。將見民風丕變，庶幾道義之輝，順帝則以周旋，而進進之機有不能以自已者矣；衆志日新，親炙文明之化，仰王言而承式，而烝烝於乂，有莫知其所以者矣。是蓋敎有成法，性有均善，君子以人治人，而民之從之也宜哉！大抵躬行之敎易從，而勉强之情難久；錫福之政有窮，而鼓舞之化爲不倦也。敷言本諸身有而達乎民，宜其於用休之戒、九歌之勸，異用同心。虞周之治，此其所以爲盛與！
詩
有渰萋萋，興雨祁祁。雨我公田，遂及我私。
石磐
同考試官敎諭祝批〔天澤溥施，不以公私爲先後，而民心愛戴，則若受公田之餘潤者，此作得之。〕
translation_en:
…source; the ruler’s words are thus Heaven’s words. Such is the subtle efficacy of setting forth these words. Through them, the common people receive his teaching, which delights in nurturing them, and their innate moral goodness is stirred. They do not merely sing his words: they hold them fast in their hearts, observing and examining themselves to assess their progress. Nor do they merely recite them: they reverently follow what they have heard and personally put its substance into practice. We shall see the customs of the people greatly transformed, approaching the radiance of the Way and righteousness. They will conduct themselves according to the Supreme Lord’s norms, with an impulse toward continual advancement that they cannot themselves restrain. The aspirations of the multitude will be renewed daily as they directly experience the transforming influence of enlightened culture. Looking up to the king’s words and accepting them as their model, they will advance toward good order without knowing how this has come about. This is because teaching has established methods, and human nature possesses goodness common to all. The gentleman governs people according to their own humanity: how fitting that the people should follow him!
In general, teaching through personal conduct is easy to follow, whereas a disposition maintained by forced effort is hard to sustain. Government that bestows blessings has its limits, but transformation through encouragement and inspiration never wearies. Setting forth words is rooted in what the ruler himself possesses and extends to the people. Fittingly, it shares the purpose of the admonition to encourage goodness and the exhortations of the Nine Songs, though their applications differ. Surely this is what made government under Yu and Zhou so flourishing!
Book of Odes
“Dense are the gathering clouds; copiously falls the rising rain. Rain upon our public fields, and then reach our private fields.”
Shi Pan
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔Heaven’s bounty is bestowed universally, without putting public or private fields first. Yet the people’s loving devotion makes them feel as though they receive the moisture left over from the public fields. This composition captures that meaning.〕

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正李批委曲清婉詩人愛領之意形容殆盡
考試官教授向批曲而盡
詩人冀天澤之下究有先公後私之義焉夫天
普萬物而無心也農人望雨於天而必先其君
其忠愛之心何切哉大田之雅農夫所以答甫
田也其三章若曰田害旣除所少者雨澤之滋
耳此豈吾農所能自致哉亦惟賴吾君之德而
已彼雲之不盛非多雨之徵也安得山川之出
===
雲也萋萋然其集矣乎雨之不徐非入土之候
也安得天之降時雨也祁祁然其興矣乎夫井
地畫而公私之界明助法行而後先之分定公
田中處君子之常祿所須也玆雨也其先雨我
公田乎君德之潛孚固宜其無恒暘之咎矣私
田外列野人之恒産所在也玆雨也其遂及我
私田乎天澤之普施固宜其有滿盈之象矣靈
貺之貽自當流之於旣溢餘潤所及亦將溥之
爲大同蓋足於此而通於彼寔農人怙德之誠
punctuated:
考試官學正李批：委曲清婉，詩人愛領之意形容殆盡。
考試官教授向批：曲而盡。
詩人冀天澤之下究，有先公後私之義焉。夫天普萬物而無心也，農人望雨於天而必先其君，其忠愛之心何切哉！大田之雅，農夫所以答甫田也。其三章若曰：田害旣除，所少者雨澤之滋耳。此豈吾農所能自致哉？亦惟賴吾君之德而已。彼雲之不盛，非多雨之徵也。安得山川之出雲也，萋萋然其集矣乎？雨之不徐，非入土之候也。安得天之降時雨也，祁祁然其興矣乎？夫井地畫而公私之界明，助法行而後先之分定。公田中處，君子之常祿所須也。玆雨也，其先雨我公田乎？君德之潛孚，固宜其無恒暘之咎矣。私田外列，野人之恒産所在也。玆雨也，其遂及我私田乎？天澤之普施，固宜其有滿盈之象矣。靈貺之貽，自當流之於旣溢；餘潤所及，亦將溥之爲大同。蓋足於此而通於彼，寔農人怙德之誠
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: Subtle, lucid, and graceful; it gives an almost exhaustive portrayal of the poet’s loving regard for his ruler [?].
Comment by Examiner Xiang, Instructor: Subtle and exhaustive.
In hoping that Heaven’s bounty will reach down everywhere, the poet expresses the principle of putting the public fields before the private. Heaven extends its blessings to all things without deliberate intent; yet when farmers look to Heaven for rain, they invariably put their ruler first. How ardent is their loyal affection! The ode “Great Fields” (Da tian) is the farmers’ response to “Vast Fields” (Fu tian). Its third stanza seems to say: Now that the pests afflicting the fields have been removed, all that is lacking is the nourishment of rain. How could we farmers bring this about ourselves? We can only rely upon our ruler’s virtue. Clouds that are not abundant give no sign of plentiful rain. How might the clouds issuing from mountains and rivers gather thickly together? Rain that does not fall gently gives no promise of penetrating the soil. How might Heaven’s seasonable rain begin falling in a gentle profusion?
Once the well-field lands are laid out, the boundaries between public and private fields become clear; once the system of assisting in cultivation is practiced, the order of precedence is established. The public fields occupy the center and supply the regular emoluments of the ruler. May this rain first fall upon our public fields! With the ruler’s virtue exerting its unseen influence, surely there should be no calamity of prolonged drought. The private fields are arrayed around the outside and constitute the country people’s permanent holdings. May this rain then reach our private fields! With Heaven’s bounty universally bestowed, surely there should be signs of abundance. The divine gift should naturally flow onward once it overflows; wherever its remaining moisture reaches, it will spread its benefits so that all share alike. For sufficiency here flowing through to there truly expresses the farmers’ sincere reliance upon their ruler’s virtue …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
先乎公而後乎私尤臣子急君之意也由是觀
之則其相賴之情相報之義舉見之矣抑考甫
田之詩有曰我取其陳食我農人又曰以祈甘
雨以介稷黍以穀我士女則上之人所以先之
者亦有道矣蓋補助之及時祈報之孔夙旣皆
出於至誠惻怛之心而其中公外私之制其勢
亦足以相維而可久則其民所以相賴而相報
者固其所也噫周人務本力穡之效一至此哉
有飶其香邦家之光有椒其馨胡考之寧
===
堯世美
同考試官敎諭祝 批 周人務本力穡之効體貼
明白
考試官學正李 批 氣充而詞裕可以爲多士
式矣
考試官敎授向 批 明暢
觀周人之慶豐年也而有宴賓養老之典焉夫
崇德尚齒國之大典也而周人將舉行之斯不
爲豐年之慶矣乎此報賽之頌所由作也意以
punctuated:
先乎公而後乎私，尤臣子急君之意也。由是觀之，則其相賴之情、相報之義，舉見之矣。抑考《甫田》之詩，有曰：「我取其陳，食我農人。」又曰：「以祈甘雨，以介稷黍，以穀我士女。」則上之人所以先之者，亦有道矣。蓋補助之及時，祈報之孔夙，旣皆出於至誠惻怛之心，而其中公外私之制，其勢亦足以相維而可久，則其民所以相賴而相報者，固其所也。噫！周人務本力穡之效，一至此哉！

有飶其香，邦家之光；有椒其馨，胡考之寧。

堯世美

同考試官敎諭祝批：周人務本力穡之効，體貼明白。

考試官學正李批：氣充而詞裕，可以爲多士式矣。

考試官敎授向批：明暢。

觀周人之慶豐年也，而有宴賓養老之典焉。夫崇德尚齒，國之大典也，而周人將舉行之，斯不爲豐年之慶矣乎？此報賽之頌所由作也。意以
translation_en:
…To put public interests before private ones expresses especially the intention of subjects to attend urgently to their ruler’s needs. Viewed in this light, their feelings of mutual reliance and their duty of mutual recompense are fully apparent. Moreover, examining the ode Broad Fields (Futian), we find: “I take the old grain and feed our farmers.” It also says: “To pray for sweet rain, to aid the millet crops, and to nourish our men and women.” Thus those above also have a proper way of taking the initiative. Timely assistance and diligent early observance of prayers and thanksgiving all arise from hearts of utmost sincerity and compassion. Moreover, the arrangement of public fields at the center and private fields around them provides a structure sufficient to sustain their mutual ties and endure. It is therefore entirely fitting that the people should rely upon and recompense those above. Ah! Could the Zhou people’s devotion to the fundamental occupation and their diligence in farming yield results such as these!

“Rich is their fragrance—the glory of the state and its ruling house; peppery is their aroma—the repose of the aged.”

Yao Shimei 堯世美

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, County School Instructor: “The results of the Zhou people’s devotion to the fundamental occupation and diligence in farming are clearly and sensitively apprehended.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Subprefectural School Instructor: “Full of vigor and ample in expression, this can serve as a model for the assembled scholars.”

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Prefectural School Instructor: “Clear and fluent.”

Observe how the Zhou people celebrated an abundant harvest: they had ceremonies for feasting guests and caring for the aged. Honoring virtue and respecting seniority are great rites of the state. When the Zhou people were about to perform them, did this not constitute a celebration of the abundant harvest? This is why the hymn of thanksgiving and fulfillment of vows was composed. Its meaning is that…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
吾人之力農也時至而事起人運而天從其獲
利於農固矣而利之所獲豈直以奉時祭而已
哉國有賓焉而燕享之禮不可已也而農之所
得實資之吾知野有豐年而利之溥者旣以裕
民則禮有時饗而物之備者可以致用其鉍然
而香者皆足以成享也由是而樂我嘉賓則燕
綏即席用孚上下之交而我周之乞言者胥此
出矣豈第登筵式啓明良之會而我周之尚賢
者即此在矣然則是舉也以煥人文以熈帝載
===
而天下將爲昭焉庸不爲邦家之光巳乎不但
巳也國有老焉而安養之典不可廢也而農之
所得實資之吾知民有餘利而國之所需者旣
裕則老有常餼而物之爲羞者自豐其椒然而
馨者皆足以致養也由是而供我耆老則太和
保合足以致可久之休而國老之在東膠者有
所養矣元氣滋培將以綏無疆之慶而庶老之
在虞庠者有所終矣然則是舉也以尊高年以
介眉壽而天下有大老焉庸不爲胡考之休巳
punctuated: 吾人之力農也，時至而事起，人運而天從，其獲利於農固矣。而利之所獲，豈直以奉時祭而已哉？國有賓焉，而燕享之禮不可已也，而農之所得實資之。吾知野有豐年，而利之溥者旣以裕民，則禮有時饗，而物之備者可以致用。其鉍然而香者，皆足以成享也。由是而樂我嘉賓，則燕綏即席，用孚上下之交，而我周之乞言者胥此出矣。豈第登筵，式啓明良之會，而我周之尚賢者即此在矣。然則是舉也，以煥人文，以熈帝載，而天下將爲昭焉，庸不爲邦家之光巳乎？不但巳也，國有老焉，而安養之典不可廢也，而農之所得實資之。吾知民有餘利，而國之所需者旣裕，則老有常餼，而物之爲羞者自豐。其椒然而馨者，皆足以致養也。由是而供我耆老，則太和保合，足以致可久之休，而國老之在東膠者有所養矣；元氣滋培，將以綏無疆之慶，而庶老之在虞庠者有所終矣。然則是舉也，以尊高年，以介眉壽，而天下有大老焉，庸不爲胡考之休巳
translation_en:
…When we devote ourselves to farming, work begins as the seasons arrive; human effort is exerted, and Heaven responds. That farming yields benefits is certain. But are those benefits used only to supply the seasonal sacrifices? The state has guests, and the rites of feasting them cannot be dispensed with: the produce of farming supplies these rites. I know that when the fields yield an abundant harvest, its widespread benefits enrich the people; then, when the appointed times for ritual feasts arrive, ample supplies are available for use. The fragrant offerings, described here by an unclear expression [?], are all sufficient to furnish the feast. Thus we delight our honored guests, who take their places at the banquet in peace and comfort, fostering trust between those above and those below. Our Zhou practice of soliciting words of counsel arises from this. Is it merely a matter of ascending to the banquet mats? It brings together an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, and therein lies our Zhou practice of honoring the worthy. Such an undertaking gives splendor to human culture and promotes the sovereign’s work, illuminating all under Heaven. Is this not a glory to the state?

Nor is this all. The state has elderly people, and the institutions for maintaining them in comfort cannot be abandoned: the produce of farming supplies these as well. I know that when the people have a surplus and the state’s needs are amply supplied, the elderly receive regular provisions, and the foods offered to them are naturally abundant. The pepper-fragrant offerings [?] are all sufficient for their nourishment. Thus we provide for our elders, preserving supreme harmony and bringing about enduring well-being, so that the elders of the state maintained at the Eastern School receive sustenance. The primal vital force is nourished, securing blessings without limit, so that the elders among the common people maintained at the Yu School can live out their remaining years. Such an undertaking honors the aged and aids them in attaining longevity, so that there are venerable elders throughout the realm. Is this not the blessing of a ripe old age…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎夫以崇德尚齒之典而皆於農乎得之則豐
年之慶誠莫大於此矣雖民力之普存而神實
尸其功焉是可以無報賽也哉抑論周之開國
以農而農亦有利於國其上下之相賴固如此
而是詩之力農則尤有足尚者祭祀燕享幽明
禮樂之際皆國典存焉而農之所獲則惟急此
之為務且侈之以為頌忠君愛國之誠眞有不
可掩者以是而報賽神必諒而歆之周有常豐
矣吁觀化於野歸善於君周之盛何如哉
===
春秋
丁亥楚子入陳〔宣公十有一年〕晉人宋人
衞人曹人同盟于清丘 宋師伐陳衞
人救陳〔俱宣公十有二年〕
王應時
同考試官教諭謝 批 議論切當深得經傳本意
可以為多士式矣
考試官學正李 批 得簡嚴體
考試官教授向 批 說傳既明措詞亦當
punctuated:
乎？夫以崇德尚齒之典，而皆於農乎得之，則豐年之慶誠莫大於此矣。雖民力之普存，而神實尸其功焉，是可以無報賽也哉？抑論周之開國以農，而農亦有利於國，其上下之相賴固如此。而是詩之力農，則尤有足尚者：祭祀燕享，幽明禮樂之際，皆國典存焉，而農之所獲，則惟急此之為務，且侈之以為頌，忠君愛國之誠眞有不可掩者。以是而報賽，神必諒而歆之，周有常豐矣。吁！觀化於野，歸善於君，周之盛何如哉！

春秋
丁亥，楚子入陳〔宣公十有一年〕。晉人、宋人、衞人、曹人同盟于清丘。宋師伐陳，衞人救陳〔俱宣公十有二年〕。

王應時

同考試官教諭謝批：議論切當，深得經傳本意，可以為多士式矣。
考試官學正李批：得簡嚴體。
考試官教授向批：說傳既明，措詞亦當。
translation_en:
…indeed? Since the institutions for honoring virtue and respecting age all derive their support from agriculture, surely no blessing of an abundant year is greater than this. Although the people's labor is everywhere engaged, the spirits truly preside over its achievement. Could one therefore dispense with offerings of thanksgiving? Moreover, Zhou founded its state upon agriculture, and agriculture in turn benefited the state: such was the mutual dependence of those above and those below. Yet there is something especially commendable about the dedication to agriculture expressed in this poem. Sacrifices and ceremonial banquets, rites and music concerning both the unseen and the visible worlds—all embody the state's institutions. The harvest's proceeds are devoted above all to these purposes; the poem further celebrates them at length in a hymn of praise. Its sincerity in loyalty to the ruler and love of the state truly cannot be concealed. With thanksgiving offerings made in this spirit, the spirits will surely recognize that sincerity and savor the offerings, and Zhou will enjoy enduring abundance. Ah! To observe the transforming influence of good government in the countryside and attribute its goodness to the ruler—how flourishing Zhou was!

Spring and Autumn Annals
On the dinghai day, the Viscount of Chu entered Chen. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xuan.〕 Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao joined in a covenant at Qingqiu. The army of Song attacked Chen; men of Wei came to Chen's rescue. 〔Both in the twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕

Wang Yingshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor (jiaoyu): The argument is apt and sound, thoroughly grasping the original meaning of the Classic and its commentary. It may serve as a model for the many scholars.
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor (xuezheng): It achieves a concise and rigorous style.
Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor (jiaoshou): Its exposition of the commentary is clear, and its wording is also appropriate.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
春秋詳兵信有罪大國之昧義者有罪與國之
失信者于以見違時干盟宋則失矣而衛亦未
爲得也且栗門之轘楚方藉口於陳而清丘之
盟晉亦爲謀於楚陳德楚而宋伐之固討貳之
兵也經乃貶之者何君子曰兵貴義動違時而
舉事非義也夫少西之變陳無賴矣晉不能庇
以成楚之強雖縣陳之惡有不可掩而復封之
德陳亦烏能以遽忘也爲宋計者省德以俟時
可矣不是之急而顧虐陳以徼怒於楚已則有
===
缺而謀人之貳不謂之先事加人不可也卒啓
申舟之釁而易子析骸之患誰其致之向無華
元之臣宋其可以爲國耶宋伐陳而衛救之固
恤患之師也經亦貶之者何君子曰國以信立
棄盟而爽約非信也清丘之歃衛人與焉宋不
自戢以釋憾于陳雖先君之約有不可背而恤
病討貳宋亦未必無詞也爲衛者協誠以輔伯
可矣不此之務而顧撓宋以市交於楚盟劑未
寒而同好輒棄不謂之見利忘義不可也卒致
punctuated:
春秋詳兵，信有罪大國之昧義者，有罪與國之失信者，于以見違時干盟，宋則失矣，而衛亦未爲得也。且栗門之轘，楚方藉口於陳；而清丘之盟，晉亦爲謀於楚。陳德楚而宋伐之，固討貳之兵也。經乃貶之者何？君子曰：「兵貴義動，違時而舉事，非義也。」夫少西之變，陳無賴矣。晉不能庇，以成楚之強。雖縣陳之惡有不可掩，而復封之德，陳亦烏能以遽忘也？爲宋計者，省德以俟時可矣。不是之急，而顧虐陳以徼怒於楚，已則有缺而謀人之貳，不謂之先事加人不可也。卒啓申舟之釁，而易子析骸之患，誰其致之？向無華元之臣，宋其可以爲國耶？

宋伐陳而衛救之，固恤患之師也。經亦貶之者何？君子曰：「國以信立，棄盟而爽約，非信也。」清丘之歃，衛人與焉。宋不自戢，以釋憾于陳，雖先君之約有不可背，而恤病討貳，宋亦未必無詞也。爲衛者，協誠以輔伯可矣。不此之務，而顧撓宋以市交於楚，盟劑未寒而同好輒棄，不謂之見利忘義不可也。卒致
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals scrutinizes warfare: it indeed condemns great states for failing to understand righteousness, and allied states for breaking faith. This shows that, in acting at the wrong time and violating the covenant, Song was at fault, while Wei was not in the right either. In the execution by dismemberment with chariots at Li Gate, Chu had found a pretext for intervening in Chen; through the covenant at Qingqiu, Jin likewise planned measures against Chu. Chen was grateful to Chu, and Song attacked it: this was certainly a campaign to punish divided allegiance. Why, then, does the Classic censure it? The gentleman says: “In warfare, what matters is acting righteously. To undertake a campaign at the wrong time is not righteous.” After the upheaval involving Shaoxi, Chen had no one to rely upon. Jin could not protect it and thereby allowed Chu to grow powerful. Although the evil of reducing Chen to a county could not be concealed, how could Chen promptly forget the kindness of restoring its enfeoffment? Those advising Song should simply have examined its virtue and awaited the proper time. Instead of making this their urgent concern, they oppressed Chen and provoked Chu’s anger. To have shortcomings oneself yet scheme against another’s divided allegiance must be called taking the initiative in attacking others. In the end, this set off the conflict over Shen Zhou. Who brought about the calamity in which people exchanged children to eat and split human bones for fuel? Had there been no minister such as Hua Yuan, could Song have continued as a state?

When Song attacked Chen, Wei came to its rescue: this was certainly an army sent to relieve distress. Why does the Classic censure it too? The gentleman says: “A state stands through good faith.
