To abandon a covenant and break an agreement is not good faith.” The men of Wei had participated in the blood oath at Qingqiu. Song failed to restrain itself and vented its resentment upon Chen. Although the agreement of Wei’s former ruler could not be disregarded, Song was not necessarily without grounds for invoking the obligation to relieve distress and punish divided allegiance. Those governing Wei should simply have cooperated sincerely in supporting the hegemon. Instead of attending to this, they obstructed Song to purchase friendship with Chu. Before the covenant was cold, they abruptly abandoned their common friendship. This must be called forgetting righteousness at the sight of advantage. In the end, they incurred…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
大國之怒而違盟不令之討誰其抗之向非孔
達之死衛亦何以自解耶可見陳有可憫而宋
之伐爲非宋不可背而衛之救爲失一書法間
而信義以明宋衛之罪均矣雖然亦晉景之無
以定伯也夫伯主者非服貳之難而無義以率
人之患辰陵之役晉則遺義於楚矣雖清丘之
盟豈固結人心之本招攜懷遠之道哉無怪乎
陳鄭回面以事楚而卒成楚莊之伯也
秋季孫意如會晉韓起齊國弱宋華亥衛
===
北宮佗鄭罕虎曹人杞人于厥憖〔昭公十有一年〕
三月公會劉子晉侯宋公蔡
侯衛侯陳子鄭伯許男曹伯莒子邾子
頓子胡子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊國
夏于召陵侵楚〔定公四年〕
林燫
同考試官教諭謝批出入諸傳曲盡當時事情蓋
究心於經學者
考試官學正李批聖人書法之妙發明殆盡
punctuated:
大國之怒，而違盟不令之討，誰其抗之？向非孔達之死，衛亦何以自解耶？可見陳有可憫，而宋之伐爲非；宋不可背，而衛之救爲失。一書法間，而信義以明，宋衛之罪均矣。雖然，亦晉景之無以定伯也。夫伯主者，非服貳之難，而無義以率人之患。辰陵之役，晉則遺義於楚矣。雖清丘之盟，豈固結人心之本、招攜懷遠之道哉？無怪乎陳鄭回面以事楚，而卒成楚莊之伯也。
秋，季孫意如會晉韓起、齊國弱、宋華亥、衛北宮佗、鄭罕虎、曹人、杞人于厥憖。〔昭公十有一年〕
三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衛侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚。〔定公四年〕
林燫
同考試官教諭謝批：出入諸傳，曲盡當時事情，蓋究心於經學者。
考試官學正李批：聖人書法之妙，發明殆盡。
translation_en:
…the anger of a great state; who could withstand its punitive action against a breach of covenant and disobedience to its commands? Had Kong Da not died, how could Wei have exonerated itself? Thus Chen deserved sympathy, and Song’s attack was wrong; yet Song could not be betrayed, and Wei’s rescue was a fault. Within a single instance of the Annals’ manner of recording events, trustworthiness and righteousness are made clear: Song and Wei were equally culpable. Nevertheless, this also resulted from Duke Jing of Jin’s inability to secure his hegemony. For a hegemon, the real concern is not the difficulty of subduing the disloyal, but the lack of righteousness with which to lead others. In the affair at Chenling, Jin had already yielded the moral initiative to Chu. Even the covenant at Qingqiu—could it provide a foundation for firmly uniting people’s hearts, or a means of attracting the estranged and winning over the distant? No wonder Chen and Zheng turned to serve Chu, ultimately establishing King Zhuang of Chu’s hegemony.
In autumn, Jisun Yiru met Han Qi of Jin, Guo Ruo of Qi, Hua Hai of Song, Beigong Tuo of Wei, Han Hu of Zheng, and representatives of Cao and Qi at Jueyin. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.〕
In the third month, the duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and invaded Chu. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding.〕
Lin Lian 林燫.
Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: He moves freely among the commentaries and thoroughly elucidates the circumstances of the time in all their particulars. Clearly, he has devoted himself to the study of the Classics.
Comment by Examiner Li, School Director: He elucidates almost completely the subtleties of the Sage’s manner of recording events.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授向批委曲
恤患而沮於力者春秋恕之攘夷而隳於利者
春秋陋之此可見厥憖之謀蔡力有不逮而召
陵之侵楚則勢可爲而沮於利也春秋誅意之
法如此夫蔡般被殺而棄疾遂圍晉于是乎有
厥憖之會維時圖楚有心而請蔡不得亦同歸
於無功爾巳列卿無貶春秋何待之恕耶蓋天
下之事固有屈於勢而格於力者君子亦盡其
在我而巳故伏甲之禍雖慘而憑陵之虐方張
===
使不爲遠圖而决於一逞則志未必得而彼勢
遂成漢陽諸姬楚且盡之矣况荀吳之慮方殷
而狐父之請又至物以無親庶幾省躬之義晉
之不德又有罪巳之言嗚呼壇坫未幾而蕞聚
繼之蓋日復一日也其情不可諒哉蔡侯被拘
而子元出質晉于是乎有召陵之役維時命卿
在會同盟合謀庶幾於王者之師矣列國書侵
春秋何陋之甚耶蓋天下之事固有以義始而
以利終者君子惟裁之義而巳故沉玉之憖有
punctuated:
考試官教授向批：委曲。

恤患而沮於力者，《春秋》恕之；攘夷而隳於利者，《春秋》陋之。此可見厥憖之謀蔡，力有不逮，而召陵之侵楚，則勢可爲而沮於利也。《春秋》誅意之法如此。夫蔡般被殺，而棄疾遂圍，晉于是乎有厥憖之會。維時圖楚有心，而請蔡不得，亦同歸於無功爾巳。列卿無貶，《春秋》何待之恕耶？蓋天下之事，固有屈於勢而格於力者，君子亦盡其在我而巳。故伏甲之禍雖慘，而憑陵之虐方張，使不爲遠圖而决於一逞，則志未必得，而彼勢遂成，漢陽諸姬，楚且盡之矣。况荀吳之慮方殷，而狐父之請又至，物以無親，庶幾省躬之義；晉之不德，又有罪巳之言。嗚呼！壇坫未幾，而蕞聚繼之，蓋日復一日也，其情不可諒哉？蔡侯被拘，而子元出質，晉于是乎有召陵之役。維時命卿在會，同盟合謀，庶幾於王者之師矣。列國書侵，《春秋》何陋之甚耶？蓋天下之事，固有以義始而以利終者，君子惟裁之義而巳。故沉玉之憖有
translation_en:
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “Subtle and thorough.”

Those who seek to relieve distress but are checked by insufficient strength receive the forbearance of the Spring and Autumn Annals; those who seek to repel the barbarians but let private gain undermine their efforts receive its censure. This distinction appears in the deliberations concerning Cai at Jueyin, where strength fell short, and in the invasion of Chu at Shaoling, where circumstances permitted action but private gain obstructed it. Such is the Annals’ method of judging intentions.

When Ban of Cai was killed and Qiji proceeded to besiege Cai, Jin convened the meeting at Jueyin. At that time, there was a will to take action against Chu, but the request concerning Cai was unsuccessful, and the undertaking likewise came to nothing. Yet the assembled ministers suffer no disparagement: why does the Annals treat them so leniently? In the affairs of the world, circumstances can indeed constrain action and insufficient strength can thwart it. The gentleman can only do all that lies within his own power. Thus, although the disaster inflicted by the concealed armed men was grievous, Chu’s tyrannical aggression was still gathering force. Had Jin abandoned long-term planning and resolved instead upon a single outburst, its aim might not have been achieved, while Chu’s power would have become firmly established. Chu would then have wiped out all the Ji-surnamed states north of the Han River.

Moreover, Xun Wu’s concerns were pressing, and Hufu’s request had also arrived. The words “things have no fixed attachments” [?] approached the principle of examining oneself; the words about Jin’s lack of virtue likewise expressed self-reproach. Alas! Scarcely had the diplomatic gathering ended before another small assembly followed: their efforts continued day after day. Should their circumstances not be regarded with understanding?

When the Marquis of Cai was detained and Ziyuan went out as a hostage, Jin undertook the campaign at Shaoling. At that time, duly appointed ministers attended the meeting, and the allied states planned together: their force almost resembled the army of a true king. Yet the action of the assembled states is recorded as an “invasion”: why does the Annals censure them so severely? In the affairs of the world, undertakings may indeed begin with righteousness and end in pursuit of gain. The gentleman judges them solely by righteousness. Thus, the resolve expressed by sinking jade in the water [?] had …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
詞而與國之誠又協使不從中止而畢力有爲
則王命可達而天討以昭漢水方城險不足恃
矣何荀寅之貨未得而蔡侯之請遂辭駕言水
潦聊爲苟且之圖藉口中山遽下班師之令嗚
呼裘馬見伐而索賂終之是以楚攻楚也厥罪
不其均乎觀於此可以見聖人忠恕之心義利
之辨矣雖然是亦蔡有罪焉不能自立而依人
以爲輕重此取敗之道也况般以饗燕就斃而
申復以珮馬見拘然則蔡之亡豈獨楚之罪也
===
哉
禮記
春作夏長仁也秋斂冬藏義也仁近於樂
義近於禮
洪世遷
考試官學正李批天地之德爲聖人制作之原能體認
者廑見此篇可錄
考試官敎授向批造語不凡而說理親切是知天地之禮樂者
記者言天地之德近乎禮樂以見制作之本也
punctuated:
詞，而與國之誠又協。使不從中止，而畢力有爲，則王命可達，而天討以昭，漢水方城，險不足恃矣。何荀寅之貨未得，而蔡侯之請遂辭？駕言水潦，聊爲苟且之圖；藉口中山，遽下班師之令。嗚呼！裘馬見伐，而索賂終之，是以楚攻楚也，厥罪不其均乎？觀於此，可以見聖人忠恕之心、義利之辨矣。雖然，是亦蔡有罪焉。不能自立，而依人以爲輕重，此取敗之道也。况般以饗燕就斃，而申復以珮馬見拘，然則蔡之亡，豈獨楚之罪也哉？

《禮記》
春作夏長，仁也；秋斂冬藏，義也。仁近於樂，義近於禮。
洪世遷

考試官學正李批：「天地之德，爲聖人制作之原。能體認者廑見，此篇可錄。」
考試官敎授向批：「造語不凡，而說理親切，是知天地之禮樂者。」

記者言天地之德近乎禮樂，以見制作之本也。
translation_en:
…words were spoken, and the allied states were also united in their sincerity. Had they not stopped midway, but exerted their full strength to accomplish something, the king’s command could have been carried out and Heaven’s punishment made manifest. The natural defenses of the Han River and Fangcheng would have afforded no dependable protection. Why, when Xun Yin failed to obtain the gifts he sought, was the Marquis of Cai’s request consequently refused? Alleging flooding, they contrived a makeshift expedient; invoking Zhongshan as a pretext, they abruptly ordered the army to return. Alas! A campaign undertaken because of fur robes and horses ended in demands for bribes: this was using Chu’s own ways to attack Chu. Were their offenses not equal? From this we can discern the Sage’s devotion to conscientiousness and reciprocity, and his distinction between righteousness and profit. Nevertheless, Cai too was at fault. Unable to stand independently, it relied on others to determine its own weight in affairs: this was the road to defeat. Moreover, Ban met his death at a banquet, while Shen in turn was detained over jade pendants and horses. Was Cai’s destruction, then, solely Chu’s fault?

Record of Rites
“To bring forth in spring and nurture growth in summer is benevolence; to gather in autumn and store in winter is righteousness. Benevolence is akin to music; righteousness is akin to ritual.”
Hong Shiqian

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: “The virtues of Heaven and Earth are the source of the sages’ establishment of institutions. Those capable of truly apprehending this are seldom seen. This essay merits inclusion.”
Comment by Examiner Xiang, Instructor: “The phrasing is uncommon, and the exposition of principle is clear and apt. Here is someone who understands the ritual and music of Heaven and Earth.”

The compiler of the Record states that the virtues of Heaven and Earth are akin to ritual and music, thereby revealing the foundation upon which the sages established their institutions.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
蓋天地之德仁與義而已而質之聖人之禮樂
夫豈遠哉今夫禮樂作於聖人而其原出於天
地是故必明於天地而後能興禮樂也何以言
之蓋天地之間一氣流行而四時異用方其陽
之用事也萬物作之於春而長之於夏蓋其生
理之翕聚則化機不容於自已而滋養之不息
則和氣之絪縕也謂非天地之仁乎及夫陰之
用事也萬物斂之以秋而藏之以冬蓋其生物
之旣成則化工不能以不止而嚴凝之愈肅則
===
性命之各復也謂非天地之義乎夫仁在天地
若與樂不相與矣然仁以生物而樂主於和故
春夏之氣行而同和樂之情於是肇焉則氣化
之周流與律呂之相生者同其機太和之默運
與聲音之克諧者合其妙是天地之仁與聖人
之樂實一致也仁不近於樂耶義在天地若與
禮不相涉矣然義以成物而禮主於序故秋冬
之質具而異序禮之制於是寓焉則品彙之各
成猶夫節文度數之有章大小之各正猶夫尊
punctuated: 蓋天地之德，仁與義而已，而質之聖人之禮樂，夫豈遠哉？今夫禮樂作於聖人，而其原出於天地，是故必明於天地，而後能興禮樂也。何以言之？蓋天地之間，一氣流行，而四時異用。方其陽之用事也，萬物作之於春，而長之於夏。蓋其生理之翕聚，則化機不容於自已；而滋養之不息，則和氣之絪縕也。謂非天地之仁乎？及夫陰之用事也，萬物斂之以秋，而藏之以冬。蓋其生物之旣成，則化工不能以不止；而嚴凝之愈肅，則性命之各復也。謂非天地之義乎？夫仁在天地，若與樂不相與矣。然仁以生物，而樂主於和，故春夏之氣行而同和，樂之情於是肇焉。則氣化之周流，與律呂之相生者同其機；太和之默運，與聲音之克諧者合其妙。是天地之仁，與聖人之樂，實一致也。仁不近於樂耶？義在天地，若與禮不相涉矣。然義以成物，而禮主於序，故秋冬之質具而異序，禮之制於是寓焉。則品彙之各成，猶夫節文度數之有章；大小之各正，猶夫尊
translation_en:
The virtues of Heaven and Earth are simply benevolence and righteousness. When measured against the rites and music of the sages, how could they be far apart? Rites and music were created by the sages, but their source lies in Heaven and Earth. Thus one must understand Heaven and Earth before one can establish rites and music. How can this be explained? Between Heaven and Earth, a single vital energy circulates, yet its functions differ through the four seasons. When yang holds sway, the myriad things spring forth in spring and grow in summer. As the principle of life gathers within them, the workings of transformation cannot cease of themselves; their unceasing nourishment manifests the interweaving of harmonious vital energies. Can this be called anything other than the benevolence of Heaven and Earth? When yin holds sway, the myriad things are gathered in autumn and stored away in winter. Once the generation of things is complete, the work of transformation must come to rest; as the severity of the cold intensifies, each returns to its own nature and allotted life. Can this be called anything other than the righteousness of Heaven and Earth?

Benevolence as it exists in Heaven and Earth might seem to have no connection with music. Yet benevolence generates things, and music centers upon harmony. Thus, as the vital energies of spring and summer move and bring all into shared harmony, the essential feeling of music originates therein. The circulation of transformation through vital energy shares its operative principle with the mutual generation of the yin and yang pitch standards; the silent workings of supreme harmony share their subtle efficacy with the concord of sounds. Thus the benevolence of Heaven and Earth and the music of the sages are truly one. Is benevolence not close to music? Righteousness as it exists in Heaven and Earth might seem to have no connection with rites. Yet righteousness brings things to completion, and rites center upon order. Thus, as the substantial forms of autumn and winter become complete and are ordered in their distinctions, the institutions of ritual are embodied therein. The completion of each category of things resembles the patterned arrangement of ritual forms, measures, and numbers; the proper disposition of the great and the small resembles that of the honored…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
卑貴賤之有等是天地之義與聖人之禮無二
理也義不近於禮耶夫以天地造化之妙爲聖
人制作之原如此自非達天德者其孰能知之
抑此自效法所本而言蓋聖人之禮樂與天地
相爲流通其始也法天地以爲禮樂旣則以禮
樂而賛天地卒之禮樂興而天地官矣是天地
者禮樂之本禮樂者天地之用聖人者又禮樂
之宗也然則天地設位而聖人成能聖人有功
於天地也大矣哉
===
溫良者仁之本也敬慎者仁之地也寬裕
者仁之作也孫接者仁之能也禮節者
仁之貌也言談者仁之文也歌樂者仁
之和也分散者仁之施也
李纘
考試官學正李批〔題八句相並作者難於措手惟此篇體裁獨異其錄以式〕
考試官教授向批〔錯綜成文而意致自明至發一言仁者〕
聖人舉眾善而歸之仁以見其道之大也蓋仁
punctuated:
卑貴賤之有等，是天地之義與聖人之禮無二理也。義不近於禮耶？夫以天地造化之妙爲聖人制作之原如此，自非達天德者，其孰能知之？抑此自效法所本而言，蓋聖人之禮樂與天地相爲流通，其始也法天地以爲禮樂，旣則以禮樂而賛天地，卒之禮樂興而天地官矣。是天地者禮樂之本，禮樂者天地之用，聖人者又禮樂之宗也。然則天地設位而聖人成能，聖人有功於天地也大矣哉！

溫良者仁之本也，敬慎者仁之地也，寬裕者仁之作也，孫接者仁之能也，禮節者仁之貌也，言談者仁之文也，歌樂者仁之和也，分散者仁之施也。

李纘

考試官學正李批〔題八句相並，作者難於措手，惟此篇體裁獨異，其錄以式。〕

考試官教授向批〔錯綜成文，而意致自明，至發一言仁者。〕

聖人舉眾善而歸之仁，以見其道之大也。蓋仁
translation_en:
…the lowly, the noble, and the base have their respective ranks. Thus the righteousness of Heaven and Earth and the ritual of the sages embody one and the same principle. Is righteousness not akin to ritual? Such is the way in which the wondrous creative transformations of Heaven and Earth provide the source for the sages’ institutions. Who could understand this without comprehending Heaven’s virtue? Yet this speaks only of the source they take as their model. The sages’ ritual and music interact freely with Heaven and Earth: at first, the sages model ritual and music upon Heaven and Earth; thereafter, through ritual and music, they assist Heaven and Earth; finally, when ritual and music flourish, Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices. Thus Heaven and Earth are the foundation of ritual and music; ritual and music are the functioning of Heaven and Earth; and the sages, in turn, are the guiding authority for ritual and music. Heaven and Earth therefore establish their positions, and the sages bring their capacities to fulfillment. Great indeed is the sages’ contribution to Heaven and Earth!

“Gentleness and goodness are the root of benevolence; reverence and caution are its ground; magnanimity is its expression in action; receiving others deferentially is its capacity; ritual observances are its outward appearance; speech and conversation are its refinement; singing and music are its harmony; distributing one’s possessions is its beneficent practice.”

Li Zuan

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: 〔The topic consists of eight juxtaposed sentences, making it difficult for a writer to know where to begin. This essay alone is distinctive in its structure; let it be recorded as a model.〕

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Prefectural School Professor: 〔The elements are interwoven into a composition whose meaning and purport are clear of themselves; “as for uttering a word on benevolence” [?].〕

The sage gathers the many forms of goodness and subsumes them under benevolence, thereby revealing the greatness of its Way. For benevolence …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
者體事而無不在者也善雖不同而何莫非仁
道之散殊哉夫子告哀公以儒行此則言其尊
讓也若曰仁之在人惟於善無不統故隨在而
可見今夫人之德曰溫良則和厚而易直也曰
敬慎則主一而寅畏也然溫良者德容之光發
於中純之懿是本之於仁也而敬慎則心存理
得推之踐履仁不有其地乎曰寬裕則廣大而
有容也曰孫接則退讓以明禮也然寬裕者無
我之公充其博愛之量是作之自仁也而孫接
===
則敦厚內崇謙光自著非仁之能事乎若夫禮
施諸身而品節不失貌可觀矣言出諸口而立
談有章文可聽矣而所以為是貌與文者非仁
耶蓋盛德之至則動容自中和順之積則英華
自發理有固然者也歌永其言而音比於樂聲
之和矣推己所有而分以與人物之施矣而所
以有是和與施者又非仁耶蓋欣喜之情暢而
託物以章惻怛之念勝而忘私以濟事有必至
者也由是觀之則善有不一而仁無不體其道
punctuated: 者，體事而無不在者也。善雖不同，而何莫非仁道之散殊哉？夫子告哀公以儒行，此則言其尊讓也。若曰：仁之在人，惟於善無不統，故隨在而可見。今夫人之德，曰溫良，則和厚而易直也；曰敬慎，則主一而寅畏也。然溫良者，德容之光，發於中純之懿，是本之於仁也。而敬慎，則心存理得，推之踐履，仁不有其地乎？曰寬裕，則廣大而有容也；曰孫接，則退讓以明禮也。然寬裕者，無我之公，充其博愛之量，是作之自仁也。而孫接，則敦厚內崇，謙光自著，非仁之能事乎？若夫禮施諸身而品節不失，貌可觀矣；言出諸口而立談有章，文可聽矣。而所以為是貌與文者，非仁耶？蓋盛德之至，則動容自中；和順之積，則英華自發，理有固然者也。歌永其言而音比於樂，聲之和矣；推己所有而分以與人，物之施矣。而所以有是和與施者，又非仁耶？蓋欣喜之情暢而託物以章，惻怛之念勝而忘私以濟，事有必至者也。由是觀之，則善有不一，而仁無不體，其道
translation_en: …is what gives substance to all affairs and is present everywhere. Though forms of goodness differ, how could any fail to be a distinct manifestation of the Way of benevolence? When the Master instructed Duke Ai concerning the conduct of the Confucian scholar, this passage addressed reverence and deference. It is as though he said: Benevolence in a person encompasses every form of goodness and thus can be seen wherever it is present. Now, among human virtues, warmth and goodness mean being harmonious, generous, amiable, and upright; reverence and caution mean maintaining singleness of purpose and respectful awe. Yet warmth and goodness are the radiance of virtuous bearing, issuing from the excellence of inner purity: this is to be rooted in benevolence. With reverence and caution, the mind is preserved and principle apprehended; when these are extended into practice, does benevolence not thereby have its ground? Magnanimity means breadth and capaciousness; humble engagement means yielding and deferring so as to make ritual propriety manifest. Yet magnanimity is the impartiality of selflessness, fulfilling one’s capacity for universal love: this is activity arising from benevolence. In humble engagement, sincerity and generosity are cultivated within, and the radiance of modesty naturally appears. Is this not what benevolence can accomplish? When ritual propriety is put into practice in one’s person without departing from its distinctions and measures, one’s bearing is worthy of observation. When words issue from one’s mouth and even spontaneous conversation has order, their refinement is worthy of a hearing. Is it not benevolence that makes such bearing and refinement possible? For when abundant virtue reaches its height, one’s movements and demeanor naturally accord with the proper measure; when harmony and compliance accumulate, their flowering naturally appears. This is inherent in principle. Singing prolongs one’s words, and tones accord with music: this is harmony in sound. Extending to others what one possesses, sharing it with them: this is the distribution of goods. And is it not again benevolence that makes such harmony and distribution possible? For feelings of joy flow freely and find expression through things; compassionate concern prevails, and one forgets private interests in bringing aid to others. These are inevitable outcomes in practice. Viewed in this light, goodness takes many forms, yet benevolence gives substance to them all; its Way…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
之大有如此聖人歷言儒行而終之以是焉有
以哉抑是數者雖皆仁道之所具而敬慎之德
則又爲爲仁之功蓋仁者人心也敬則心存心
存則理得由是而推之則無往而非仁道之流
通矣故言其德之所成則敬慎爲仁之地而本
其功之所始則敬慎爲仁之要也此又存仁者
所當知
第貳場
論
===
天地之所以爲大
李鳴金
同考試官教諭方 批 場中作者多以神化機立論惟
此篇不失中庸本旨宜冠多士
同考試官教諭夏 批 發明天地聖人之所以大道理明
白無駕空鑿虛之說自是真詮可式可式
考試官學正李 批 深得子思形容聖道之意而以
天地聖人歸之於誠尤見明理之學
考試官教授向 批 立論正大鋪敘有體
punctuated:
之大有如此！聖人歷言儒行，而終之以是焉，有以哉！抑是數者，雖皆仁道之所具，而敬慎之德，則又爲爲仁之功。蓋仁者，人心也。敬則心存，心存則理得。由是而推之，則無往而非仁道之流通矣。故言其德之所成，則敬慎爲仁之地；而本其功之所始，則敬慎爲仁之要也。此又存仁者所當知。
第貳場
論
天地之所以爲大
李鳴金
同考試官教諭方批：「場中作者多以神化機立論，惟此篇不失中庸本旨，宜冠多士。」
同考試官教諭夏批：「發明天地聖人之所以大，道理明白，無駕空鑿虛之說，自是真詮，可式可式。」
考試官學正李批：「深得子思形容聖道之意，而以天地聖人歸之於誠，尤見明理之學。」
考試官教授向批：「立論正大，鋪敘有體。」
translation_en:
…Such is the greatness of its Way! The sage enumerated the conduct of the learned and concluded with this for good reason! Yet although these several qualities all belong to the Way of benevolence, the virtue of reverence and caution also constitutes the work of practicing benevolence. For benevolence is the human heart. Through reverence the heart is preserved; when the heart is preserved, principle is apprehended. Extending this further, wherever one goes, the Way of benevolence flows freely. Thus, speaking of what brings this virtue to completion, reverence and caution are the ground of benevolence; tracing the work back to its beginning, reverence and caution are the essentials of benevolence. This too is something those who preserve benevolence should understand.
Second Session
Discourse
What Makes Heaven and Earth Great
Li Mingjin
Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor, comments: “Most writers in this examination based their arguments on the workings of numinous transformation. This essay alone preserves the fundamental purport of the Doctrine of the Mean and deserves to rank first among the candidates.”
Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor, comments: “It elucidates what makes Heaven, Earth, and the sage great. Its reasoning is clear, with no assertions built on empty speculation. This is indeed a true interpretation, worthy of emulation, worthy of emulation!”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It deeply grasps Zisi’s intention in describing the Way of the sage. By tracing Heaven, Earth, and the sage alike to sincerity, it particularly demonstrates learning that comprehends principle.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “The argument is upright and grand; its exposition is well structured.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
論曰聖人之大也大於道觀諸天地而可見矣
夫道生天地天地生聖人天地道中之一物而
聖人又天地中之一物耳以形觀形則天地之
物有大於聖人者而況天地之不相侔乎以道
觀道則維天之命與聖人之性一也在天地者
非有餘在聖人者非不足聖人蓋有心之天地
而天地乃無心之聖人其道同則其所以爲大
亦同而未可以殊論也故曰觀乎天地則見聖
人昔者孔子生於周末蓋春秋之聖人也而前
===
乎孔子有文武前乎文武有堯舜皆聖也而其
稱堯舜者曰精一執中啟千聖之傳也稱文武
者曰謨訓功烈備一代之法也道行於上而德
業光矣孔子窮而在下無位與時有周公之志
而不得行而徒發之於言曰吾學周禮今用之
吾從周他日又舉文武之政以告魯哀公而九
經之陳無慮數百言至其皇皇列國而終不得
行也乃以其道告諸門人曾子曰吾道一以貫
之後之論孔子者遂謂其宗堯舜之道而守文
punctuated:
論曰：聖人之大也，大於道，觀諸天地而可見矣。夫道生天地，天地生聖人。天地，道中之一物，而聖人又天地中之一物耳。以形觀形，則天地之物有大於聖人者，而況天地之不相侔乎？以道觀道，則維天之命與聖人之性一也。在天地者非有餘，在聖人者非不足。聖人蓋有心之天地，而天地乃無心之聖人。其道同，則其所以爲大亦同，而未可以殊論也。故曰：觀乎天地，則見聖人。
昔者孔子生於周末，蓋春秋之聖人也。而前乎孔子有文武，前乎文武有堯舜，皆聖也。而其稱堯舜者曰：精一執中，啟千聖之傳也。稱文武者曰：謨訓功烈，備一代之法也。道行於上，而德業光矣。孔子窮而在下，無位與時，有周公之志而不得行，而徒發之於言，曰：「吾學周禮，今用之，吾從周。」他日又舉文武之政以告魯哀公，而九經之陳，無慮數百言。至其皇皇列國而終不得行也，乃以其道告諸門人曾子，曰：「吾道一以貫之。」後之論孔子者，遂謂其宗堯舜之道而守文
translation_en:
The discourse states: The sage’s greatness lies in the Way; this can be seen by contemplating Heaven and Earth. The Way gives birth to Heaven and Earth, and Heaven and Earth give birth to the sage. Heaven and Earth are but one entity within the Way, and the sage, in turn, is but one entity within Heaven and Earth. Judging physical forms by physical form, there are things within Heaven and Earth larger than the sage; how much less can his size match Heaven and Earth themselves? Judging the Way by the Way, however, Heaven’s mandate and the sage’s nature are one. What is present in Heaven and Earth is no greater, and what is present in the sage is no less. The sage is Heaven and Earth endowed with a mind; Heaven and Earth are a sage without a mind. Their Way is the same, and so is that which makes them great: they cannot be judged differently. Thus it is said: contemplate Heaven and Earth, and you will see the sage.
Long ago, Kongzi was born toward the end of the Zhou: he was the sage of the Spring and Autumn period. Before Kongzi there were Wen and Wu, and before Wen and Wu there were Yao and Shun—all were sages. Those who praise Yao and Shun say that, through refinement and singleness of mind and holding fast to the Mean, they inaugurated the transmission through a thousand sages. Those who praise Wen and Wu say that their counsels, instructions, achievements, and glorious deeds provided a complete model for a dynasty. The Way was practiced by those above, and their virtue and accomplishments shone forth. Kongzi, frustrated and in a lowly station, had neither the position nor the opportunity. He possessed the aspirations of the Duke of Zhou but could not put them into practice, and could only express them in words, saying: “I have studied the rites of Zhou; if they are to be employed today, I follow Zhou.” On another occasion, he explained the government of Wen and Wu to Duke Ai of Lu, setting forth the nine guiding principles in several hundred words. Yet, after his restless travels among the states, he was ultimately unable to put his Way into practice. He therefore conveyed it to his disciple Zengzi, saying: “My Way is threaded together by one principle.” Those who later discussed Kongzi consequently said that he took the Way of Yao and Shun as his guiding source and upheld the model of Wen…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
武之法夫堯舜以帝文武以王而豈於孔子若
是班乎噫此蓋以道言也論事功則孔子不如
堯舜文武之達而顯論道德則堯舜之道文武
之法孔子實備之是惟無用用則舉而措之而
方且以其所宗所守於堯舜文武者述之六經
告之天下後世使其道其法愈久而愈光而萬
世之言學者無異術論治者無異政夷考其行
仕止久速與時偕行隨寓而安居易俟命雖堯
舜文武亦不是過而天地之理且不能違焉嗚
===
呼其為道大矣子貢宰我見其道而言曰仲尼
日月也曰夫子賢於堯舜天下之人皆韙其言
而子思猶以為未足曰是天地之大也今夫天
位乎上地位乎下四時之錯行而寒暑迭運也
日月之代明而晝夜相禪也萬物之飛潛動植
並育於其間而不相侵害也夫何以能然也蓋
陰陽之散殊而性命之各正春夏秋冬各一其
氣日往月來各一其度飛潛動植各一其性不
相假借不相凌奪譬之川焉支分派別各異其
punctuated: 武之法。夫堯舜以帝，文武以王，而豈於孔子若是班乎？噫！此蓋以道言也。論事功，則孔子不如堯舜文武之達而顯；論道德，則堯舜之道、文武之法，孔子實備之。是惟無用，用則舉而措之。而方且以其所宗所守於堯舜文武者，述之六經，告之天下後世，使其道其法愈久而愈光，而萬世之言學者無異術，論治者無異政。夷考其行，仕止久速，與時偕行；隨寓而安，居易俟命。雖堯舜文武，亦不是過，而天地之理且不能違焉。嗚呼！其為道大矣！子貢、宰我見其道而言，曰：「仲尼日月也。」曰：「夫子賢於堯舜。」天下之人皆韙其言，而子思猶以為未足，曰：「是天地之大也。」今夫天位乎上，地位乎下，四時之錯行而寒暑迭運也，日月之代明而晝夜相禪也，萬物之飛潛動植並育於其間而不相侵害也，夫何以能然也？蓋陰陽之散殊，而性命之各正，春夏秋冬各一其氣，日往月來各一其度，飛潛動植各一其性，不相假借，不相凌奪。譬之川焉，支分派別，各異其
translation_en: …the laws of King Wu. Yao and Shun were emperors, and Wen and Wu were kings: how could they be ranked alongside Confucius in this way? Ah! This is surely speaking in terms of the Way. In practical achievements, Confucius did not attain the eminence and manifest success of Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu. In the Way and virtue, however, Confucius fully possessed the Way of Yao and Shun and the laws of Wen and Wu. He merely lacked an opportunity to put them into practice; given that opportunity, he would have implemented them. Moreover, he set forth in the Six Classics what he revered and upheld from Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu, transmitting it to the world and to later generations. Thus their Way and laws grew ever more illustrious with time, so that through all ages those who discussed learning would follow no divergent methods, and those who discussed government would advocate no divergent policies. Examining his conduct impartially, whether he entered office or withdrew, remained long or departed quickly, he acted in accord with the times. Wherever he found himself, he was at peace, dwelling in ease and awaiting Heaven’s mandate. Even Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu did not surpass this, and even the principles of Heaven and Earth could not run counter to it. Ah, how great was his Way! Zigong and Zai Wo perceived his Way and said, respectively, “Zhongni is the sun and moon,” and “Our Master surpasses Yao and Shun in worth.” All the world approved their words, yet Zisi still considered them insufficient, saying, “This is the greatness of Heaven and Earth.” Now Heaven occupies its place above and Earth its place below. The four seasons proceed in succession, cold and heat alternating; the sun and moon take turns shining, day and night succeeding one another; and all creatures that fly or swim, move or take root, grow together between them without harming one another. How is this possible? It is because yin and yang disperse into distinct forms, and each being’s nature and allotted destiny are duly established. Spring, summer, autumn, and winter each have their own vital energy; the departing sun and returning moon each have their own measure; and creatures that fly or swim, move or take root, each have their own nature. They neither borrow from one another nor encroach upon or dispossess one another. Compare this to rivers: their branches divide into distinct streams, each differing in its…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
流而逝者不息是天地之小德也而其所以錯
行所以代明所以並育者夫孰主張綱維之蓋
渾淪磅礴之中而有合一不測之神動靜闔闢
互爲其根由是而萬化出焉寒暑本之以成四
時日月本之以成晝夜萬物本之以爲性命敦
厚博大其出無窮是天地之大德也夫存之有
神而化之不可窮此天地之所以爲大也不然
則形聲色象何所稟命以顯其仁而歸根復命
何所主宰以藏其用造化之運有時而窮而天
===
地何以成其大乎知天地則可以知聖人矣夫
堯舜也文武也道之至也法之備也天時也水
土也運之自然也理之一定也孔子以一人之
身語道而道存語法而法守上同其運下因其
理可以堯舜而帝可以文武而王可以四時而
運而用舍行藏各惟其時可以列國而居而逢
掖章甫各適其俗以至富貴貧賤夷狄患難之
處無所不可而文之以易詩書春秋禮樂之經
存之於君臣父子兄弟夫婦朋友之倫而達之
punctuated: 流，而逝者不息，是天地之小德也。而其所以錯行、所以代明、所以並育者，夫孰主張綱維之？蓋渾淪磅礴之中，而有合一不測之神，動靜闔闢，互爲其根，由是而萬化出焉。寒暑本之以成四時，日月本之以成晝夜，萬物本之以爲性命，敦厚博大，其出無窮，是天地之大德也。夫存之有神，而化之不可窮，此天地之所以爲大也。不然，則形聲色象何所稟命以顯其仁，而歸根復命何所主宰以藏其用？造化之運有時而窮，而天地何以成其大乎？知天地，則可以知聖人矣。夫堯舜也，文武也，道之至也，法之備也；天時也，水土也，運之自然也，理之一定也。孔子以一人之身，語道而道存，語法而法守，上同其運，下因其理。可以堯舜而帝，可以文武而王，可以四時而運，而用舍行藏各惟其時；可以列國而居，而逢掖章甫各適其俗。以至富貴貧賤、夷狄患難之處，無所不可，而文之以《易》《詩》《書》《春秋》《禮》《樂》之經，存之於君臣父子兄弟夫婦朋友之倫，而達之
translation_en:
…their streams, flowing onward without cease: these are the lesser virtues of Heaven and Earth. Yet what governs and holds together their alternating courses, their successive illumination, and their nurturing of all things together? Within their undivided, all-encompassing immensity there is a unified and unfathomable spiritual efficacy. Movement and stillness, closing and opening, are each the root of the other; from these emerge the myriad transformations. Cold and heat draw upon this to constitute the four seasons; sun and moon draw upon it to constitute day and night; the myriad things draw upon it for their natures and allotted lives. Profound and substantial, broad and great, it brings forth without end: this is the great virtue of Heaven and Earth. What abides within them possesses spiritual efficacy, and their transforming activity cannot be exhausted: this is what makes Heaven and Earth great. Otherwise, from what would forms, sounds, colors, and appearances receive their mandate so as to manifest their benevolence? And what would govern their returning to the root and reverting to their mandate so as to store away their efficacy? If the workings of creation and transformation should at some point be exhausted, how could Heaven and Earth attain their greatness?

Knowing Heaven and Earth, one can then know the sage. Yao and Shun, Wen and Wu represent the utmost realization of the Way and the full provision of models. The seasons of Heaven and the waters and soils represent the natural course of things and the settled determination of principle. Kongzi, in his single person, embodied the Way when one spoke of the Way, and upheld the models when one spoke of models. Above, he accorded with Heaven’s operations; below, he followed Earth’s principles. He could act as emperor like Yao and Shun, or as king like Wen and Wu. He could move with the four seasons, his employment or dismissal, his public service or withdrawal, each fitting its time. He could dwell in the various states, his broad-sleeved robes and zhangfu cap each suited to local custom. Even in wealth and honor, poverty and low station, among the Yi and Di peoples, or amid adversity and hardship, there was no situation in which he could not act fittingly. He gave this patterned expression through the classics—the Changes, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites, and Music—preserved it in the relationships between ruler and minister, father and son, elder and younger brothers, husband and wife, and friends, and extended it to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
於動靜語默飮食起居之常無不各當其理燦
然萬善之咸備也而求其道則惟曰一以貫之
嗚呼此孔子之所以爲大也夫其萬善之咸備
也是小德之川流也其一以貫之也是大德之
敦化也其大不同其所以爲大者無不同求之
聖人而天地之道可見觀於天地而聖人之道
益明矣子思子其善言聖道者歟然非惟子思
言之也昔之賛堯舜者曰蕩蕩如天曰帝德廣
運賛文武者曰光于四方曰冒之如天則堯舜
===
文武之道皆天也而皆統之於夫子然則明夫
子之道信非天地不足以擬諸其形容矣雖然
子思之言其於道亦有指乎嘗觀其論至誠功
業而曰博厚配地高明配天悠久無疆而歸之
於文王之德之純至論天地之道則曰可一言
而盡其爲物不貳則其生物不測嗚呼此子思
之所以傳孔子之道者乎夫天地之不貳誠也
文王之純與堯舜之中孔子之一皆是物也天
以誠而運於穆之命聖人以誠而乆化成之道
punctuated:
於動靜語默、飮食起居之常，無不各當其理，燦然萬善之咸備也。而求其道，則惟曰：「一以貫之。」嗚呼！此孔子之所以爲大也。夫其萬善之咸備也，是小德之川流也；其一以貫之也，是大德之敦化也。其大不同，其所以爲大者無不同。求之聖人，而天地之道可見；觀於天地，而聖人之道益明矣。子思子其善言聖道者歟！然非惟子思言之也。昔之賛堯舜者曰：「蕩蕩如天。」曰：「帝德廣運。」賛文武者曰：「光于四方。」曰：「冒之如天。」則堯舜文武之道皆天也，而皆統之於夫子。然則明夫子之道，信非天地不足以擬諸其形容矣。

雖然，子思之言，其於道亦有指乎？嘗觀其論至誠功業，而曰：「博厚配地，高明配天，悠久無疆。」而歸之於文王之德之純。至論天地之道，則曰：「可一言而盡，其爲物不貳，則其生物不測。」嗚呼！此子思之所以傳孔子之道者乎！夫天地之不貳，誠也。文王之純，與堯舜之中、孔子之一，皆是物也。天以誠而運於穆之命，聖人以誠而乆化成之道，
translation_en:
…to the everyday activities of movement and stillness, speech and silence, eating and drinking, rising and resting: everything accords with its proper principle, and all goodness is brilliantly complete. Yet, when we seek the Way underlying this, he says only: “A single thread runs through it.” Ah! This is what makes Confucius great. His complete possession of all goodness is the flowing of lesser virtues like rivers; the single thread running through it is the abundant transforming power of the greater virtue. Their forms of greatness differ, but what makes them great is in every case the same. Seek it in the sage, and the Way of Heaven and Earth becomes visible; contemplate Heaven and Earth, and the sage’s Way becomes still clearer. Was Master Zisi not skilled at speaking of the sagely Way! Yet Zisi was not alone in saying this. Those who formerly praised Yao and Shun said, “Vast as Heaven,” and “The emperor’s virtue is far-reaching and all-embracing.” Those who praised Kings Wen and Wu said, “Its light reaches the four quarters,” and “He covers them like Heaven.” Thus the Ways of Yao, Shun, Wen, and Wu are all Heaven’s Way, and all are brought together in the Master. To elucidate the Master’s Way, then, surely nothing short of Heaven and Earth suffices as a comparison by which to describe it.

Nevertheless, do Zisi’s words also point to something specific concerning the Way? Consider his discussion of the achievements of utmost sincerity: “Broad and thick, it matches Earth; lofty and luminous, it matches Heaven; enduring, it is without bounds.” He attributes this to the purity of King Wen’s virtue. When discussing the Way of Heaven and Earth, he says: “It can be exhausted in a single statement: as a thing, it is undivided; thus its generation of things is unfathomable.” Ah! Is this not how Zisi transmitted Confucius’s Way? The undividedness of Heaven and Earth is sincerity. King Wen’s purity, the centrality of Yao and Shun, and the oneness of Confucius are all this same thing. Through sincerity, Heaven carries forward its profound mandate; through sincerity, the sage perpetuates the Way of transforming and bringing to completion…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
其道同故其功同而天地之所不能爲者且有
待於聖人之裁成輔相者矣故曰至誠與天地
參然則求聖人之道者宜何如子思固言之矣
曰誠者天之道也誠之者人之道也誠者聖人
之事而誠之者學者之功
表
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士
謝表〔景德二年〕
黃廷楫
===
同考試官敎諭陳批題本平正作亦稱之蓋工
於四六者
同考試官敎諭邵批忠愛之心溢於言表非苟作者
考試官學正李批對君之言自應如此
考試官敎授向批典則
景德二年某月日伏蒙
聖恩以臣億爲翰林學士謹奉表稱
謝者
西掖承恩清切紫薇之署北門待詔榮登白
punctuated:
其道同，故其功同，而天地之所不能爲者，且有待於聖人之裁成輔相者矣。故曰：「至誠與天地參。」然則求聖人之道者宜何如？子思固言之矣，曰：「誠者，天之道也；誠之者，人之道也。」誠者，聖人之事，而誠之者，學者之功。
表
擬宋以楊億爲翰林學士謝表〔景德二年〕
黃廷楫
同考試官敎諭陳批：「題本平正，作亦稱之，蓋工於四六者。」
同考試官敎諭邵批：「忠愛之心溢於言表，非苟作者。」
考試官學正李批：「對君之言，自應如此。」
考試官敎授向批：「典則。」
景德二年某月日，伏蒙聖恩，以臣億爲翰林學士，謹奉表稱謝者。
西掖承恩，清切紫薇之署；北門待詔，榮登白
translation_en:
…Their Way is the same, and so their achievements are the same. Even what Heaven and Earth cannot accomplish must await the sage’s work of ordering and assisting their operations. Thus it is said: “Utmost sincerity forms a triad with Heaven and Earth.” How, then, should those who seek the Way of the sage proceed? Zisi has already explained it: “Sincerity is the Way of Heaven; making oneself sincere is the Way of humankind.” Sincerity is the state of the sage; making oneself sincere is the work of the learner.
Memorial
A memorial of thanks composed in the person of Yang Yi upon his appointment as Hanlin Academician under the Song dynasty. 〔Second year of Jingde [1005]〕
Huang Tingji
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The topic is straightforward and balanced, and the composition matches it. This is evidently the work of someone skilled in four-and-six parallel prose.”
Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor, comments: “A heart of loyalty and devotion overflows beyond the words. This is no carelessly composed work.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Words addressed to one’s sovereign should indeed be like this.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “Classical and well regulated.”
On an unspecified day and month in the second year of Jingde, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment of me, your servant Yi, as Hanlin Academician. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks.
In the Western Side Chamber I receive your favor, serving in the pure and intimate precincts of the Purple Myrtle office; at the Northern Gate I await your commands, gloriously ascending the white …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
玉之堂寵溢分涯恩生望外臣億誠惶誠
恐稽首頓首上言伏以
聖世右文式謹論思之地
明王宅俊爰崇密勿之司故自漢有代言之官
而歷代重儒臣之選弘文新啓榮擬登瀛
供奉載更親稱內相洎於
今日尤重詞科
紫禁宣麻木鳳高翔於雲路
黃扉視草銅螭對立於瓊庭通
===
金殿之爐香地鄰閶闔掌
玉皇之案箓境入蓬壺宜處宿儒以光清秩臣
億草茅賤品樗櫟散材幼稟顓蒙忽悟登
樓之咏長通章句偶叨上第之榮故嘗搴
中葉之詞林酌前脩之筆海西崑體變妄
希刻鵠之能朔漠名傳慚竊雕蟲之技豈
期膚末謬辱甄收玆蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
堯文丕煥
punctuated: 玉之堂，寵溢分涯，恩生望外。臣億誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首上言：伏以聖世右文，式謹論思之地；明王宅俊，爰崇密勿之司。故自漢有代言之官，而歷代重儒臣之選。弘文新啓，榮擬登瀛；供奉載更，親稱內相。洎於今日，尤重詞科。紫禁宣麻，木鳳高翔於雲路；黃扉視草，銅螭對立於瓊庭。通金殿之爐香，地鄰閶闔；掌玉皇之案箓，境入蓬壺。宜處宿儒，以光清秩。臣億草茅賤品，樗櫟散材。幼稟顓蒙，忽悟登樓之咏；長通章句，偶叨上第之榮。故嘗搴中葉之詞林，酌前脩之筆海。西崑體變，妄希刻鵠之能；朔漠名傳，慚竊雕蟲之技。豈期膚末，謬辱甄收。玆蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，堯文丕煥，
translation_en:
…the Hall of White Jade. Favor exceeds my allotted station; grace comes beyond my hopes. Your servant Yi, truly trembling and fearful, bows his head to the ground and submits these words:
I humbly reflect that a sage age honors letters and duly safeguards the place for deliberation and reflection; an enlightened sovereign gives worthy men their proper stations and exalts the office of confidential service. Thus, from the Han onward, there have been officials who speak on the ruler’s behalf, and successive dynasties have attached great importance to selecting scholarly ministers. When the Institute for the Advancement of Literature first opened, the honor was likened to ascending the immortal isle of Yingzhou; when the designation of those in attendance was subsequently changed, they were affectionately called “inner chief ministers.” Down to the present day, particular importance has been attached to literary appointments. Within the Purple Forbidden Palace, appointments are proclaimed from hemp-paper edicts, and the wooden phoenix soars high along the cloudy way; behind the yellow doors, drafts are reviewed, and bronze hornless dragons stand facing one another in the jade court. Incense from the burners of the golden hall reaches this place, which adjoins the gates of Heaven; to manage the Jade Emperor’s documents and registers is to enter the realm of the immortals’ isle of Penghu. Seasoned scholars should occupy these posts, lending luster to their pure and distinguished rank.
Your servant Yi is of humble rustic stock, useless timber like the ailanthus and the oak. In childhood I was endowed with dullness and ignorance, yet suddenly grasped the meaning of the verse on ascending a tower; when grown, I became conversant with textual interpretation and happened to receive the honor of a high examination placing. Thus I have gathered blossoms from the literary groves of the middle period and drawn from the ocean of my predecessors’ writings. As the Xikun style changed, I presumptuously hoped for the skill to carve a swan; as my name spread to the northern deserts, I felt ashamed of having appropriated the petty craft of carving insects. How could I have expected that my shallow accomplishments would mistakenly receive the favor of selection? This is surely because I have humbly encountered 〇〇〇〇, whose Yao-like literary brilliance shines magnificently…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
舜哲重華
象日月以嚮明
配乾坤而立極禮隆
宗廟孝洽
慈闈
鑾輿親幸乎尼丘四海被崇文之化
玉節遙臨於澶水萬方賴偃武之休仰
峻德以難名歌太平而有象謂翰苑之設最爲
貴近之階而學士之名尤出朝紳之右眷
茲重寄猥及凡庸戴德難勝撫躬知愧臣
億敢不殫心論述畢力校讎惟三謨二典
之上陳豈八索九丘之徒博叩
鑾坡而奏記遠希陸贄之忠處
鳳掖以敷言近效竇儀之直伏願
聖敬日躋丕懋緝熈之學
皇仁天覆式符光被之勳文運與
國運俱昌世道與
君道並泰臣億無任瞻
punctuated: 舜哲重華，象日月以嚮明，配乾坤而立極。禮隆宗廟，孝洽慈闈。鑾輿親幸乎尼丘，四海被崇文之化；玉節遙臨於澶水，萬方賴偃武之休。仰峻德以難名，歌太平而有象。謂翰苑之設，最爲貴近之階；而學士之名，尤出朝紳之右。眷茲重寄，猥及凡庸。戴德難勝，撫躬知愧。臣億敢不殫心論述，畢力校讎？惟三謨二典之上陳，豈八索九丘之徒博？叩鑾坡而奏記，遠希陸贄之忠；處鳳掖以敷言，近效竇儀之直。伏願聖敬日躋，丕懋緝熈之學；皇仁天覆，式符光被之勳。文運與國運俱昌，世道與君道並泰。臣億無任瞻
translation_en: …Your sagacity, like Shun’s, renews his splendor. You emulate the sun and moon in turning toward the light, and match Heaven and Earth in establishing the supreme standard. Your rites exalt the ancestral temples; your filial devotion pervades the quarters of the imperial mother. Your imperial carriage personally visited Niqiu, and all within the Four Seas received the transforming influence of your esteem for letters. Your jade tally of authority reached the distant waters of Chan, and the myriad regions benefited from the blessings of laying arms to rest. Looking up to your lofty virtue, we find it beyond naming; singing of the Great Peace, we find its manifestations tangible. You consider service in the Hanlin Academy the foremost avenue to honored proximity to the throne, and the title of Academician especially preeminent among court officials. In your regard for this weighty charge, you have condescended to entrust it to one so ordinary. Overwhelmed by gratitude for your favor, I reflect upon myself and know shame. How could your servant Yi fail to devote his whole heart to exposition and composition, and all his strength to collation? I would lay before Your Majesty the Three Counsels and Two Canons; how could I seek merely the broad learning of the Eight Cords and Nine Mounds? Presenting written submissions at the Hanlin Academy, I would aspire to the loyalty of Lu Zhi of earlier times; setting forth my words within the palace precincts, I would emulate the uprightness of Dou Yi of more recent times. I humbly wish that your sagely reverence may increase daily, and that you may greatly advance your pursuit of ever-brighter learning; that your imperial benevolence may shelter all like Heaven, fulfilling the achievement of spreading radiance everywhere. May the fortunes of letters and of the state flourish together, and may the ways of the age and of the sovereign alike enjoy peace. Your servant Yi cannot contain his feelings as he gazes upward…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁塲
策
第一問
周欽
===
同考試官教諭邵批我
皇上妙契
皇祖同符往聖心法之傳模寫近似蓋涵泳
聖訓而知所會歸者
同考試官教諭陳批兩引
聖諭以明
聖製體認親切足徵心得
考試官學正李批敷敘詳整篇末能言我
皇祖
punctuated:
天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁塲
策
第一問
周欽

同考試官教諭邵批：我皇上妙契皇祖，同符往聖，心法之傳，模寫近似。蓋涵泳聖訓而知所會歸者。

同考試官教諭陳批：兩引聖諭以明聖製，體認親切，足徵心得。

考試官學正李批：敷敘詳整，篇末能言我皇祖
translation_en:
…Heaven and look up reverently to Your Majesty, with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essay
First Question
Zhou Qin

Comment by Associate Examiner Shao, Instructor: The essay closely portrays the transmission of the learning of the mind, through which our August Emperor accords profoundly with the Imperial Ancestor and shares the same principles as the sages of old. Its author has evidently steeped himself in the imperial teachings and understood their unifying purport.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Twice quoting imperial instructions to elucidate the imperially composed text, the essay shows an intimate understanding, sufficient to demonstrate the author’s personal insight.

Comment by Examiner Li, School Director: The exposition is detailed and well ordered. At the end of the essay, the author succeeds in describing our Imperial Ancestor…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上盛美之實尤見委曲
考試官敎授向批紀實而有據頌
美而不諛可以爲多士式矣
帝王之治本於道帝王之道本於心夫其
本於道也則政不必同而同于治夫其本
於心也則治不必同而同于道得其心則
政與治有可得而言者矣執事發策而以
我
太祖高皇帝我
===
皇上政治心法之蘊下詢承學夫頌
聖德而彰其美載
國實而揚其休非鴻筆之儒不能也愚也何
足以知之孔子曰大哉堯之爲君也蕩蕩
乎民無能名君哉舜也巍巍乎有天下而
不與然巍乎成功煥乎文章而光天之下
洽于民心者自不可掩故睹其巍然煥然
而蕩蕩者彷佛而可名卽其光之所洽而
巍巍者庶幾乎可得何者藏諸用者難窺
punctuated:
皇上盛美之實，尤見委曲。
考試官敎授向批：紀實而有據，頌美而不諛，可以爲多士式矣。
帝王之治本於道，帝王之道本於心。夫其本於道也，則政不必同而同于治；夫其本於心也，則治不必同而同于道。得其心，則政與治有可得而言者矣。執事發策，而以我太祖高皇帝、我皇上政治心法之蘊下詢承學。夫頌聖德而彰其美，載國實而揚其休，非鴻筆之儒不能也。愚也何足以知之？孔子曰：「大哉，堯之爲君也！蕩蕩乎，民無能名。」「君哉，舜也！巍巍乎，有天下而不與。」然巍乎成功，煥乎文章，而光天之下、洽于民心者，自不可掩。故睹其巍然煥然而蕩蕩者，彷佛而可名；卽其光之所洽而巍巍者，庶幾乎可得。何者？藏諸用者難窺
translation_en:
…the actual grandeur and excellence of His Majesty, displaying particularly attentive treatment of their subtleties.
Examiner Xiang, a Professor, comments: “The account records facts and has supporting evidence; it praises excellence without flattery. It can serve as a model for the many candidates.”
The governance of emperors and kings is rooted in the Way; the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the mind. Because their governance is rooted in the Way, their policies need not be identical, yet they converge in good order. Because their Way is rooted in the mind, their forms of governance need not be identical, yet they converge in the Way. Once one grasps that mind, their policies and governance become accessible to discussion. You, honoured examiners, have issued a policy question, condescending to ask us students about the profound principles of government and the method of cultivating the mind embodied by our Emperor Taizu Gao and our present sovereign. To extol sagely virtue and manifest its beauty, to record the facts of the dynasty and proclaim its glory—these are things only a scholar of commanding literary talent can accomplish. How could someone as ignorant as I understand them adequately? Confucius said: “Great indeed was Yao as a ruler! So vast was he that the people could find no name for him.” And: “What a ruler Shun was! How lofty! He possessed all under Heaven, yet took no part in it.” Nevertheless, lofty achievements and splendid cultural forms, whose radiance shines throughout the world and whose influence permeates the people's hearts, cannot remain concealed. Thus, by observing their loftiness, splendour, and vastness, one may form an approximate conception and give them a name; by following the reach of their radiance, one may perhaps apprehend their loftiness. Why is this? What is concealed in its operation is difficult to discern…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
而顯諸仁者可測也知此庶有以復執事
之明問矣夫唐虞之際治出於一而政敎
無二致三代而下治出於二而政敎爲兩
途故考象授時明刑降典政也亦敎也危
微精一允執厥中敎也亦政也是故黎民
於變人知堯之放勳矣然欽明文思允恭
克讓者實有以爲化裁之原四方風動人
知舜之協于帝矣然濬哲文明溫恭允塞
者實有以爲運用之本執事所謂推行有
===
自而功化之極不待外求豈不信哉我
太祖高皇帝
聖德
神功度越百世
洪謨
大訓垂範萬年漸被之餘蓋嘗莊誦
聖政記及
大明日曆而仰測高深竊窺涯涘雖
天府之藏難悉而儒臣之傳習見而竊伏歎我
punctuated:
而顯諸仁者可測也。知此，庶有以復執事之明問矣。夫唐虞之際，治出於一，而政敎無二致；三代而下，治出於二，而政敎爲兩途。故考象授時、明刑降典，政也，亦敎也；危微精一、允執厥中，敎也，亦政也。是故黎民於變，人知堯之放勳矣；然欽明文思、允恭克讓者，實有以爲化裁之原。四方風動，人知舜之協于帝矣；然濬哲文明、溫恭允塞者，實有以爲運用之本。執事所謂推行有自，而功化之極不待外求，豈不信哉？
我太祖高皇帝，聖德神功，度越百世；洪謨大訓，垂範萬年。漸被之餘，蓋嘗莊誦《聖政記》及《大明日曆》，而仰測高深，竊窺涯涘。雖天府之藏難悉，而儒臣之傳，習見而竊伏歎我
translation_en:
…yet what is manifested in benevolence can be discerned. Understanding this, I may perhaps offer a reply to your discerning question. In the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, governance issued from a single source, and administration and moral instruction had no divergent aims. From the Three Dynasties onward, governance issued from two sources, and administration and moral instruction took separate paths. Thus, examining celestial phenomena and communicating the seasons, clarifying punishments and promulgating statutes, were administration, but also moral instruction. Recognizing the perilousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the mind of the Way, being discerning and single-minded, and faithfully holding to the mean were moral instruction, but also administration. Hence, when the common people were transformed, people recognized Yao’s vast achievement; yet it was his reverence, intelligence, refinement, and thoughtfulness, his genuine respectfulness and capacity for deference, that truly supplied the source of his transforming and shaping influence. When the four quarters responded as grass bends before the wind, people recognized that Shun accorded with the emperor Yao; yet it was his profound wisdom and luminous refinement, his gentleness, respectfulness, and sincerity, that truly supplied the basis of his practical conduct. You have said that the implementation of governance has its source, and that the highest achievements of moral transformation need not be sought outside it. Is this not indeed true?
Our Emperor Taizu Gao’s sagely virtue and divine achievements surpassed a hundred generations; his grand plans and great instructions established models for ten thousand years. Having received their pervasive influence, I have reverently recited the Record of Sagely Governance (Shengzheng ji) and the Daily Record of the Great Ming (Da Ming rili), looking upward to gauge their height and depth and venturing to glimpse their bounds. Although it is difficult to know fully what is held in the imperial repositories, I have frequently encountered the accounts transmitted by Confucian officials and have humbly marveled at our…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之心即堯舜之心也是故
諭輔臣有曰心為身之主若一事不合理則
百事皆廢所以常自檢點此心與身如兩
敵然而觀無逸則曰人君之心當存兢惕
其論治道曰大學一書其要只在脩身又
曰防閑此身使不妄動則信已能若防閑
此心使不妄動尚難能也盖其體道之誠
如有求而不得而謙虛之至雖已能而不
居考之精一之義不謀而同稽於兢業之
===
心不期而合矣是故奄有萬方取中國既
淪之境土毆除北狄復中國既墬之衣冠
而又身致太平坐收成績功昭天地而山
川鬼神效順不違化被蠻夷而奉幣獻琛
歸命恐後人徒見功烈之盛而豈知根於
聖心之兢惕哉故觀於
聖諭有曰人君一心治化之本存於中者無堯
舜之心而欲施於政者有堯舜之治必不
可得有可見矣我
punctuated: 聖祖之心，即堯舜之心也。是故諭輔臣有曰：「心為身之主，若一事不合理，則百事皆廢。所以常自檢點，此心與身如兩敵然。」而觀《無逸》，則曰：「人君之心當存兢惕。」其論治道曰：「《大學》一書，其要只在脩身。」又曰：「防閑此身，使不妄動，則信已能；若防閑此心，使不妄動，尚難能也。」盖其體道之誠，如有求而不得；而謙虛之至，雖已能而不居。考之精一之義，不謀而同；稽於兢業之心，不期而合矣。是故奄有萬方，取中國既淪之境土，毆除北狄，復中國既墬之衣冠，而又身致太平，坐收成績。功昭天地，而山川鬼神效順不違；化被蠻夷，而奉幣獻琛，歸命恐後。人徒見功烈之盛，而豈知根於聖心之兢惕哉？故觀於聖諭，有曰：「人君一心，治化之本。存於中者無堯舜之心，而欲施於政者有堯舜之治，必不可得。」有可見矣。我
translation_en:
…the mind of our sagely progenitor was the very mind of Yao and Shun. Thus, in instructing his assisting ministers, he said: “The mind is the master of the person. If even one matter fails to accord with principle, all affairs fall into ruin. Therefore I constantly examine myself, with this mind and person confronting one another like two adversaries.” On reading “Against Ease” (Wu yi), he said: “A ruler’s mind must remain apprehensive and vigilant.” Discussing the Way of government, he said: “The essential point of the Great Learning lies solely in cultivating oneself.” He also said: “To restrain this person and keep it from acting recklessly is something I can indeed already do. But to restrain this mind and keep it from stirring recklessly is still difficult.” Such was his sincerity in embodying the Way that he seemed always to be seeking something he had not attained; such was his utmost humility that, even when he had attained a capacity, he claimed no credit for it. Measured against the meaning of refinement and single-mindedness, his practice accorded with it without deliberation; examined against the disposition of reverent vigilance, his mind matched it without deliberate striving.

Thus he came to possess all regions, recovered the territory of the Central Realm that had fallen into alien hands, expelled the northern barbarians, and restored the caps and robes—the civilized institutions—of the Central Realm that had fallen into disuse. He personally brought about great peace and enjoyed the fruits of his achievements. His accomplishments shone throughout Heaven and Earth, and the spirits of mountains and rivers submitted without resistance. His transforming influence reached the foreign peoples, who presented silks and offered treasures, hastening to pledge allegiance lest they fall behind. People see only the grandeur of his achievements; how could they know that these were rooted in the apprehension and vigilance of his sagely mind? Hence we find in his sagely instructions: “The ruler’s single mind is the foundation of government and moral transformation. If what he harbors within is not the mind of Yao and Shun, yet he wishes to achieve the government of Yao and Shun in his administration, this will certainly be unattainable.” Here this truth can be discerned. Our…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇上聰明天授
聖德日新紹心學之傳發道統之秘萬幾之暇
親製敬一箴及
註釋視聽言動心箴而又頒布學宮陳之藝極
蓋嘗沐浴譽髦之化而躬承棫樸之風而
有以仰窺
皇上之心卽
高皇帝之心也故曰人有此心萬理咸具示本
體也匪一弗純匪敬弗聚明聖功也
===
郊則恭誠
廟嚴孝趨萃孝享也肅於明庭慎於閒居合動
靜也弗參以三弗貳以二求致一也靜虛
無欲日新不已務緝熈也至於操存在心
無有遠近視之如一口鼻之覺賢於耳目
此又前賢所未發而
聖心所獨得蓋身有之言故親切而有味躬行
之敎故光大而可傳蓋質之堯舜則世異
而道同而協之
punctuated:
皇上聰明天授，聖德日新，紹心學之傳，發道統之秘。萬幾之暇，親製《敬一箴》及註釋《視聽言動心箴》，而又頒布學宮，陳之藝極。蓋嘗沐浴譽髦之化，而躬承棫樸之風，而有以仰窺皇上之心，卽高皇帝之心也。故曰：「人有此心，萬理咸具。」示本體也。「匪一弗純，匪敬弗聚。」明聖功也。
「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨。」萃孝享也。「肅於明庭，慎於閒居。」合動靜也。「弗參以三，弗貳以二。」求致一也。「靜虛無欲，日新不已。」務緝熈也。至於「操存在心，無有遠近，視之如一，口鼻之覺，賢於耳目」，此又前賢所未發，而聖心所獨得。蓋身有之言，故親切而有味；躬行之敎，故光大而可傳。蓋質之堯舜，則世異而道同；而協之
translation_en:
…His Majesty possesses Heaven-bestowed intelligence, and his sagely virtue is renewed daily. He continues the transmission of the learning of the mind and reveals the mysteries of the succession of the Way. Amid his myriad affairs, he personally composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen) and commentaries on the Admonitions on Seeing, Hearing, Speaking, Acting, and the Mind. He further distributed these to the schools, setting them forth as the highest standards of learning. Having benefited from the transforming influence that nurtures outstanding scholars, and personally received the influence celebrated in “The Oak Trees” (Yupu), we can thereby glimpse, looking upward, that His Majesty’s mind is precisely the mind of Emperor Gao. Thus the words “People possess this mind; all principles are fully present within it” reveal its fundamental substance. “Without unity, it cannot be pure; without reverence, it cannot be gathered together” illuminates the work of sagehood.
“At the suburban sacrifice, be reverent and sincere; in the ancestral temple, solemnly hasten to filial service [?]” concentrates attention on filial offerings. “Be solemn in the public court; be cautious in private repose” unites activity and stillness. “Do not divide it into three; do not split it into two” seeks the attainment of unity. “Still and empty, without desires; renewed daily without cease” urges the continued cultivation of luminous virtue. As for “Maintaining and preserving it lies in the mind; whether distant or near, regard it as one; the awareness of mouth and nose surpasses that of ears and eyes,” these are insights that earlier worthies had not articulated and that the sagely mind alone has attained. Because these words express what he himself embodies, they are intimate and rich in meaning; because this teaching is enacted in his own conduct, it is expansive and luminous, worthy of transmission. Measured against Yao and Shun, the ages differ but the Way is the same; and brought into accord with…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
皇祖則言殊而理一矣是故
郊廟正而羣祀舉
大典成而彝倫明定先師之號而道統有光立
帝王之廟而治統益振撤
內殿之佛像毀夷主之瀆祀百廢具舉衆志
一新當百年禮樂之期成一代
中興之典人徒知文明之化而豈知由於
聖心之敬一哉故觀於
聖製有曰欲盡持敬之功以馴致乎一德其先
===
務又在虛心寡慾斯可行純王之道以坐
致太平雍熈之至治有可知矣夫莫爲之
前雖美而弗彰莫爲之後雖盛而弗傳以
堯舜之盛而繼世無聞以文武之光而再
傳則息孰有如我
聖祖
皇上前作後述繼繼繩繩以垂萬億年無疆之
大業者哉愚生躬逢
聖世竊伏海邦望汪洋而蠡測瞻高遠而管窺
punctuated:
皇祖，則言殊而理一矣。是故郊廟正而羣祀舉，大典成而彝倫明。定先師之號而道統有光，立帝王之廟而治統益振。撤內殿之佛像，毀夷主之瀆祀，百廢具舉，衆志一新。當百年禮樂之期，成一代中興之典。人徒知文明之化，而豈知由於聖心之敬一哉？故觀於聖製，有曰：「欲盡持敬之功，以馴致乎一德，其先務又在虛心寡慾，斯可行純王之道，以坐致太平。」雍熈之至治，有可知矣。
夫莫爲之前，雖美而弗彰；莫爲之後，雖盛而弗傳。以堯舜之盛，而繼世無聞；以文武之光，而再傳則息。孰有如我聖祖、皇上，前作後述，繼繼繩繩，以垂萬億年無疆之大業者哉？愚生躬逢聖世，竊伏海邦，望汪洋而蠡測，瞻高遠而管窺。
translation_en:
…the Imperial Progenitor, the words differ but the principle is one. Thus the suburban and ancestral-temple sacrifices have been set right, and the various rites of worship duly performed; the great ceremonial ordinances have been established, and the enduring human relationships clarified. By settling the title of the First Teacher, Confucius, you have brought lustre to the succession of the Way; by establishing a temple to emperors and kings, you have further strengthened the succession of rightful governance. You have removed Buddhist images from the inner palace halls and abolished the profane sacrifices to foreign deities [?]. All neglected undertakings have been revived, and the aspirations of the multitude renewed. At the appointed time for rites and music to flourish after a hundred years, you have established the institutions of a dynastic resurgence. People know only the transforming influence of your illustrious culture; how could they know that it springs from the reverent unity of your sagely mind? Thus we read in your imperial composition: “To bring the work of maintaining reverence to its fullest accomplishment, and thereby gradually attain unified virtue, the first task lies in keeping the mind receptive and desires few. Only then can one practise the pure way of true kingship and bring about great peace without exertion.” From this, the prospect of consummate government in harmony and prosperity can be understood.
If no one initiates an undertaking, however fine it may be, it will not become manifest; if no one carries it forward, however flourishing it may be, it will not be transmitted. Despite the greatness of Yao and Shun, their succeeding generations achieved no renown; despite the brilliance of Kings Wen and Wu, after two transmissions their achievement ceased. Who can compare with our sagely progenitor and Your Majesty, the former creating and the latter carrying forward, continuing in unbroken succession to bequeath an enduring imperial enterprise for countless millions of years? I, an unworthy scholar, have personally been fortunate to live in this sagely age. Humbly secluded in this coastal region, I gaze upon the vast ocean and measure it with a gourd; I look toward the lofty and distant and peer at it through a tube…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
盛大難名揄揚莫罄若夫
治化之光昭
頌聲之洋溢內夏外夷鼓舞詠歌久矣又奚
待愚生之賛揚也哉謹對
第二問
陳南星
同考試官教諭方批敷叙前代之文而終之以取法朱子
子其有心於聖賢之文者耶
同考試官教諭夏批斯文斷案昔人已有定說此策
===
能歷歷言之蓋必學文而有得者
考試官學正李批斟酌古人之文抑揚不失
佳士也
考試官教授向批條答無遺學識自見
文者道之顯也有道斯有文矣道者文之
實也知道斯知文矣聖人非有意於文也
道不容以自秘則於文乎洩之故聖人之
文如風行水上自然之文也後之為文者
習之以藝而無見於道無怪乎其文之不
punctuated:
盛大難名，揄揚莫罄。若夫治化之光昭，頌聲之洋溢，內夏外夷鼓舞詠歌久矣，又奚待愚生之賛揚也哉？謹對。

第二問
陳南星

同考試官教諭方批：敷叙前代之文，而終之以取法朱子。子其有心於聖賢之文者耶？
同考試官教諭夏批：斯文斷案，昔人已有定說，此策能歷歷言之，蓋必學文而有得者。
考試官學正李批：斟酌古人之文，抑揚不失，佳士也。
考試官教授向批：條答無遺，學識自見。

文者，道之顯也，有道斯有文矣。道者，文之實也，知道斯知文矣。聖人非有意於文也，道不容以自秘，則於文乎洩之。故聖人之文，如風行水上，自然之文也。後之為文者，習之以藝而無見於道，無怪乎其文之不
translation_en:
…Its grandeur is difficult to describe, and no praise can exhaust it. As for the brilliance of the transforming influence of your governance and the abundance of songs of praise, the Chinese within and the foreign peoples beyond have long danced and sung in celebration. What need is there, then, to await the praise of this unworthy student? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Question
Chen Nanxing 陳南星

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: You expound the writings of earlier ages and conclude by taking Master Zhu as your model. Surely you aspire to the writing of the sages and worthies?

Comment by Associate Examiner Xia, Instructor: Earlier writers have already reached settled judgments on this literature. This policy essay articulates them distinctly, one by one. Its author must surely have gained something from his study of writing.

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: He weighs the writings of the ancients, finding the proper measure in both criticism and praise. A fine scholar indeed.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: His point-by-point response omits nothing; his learning and discernment are evident of themselves.

Writing is the manifestation of the Way: where there is the Way, there is writing. The Way is the substance of writing: to understand the Way is thus to understand writing. The sages did not deliberately set out to produce writing. Since the Way could not remain concealed within them, they gave it expression in writing. Thus the writing of the sages resembles wind moving over water: its patterns arise naturally. Those who wrote in later ages practiced writing as a skill but had no insight into the Way. It is no wonder that their writing does not…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
類聖人也然天下豈有道外之文哉君子
之於文也亦惟求諸道焉而已矣世之論
文者曰有聖賢之文有文人之文自世之
有是言也而始離道於文而不知道之與
文本不相離也嘗觀史臣之賛堯也曰欽
明文思其賛舜也曰濬哲文明夫當其時
六經未作也而奚有於文子思曰於乎不
顯文王之德之純蓋曰文王之所以爲文
也夫方策之政孰非文也而必歸諸其德
===
之純此其故何也豈不以四表之光無非
至道西土之顯咸爲至文耶知此則可以
論文矣是故有聖人之時則有潔淨精微
之文有聖人之政事則有疏通知遠之文
有聖人之性情則有溫柔敦厚之文有聖
人之名分則有屬辭比事之文有聖人之
中和則有恭敬齊莊廣博易良之文是何
也文與道一也聖人之言猶化工也無意
於文而自無不文者也夫是之謂聖賢之
punctuated: 類聖人也。然天下豈有道外之文哉？君子之於文也，亦惟求諸道焉而已矣。世之論文者曰：「有聖賢之文，有文人之文。」自世之有是言也，而始離道於文，而不知道之與文本不相離也。嘗觀史臣之賛堯也，曰：「欽明文思。」其賛舜也，曰：「濬哲文明。」夫當其時，六經未作也，而奚有於文？子思曰：「於乎不顯，文王之德之純！」蓋曰文王之所以爲文也。夫方策之政，孰非文也？而必歸諸其德之純，此其故何也？豈不以四表之光，無非至道；西土之顯，咸爲至文耶？知此，則可以論文矣。是故有聖人之時，則有潔淨精微之文；有聖人之政事，則有疏通知遠之文；有聖人之性情，則有溫柔敦厚之文；有聖人之名分，則有屬辭比事之文；有聖人之中和，則有恭敬齊莊、廣博易良之文。是何也？文與道一也。聖人之言，猶化工也，無意於文，而自無不文者也。夫是之謂聖賢之
translation_en:
…resemble that of the sages. Yet can there be any writing under Heaven outside the Way? In approaching writing, the gentleman merely seeks it in the Way. Those who discuss writing nowadays say: “There is the writing of sages and worthies, and there is the writing of literary men.” Only when this saying arose did people begin to separate the Way from writing, failing to understand that the Way and writing are inherently inseparable. I have observed that the court historian’s praise of Yao says: “Reverent, enlightened, accomplished, and thoughtful.” His praise of Shun says: “Profoundly wise, cultured, and luminous.” At that time the Six Classics had not yet been composed: in what, then, did their cultural accomplishment consist? Zisi said: “Ah, how illustrious was the purity of King Wen’s virtue!” This surely explains why King Wen was called Wen, “the Cultured.” Of the acts of government recorded on tablets and documents, which was not an expression of culture? Yet the praise must be traced back to the purity of his virtue. Why is this? Is it not because the radiance reaching the four farthest bounds was entirely the consummate Way, and the illustrious manifestation in the western lands was entirely consummate cultural expression? Understanding this, one may discuss writing.

Thus, where there is the sages’ understanding of the times, there is writing that is pure, refined, and subtle; where there are the sages’ affairs of government, there is writing that is penetrating and comprehends the distant past; where there are the sages’ dispositions and feelings, there is writing that is gentle, generous, and sincere; where there are the sages’ distinctions of status and duty, there is writing that orders its words and juxtaposes events; where there are the sages’ equilibrium and harmony, there is writing that is reverent and solemn, broadly informed, accessible, and good. Why is this? Writing and the Way are one. The sages’ words resemble the workings of creation: without deliberate intent to produce literary form, they naturally possess it throughout. This is what is called the sages’ and worthies’…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
文昔者子貢之在聖門夫子之文章可得
而聞矣而猶示之無言孟子之於楊墨也
辭而闢之廓如矣而猶謂之不得已此其
故何也豈不以空言無補不如無言苟可
無辯不如且已乎知此則可以論爲文矣
是故無孔子正名之志則筆削於簡冊者
不過爲呂氏之春秋無孟子仁義之旨則
問答於門弟者或至爲王通之中說是何
也文與道二也後世之言猶繪事也雖得
===
其似而失其真者也夫是之謂文人之文
孔孟而下其爲聖賢之文者或寡矣司馬
遷之史記世所謂西京之文也其事核其
文直亦嘗見推於班史矣然其敘六家之
要旨則以儒次於陰陽而其論義理之文
則以莊助朱買臣輩當之玆文也藝也安
望其有所發明於道耶班固之漢書世所
謂東漢之文也贍而不穢詳而有體亦嘗
見稱於范曄矣然其志藝文也則以儒竝
punctuated:
文。昔者子貢之在聖門，夫子之文章可得而聞矣，而猶示之無言；孟子之於楊墨也，辭而闢之廓如矣，而猶謂之不得已。此其故何也？豈不以空言無補，不如無言；苟可無辯，不如且已乎？知此則可以論爲文矣。是故無孔子正名之志，則筆削於簡冊者，不過爲呂氏之春秋；無孟子仁義之旨，則問答於門弟者，或至爲王通之中說。是何也？文與道二也。後世之言猶繪事也，雖得其似，而失其真者也。夫是之謂文人之文。
孔孟而下，其爲聖賢之文者或寡矣。司馬遷之史記，世所謂西京之文也。其事核，其文直，亦嘗見推於班史矣。然其敘六家之要旨，則以儒次於陰陽；而其論義理之文，則以莊助、朱買臣輩當之。玆文也，藝也，安望其有所發明於道耶？班固之漢書，世所謂東漢之文也。贍而不穢，詳而有體，亦嘗見稱於范曄矣。然其志藝文也，則以儒竝
translation_en:
…writing. In former times, when Zigong studied in the sage’s school, he could hear the Master’s cultured discourse, yet the Master still showed him the teaching of wordlessness. Mencius, in confronting the doctrines of Yang Zhu and Mo Di, refuted them so thoroughly that he swept them away, yet he still said that he had no choice but to argue. Why was this? Was it not because empty words accomplish nothing, so that silence is preferable, and because, if disputation can be avoided, it is better to desist? Understanding this, one can discuss the practice of writing. Thus, without Confucius’s resolve to rectify names, what one commits to or excises from the written record amounts to no more than Master Lü’s Spring and Autumn Annals; without Mencius’s commitment to benevolence and righteousness, one’s questions and answers with disciples may end up becoming something like Wang Tong’s Explanations of the Mean (Zhongshuo). Why is this? Because writing and the Way have become two separate things. The words of later generations resemble painting: although they capture a likeness, they lose the truth. This is what is called the writing of literary men.
After Confucius and Mencius, perhaps few produced the writing of sages and worthies. Sima Qian’s Records of the Grand Historian is what the world calls the writing of the Western Capital period. Its facts are sound and its prose straightforward: it was indeed praised in Ban Gu’s history. Yet in setting out the essential tenets of the six schools, it places the Confucians below the School of Yin and Yang; and when discussing writings on moral principles, it takes the works of Zhuang Zhu, Zhu Maichen, and their like as representative. Such writing is literary craft. How could one expect it to illuminate the Way? Ban Gu’s History of the Han is what the world calls the writing of the Eastern Han. Rich without being cluttered, detailed yet well structured, it too received praise from Fan Ye. Yet in its bibliographical treatise, it places the Confucians alongside …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
列於九家而其傳儒林也則以博士弟子
所習業者當之玆文也史也又惡能有所
發明於道耶魏晉以降風逾下矣撰典論
者空聨建安之名作文賦者無補建春之
過漢書之續自謂奇作矣竟悲絃外之音
宋書之脩自稱見事矣莫贖懷中之草風
雲月露之篇皆浮華纖麗之習雖謂之無
文可也自駢儷之體興而唐之文弊矣韓
愈氏起而變之因文見道所謂唐之山斗
===
也柳宗元氏從而和之雄深雅健之作亦
一時之善鳴也故論唐文者必歸之韓柳
焉然考其實則韓子之原道發明道德之
義力排似是之非信非柳子之所能與也
况柳子不戒匪人之比卒貽遠擯之戚又
自離於聖人之道乎自軋茁之習熾而宋
之文弊矣歐陽脩起而變之崇雅黜浮所
謂宋之韓愈也蘇氏兄弟從而和之捭闔
變化之妙蓋天下之奇才也故論宋文者
punctuated: 列於九家，而其傳儒林也，則以博士弟子所習業者當之。玆文也，史也，又惡能有所發明於道耶？魏晉以降，風逾下矣。撰《典論》者，空聨建安之名；作《文賦》者，無補建春之過。《漢書》之續，自謂奇作矣，竟悲絃外之音；《宋書》之脩，自稱見事矣，莫贖懷中之草。風雲月露之篇，皆浮華纖麗之習，雖謂之無文可也。自駢儷之體興，而唐之文弊矣。韓愈氏起而變之，因文見道，所謂唐之山斗也。柳宗元氏從而和之，雄深雅健之作，亦一時之善鳴也。故論唐文者，必歸之韓柳焉。然考其實，則韓子之《原道》，發明道德之義，力排似是之非，信非柳子之所能與也。况柳子不戒匪人之比，卒貽遠擯之戚，又自離於聖人之道乎？自軋茁之習熾，而宋之文弊矣。歐陽脩起而變之，崇雅黜浮，所謂宋之韓愈也。蘇氏兄弟從而和之，捭闔變化之妙，蓋天下之奇才也。故論宋文者
translation_en:
…ranked among the nine schools; and in his biographies of the Confucian scholars, he treated the learning pursued by the students of the Erudites as representing it. Such writing is merely history: how, again, could it illuminate the Way? From the Wei and Jin onward, literary standards declined still further. The author of Discourses on the Standards (Dianlun) merely linked himself with the literary fame of the Jian’an era; the author of the Rhapsody on Literature (Wen fu) could not thereby make amends for his error at Jianchun [?]. The author of a continuation of the History of the Han considered it an extraordinary work, yet ultimately lamented the sound beyond the strings [?]; the compiler of the History of the Song claimed insight into affairs, yet could not redeem himself from the draft hidden in his bosom [?]. Pieces on wind and clouds, moonlight and dew all followed the fashion for superficial ornament and delicate elegance. One might even say that they were no literature at all.

With the rise of parallel prose, Tang writing fell into bad habits. Han Yu arose to transform it, revealing the Way through literature: he was what people call the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the Tang. Liu Zongyuan followed and responded to him. His powerful, profound, elegant, and vigorous works likewise gave distinguished expression to their age. Thus those who discuss Tang literature invariably turn to Han and Liu. Yet, upon examining the substance, Master Han’s Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao) elucidated the meaning of the Way and virtue and vigorously rejected specious errors. This was assuredly beyond Master Liu’s ability to match. Moreover, Master Liu failed to guard against associating with unworthy men and ultimately brought upon himself the sorrow of distant banishment. Did he not thereby also depart from the Way of the sages?

As the fashion for strained and awkward writing [?] flourished, Song literature fell into bad habits. Ouyang Xiu arose to transform it, honoring elegance and rejecting superficiality: he was what people call the Han Yu of the Song. The Su brothers followed and responded to him. With their marvelous command of rhetorical expansion, contraction, and variation, they were indeed exceptional talents in the realm. Thus those who discuss Song literature…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
必美乎歐蘇焉然考其時則周子之太極
圖張子之西銘程子之易傳春秋傳序究
極天人之蘊發明聖經之旨亦非歐蘇之
所能及也况歐之性非所先蘇之以術談
經又自外於聖人之道乎故論唐之文至
韓愈正矣然其時又不有陸宣公乎行在
諸疏經國弘猷奉天一詔聞者感泣玆固
其文也然其上不負天子下不負所學無
愧平生之言寧人負我無我負人深合聖
===
經之旨則又不特論諫之可法而已所謂
智如子房而學則過才如賈誼而術不疎
蘇子眞知言哉論宋之文至周程張子偉
矣然其時又不有朱子乎傳註之作折衷
羣籍告君之言不離誠正玆固其文也然
其居敬以立其體窮理以致其知克己以
滅其私存誠以踐其實則亦不特著述之
可傳而已所謂傳濂洛之正統集諸儒之
大成吳澄氏豈溢美哉之二公者皆庶幾
punctuated:
必美乎歐蘇焉。然考其時，則周子之《太極圖》、張子之《西銘》、程子之《易傳》《春秋傳序》，究極天人之蘊，發明聖經之旨，亦非歐蘇之所能及也。况歐之「性非所先」，蘇之以術談經，又自外於聖人之道乎？故論唐之文，至韓愈正矣。然其時又不有陸宣公乎？行在諸疏，經國弘猷；奉天一詔，聞者感泣。玆固其文也。然其上不負天子，下不負所學，無愧平生之言；「寧人負我，無我負人」，深合聖經之旨，則又不特論諫之可法而已。所謂「智如子房而學則過，才如賈誼而術不疎」，蘇子眞知言哉！
論宋之文，至周程張子偉矣。然其時又不有朱子乎？傳註之作，折衷羣籍；告君之言，不離誠正。玆固其文也。然其居敬以立其體，窮理以致其知，克己以滅其私，存誠以踐其實，則亦不特著述之可傳而已。所謂「傳濂洛之正統，集諸儒之大成」，吳澄氏豈溢美哉？之二公者，皆庶幾
translation_en:
…one must praise Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi. Yet, examining their age, we find that Master Zhou’s Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate, Master Zhang’s Western Inscription, and Master Cheng’s Commentary on the Changes and Preface to the Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals probed the deepest mysteries of Heaven and humanity and elucidated the meaning of the sages’ classics. These, too, lay beyond what Ouyang and Su could attain. Moreover, Ouyang held that “human nature is not the foremost concern,” while Su discussed the classics in terms of expedient methods: did they not thereby place themselves outside the Way of the sages? Thus, in discussing Tang prose, with Han Yu we arrive at what is correct. Yet was there not also Lu Xuangong in his day? His memorials submitted at the emperor’s temporary residence offered grand plans for governing the state; his single edict issued at Fengtian moved its hearers to tears. These were indeed his literary achievements. Yet he neither failed the Son of Heaven above nor betrayed his learning below, and he lived without shame in relation to the words he had spoken throughout his life. “Better that others betray me than that I betray others”: this accorded profoundly with the meaning of the sages’ classics. Thus, it was not merely his arguments and remonstrances that deserved to serve as models. As Su Shi said, “His wisdom matched Zifang’s, but his learning surpassed it; his talent matched Jia Yi’s, but his methods were free of shortcomings.” Truly, Master Su spoke with discernment!
In discussing Song prose, with Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang we arrive at greatness. Yet was there not also Master Zhu in their day? In his commentaries and annotations, he weighed and reconciled the various books; in his words of counsel to the ruler, he never departed from sincerity of intention and rectification of the heart. These were indeed his literary achievements. Yet he also maintained reverence to establish his moral foundation, investigated principles to extend his knowledge, mastered himself to extinguish selfishness, and preserved sincerity to put these principles into practice. Thus, it was not merely his writings that deserved transmission. As Wu Cheng said, he “transmitted the orthodox succession of Lian and Luo and brought together the great achievements of the Confucian scholars.” Was this excessive praise? These two gentlemen both came close to…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
乎聖賢之文者也然合而論之諫行言聴
經國制變則朱子不如宣公之大立德立
言傳道教人則宣公不如朱子之久要之
朱子載道之文上承道統之正宣公不得
而與也善乎其徒黃幹之言曰孔子沒曾
子子思繼其微至孟子而始著孟子沒周
程張子繼其絕至朱子而始明茲言也其
斯文之斷案矣乎噫六經孔孟之文不可
得而續矣論文者取衷於朱子斯可矣聖
===
人自然之文不可得而見矣爲文者取法
於朱子亦足矣雖然文不可以易爲也而
所以昌之者存乎氣道不可以襲取也而
所以明之者存乎心蓋心者道之管也氣
者文之充也故爲文者莫先乎治心其次
莫若養氣心以爲主氣以出之然後可以
不離於道而昌其辭學者執是道以往則
載道之文其庶幾乎周子所謂篤實而藝
書美愛而久傳者或在茲也不然亦虛車
punctuated:
乎聖賢之文者也。然合而論之，諫行言聴，經國制變，則朱子不如宣公之大；立德立言，傳道教人，則宣公不如朱子之久。要之，朱子載道之文，上承道統之正，宣公不得而與也。善乎其徒黃幹之言曰：「孔子沒，曾子、子思繼其微，至孟子而始著；孟子沒，周、程、張子繼其絕，至朱子而始明。」茲言也，其斯文之斷案矣乎！噫！六經孔孟之文，不可得而續矣；論文者取衷於朱子，斯可矣。聖人自然之文，不可得而見矣；爲文者取法於朱子，亦足矣。

雖然，文不可以易爲也，而所以昌之者存乎氣；道不可以襲取也，而所以明之者存乎心。蓋心者，道之管也；氣者，文之充也。故爲文者莫先乎治心，其次莫若養氣。心以爲主，氣以出之，然後可以不離於道而昌其辭。學者執是道以往，則載道之文，其庶幾乎！周子所謂「篤實而藝，書美愛而久傳」者，或在茲也。不然，亦虛車
translation_en:
…approach the writings of the sages and worthies. Yet, considered together, in having remonstrances acted upon and advice heeded, ordering the state and managing unforeseen changes, Master Zhu did not match the greatness of Duke Xuan. In establishing virtue and enduring teachings, transmitting the Way and instructing others, Duke Xuan did not match Master Zhu’s lasting influence. In sum, Master Zhu’s writings, which bear the Way, directly inherited the orthodox transmission of the Way; Duke Xuan could not share this distinction. How well his disciple Huang Gan expressed it: “After Confucius died, Zengzi and Zisi continued his subtle teachings, which only with Mengzi became manifest. After Mengzi died, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang resumed the interrupted transmission, which only with Master Zhu became clear.” Surely these words constitute the definitive judgment on this cultural tradition! Alas! The writings of the Six Classics, Confucius, and Mengzi cannot be continued. Those who discuss writing need only take Master Zhu as their standard. The sages’ spontaneous writing can no longer be witnessed; for those who compose, taking Master Zhu as their model is sufficient.

Nevertheless, writing cannot be undertaken lightly: what makes it flourish lies in vital force, qi. The Way cannot be acquired by mere borrowing: what illuminates it lies in the mind. The mind is the conduit of the Way, and vital force is what fills writing. Thus, for those who write, nothing takes precedence over ordering the mind; next, nothing is better than nourishing vital force. With the mind governing and vital force giving expression to it, one can then make one’s language flourish without departing from the Way. If students proceed along this path, they may come close to writing that bears the Way! What Master Zhou called “being earnest and substantial, yet accomplished in the arts, so that writing is beautiful, cherished, and long transmitted” [?] may lie here. Otherwise, it is merely an empty carriage…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
耳執事何庸焉
第三問
石磐
同考試官教諭祝批議論有據詞致亦工佳
士也
考試官學正李批敷敘有體斷制不差
程式之文也
考試官教授向批詳贍
達經制之宜者而後知聖人制治之法通
===
損益之故者而後知聖人制法之詳夫聖
人立法以維治非聖人意也勢也世非忘
言則法不得以不立日入于多事則制不
容以不詳故創法以制治存之為百王之
典因典以貽則垂之為萬世之經此皆聖
人精神心術之運裁成輔相之能也議法
者不達其宜疑之所以生也猶輪人之巧
不足而欲廢大匠之規矩者也用法者弗
獲其效沮之所以生也猶醫人不求標木
punctuated:
耳，執事何庸焉？

第三問
石磐
同考試官教諭祝批：「議論有據，詞致亦工，佳士也。」
考試官學正李批：「敷敘有體，斷制不差，程式之文也。」
考試官教授向批：「詳贍。」

達經制之宜者，而後知聖人制治之法；通損益之故者，而後知聖人制法之詳。夫聖人立法以維治，非聖人意也，勢也。世非忘言，則法不得以不立；日入于多事，則制不容以不詳。故創法以制治，存之為百王之典；因典以貽則，垂之為萬世之經。此皆聖人精神心術之運，裁成輔相之能也。議法者不達其宜，疑之所以生也，猶輪人之巧不足而欲廢大匠之規矩者也。用法者弗獲其效，沮之所以生也，猶醫人不求標木
translation_en:
…that is all. What use would you have for it, sir?

Third Policy Question
Shi Pan
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “His arguments are well grounded, and his expression is accomplished. He is a fine scholar.”
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “The exposition is properly structured, and the judgments are sound. This is an essay that exemplifies the prescribed form.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “Detailed and ample.”

Only those who understand the appropriateness of established institutions can understand the sages’ methods of bringing about orderly government; only those who comprehend the reasons for subtraction and addition can understand the detail of the sages’ legislation. The sages established laws to sustain orderly government, not from personal inclination, but because circumstances required it. Since the world had not ‘forgotten words’ [?], laws could not but be established; as affairs grew more numerous by the day, institutions could not but become more detailed. Thus they created laws to establish orderly government, preserving them as canons for successive kings; drawing upon these canons, they bequeathed standards, handing them down as enduring guides for myriad generations. All this was the working of the sages’ spiritual energies and arts of the mind, their capacity to shape and complete things and assist their proper development. Those who discuss laws fail to understand their appropriateness, and this gives rise to doubt. They resemble a wheelwright whose skill is inadequate but who wishes to discard the compass and square of a master craftsman. Those who apply laws fail to obtain their benefits, and this gives rise to discouragement. They resemble physicians who do not investigate the branches and root [?]…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
之理而歸咎于古人之方者也周禮之不
幸類是其不明不行也宜哉執事以周禮
策諸生而致疑於建官出令之詳此愚生
之所以不容不辯也夫周公相成王以成
一代之治斟酌損益著爲定制周禮者所
以紀其經緯彌綸之迹也其規模統體之
極其大條理節目之盡其詳具有成書固
無俟於贅矣顧流言肆而東居之轍遠嬴
計左而瓜丘之焰張其志弗竟而法之弗
===
行是以弗著弗察無惑乎後人是非疑信
之不一雖經程朱胡蘇之辯論而終莫取
衷豈聖人之制可疑哉無亦議之者之見
爾自今觀之政莫重於建官而法必先於
出令建官惟其人出令惟其時治之所係
不小也是故政不可以一人理任職親民
以計治弊訟官之不可巳也然禄以馭冨
官衆而禄將奚從出乎唐虞惟百夏商官
倍亦克用乂周禮五官之屬衆至數萬執
punctuated: 之理，而歸咎于古人之方者也。周禮之不幸類是，其不明不行也宜哉！執事以《周禮》策諸生，而致疑於建官出令之詳，此愚生之所以不容不辯也。夫周公相成王，以成一代之治，斟酌損益，著爲定制。《周禮》者，所以紀其經緯彌綸之迹也。其規模統體之極其大，條理節目之盡其詳，具有成書，固無俟於贅矣。顧流言肆而東居之轍遠，嬴計左而瓜丘之焰張，其志弗竟而法之弗行，是以弗著弗察，無惑乎後人是非疑信之不一。雖經程朱胡蘇之辯論，而終莫取衷，豈聖人之制可疑哉？無亦議之者之見爾。自今觀之，政莫重於建官，而法必先於出令。建官惟其人，出令惟其時，治之所係不小也。是故政不可以一人理，任職親民，以計治弊，訟官之不可巳也。然禄以馭冨，官衆而禄將奚從出乎？唐虞惟百，夏商官倍，亦克用乂。《周禮》五官之屬，衆至數萬，執
translation_en:
…the principles involved, yet lay the blame on the prescriptions of the ancients. The misfortune suffered by the Rites of Zhou is similar: no wonder it has neither been understood nor put into practice! You, sir, have set the candidates a policy question on the Rites of Zhou, expressing doubts about its detailed provisions for establishing offices and issuing commands. This is why I, an unworthy student, cannot refrain from offering a defense.

The Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng in bringing an entire age under good government. He weighed what should be removed or added and set it down as established institutions. The Rites of Zhou records the traces of his work in ordering and comprehensively regulating the realm. The vast scope of its overall structure and the exhaustive detail of its arrangements and provisions are all contained in the completed book; there is certainly no need to elaborate upon them here. Yet slander ran rampant, and the tracks of his journey to dwell in the east led far away; the Ying house’s schemes went awry, and the flames at Guaqiu blazed high [?]. His aspirations were not fulfilled, and his institutions were not implemented. Consequently, they were neither made manifest nor clearly understood. It is no wonder that later generations have differed in their judgments of right and wrong, their doubts and their trust. Even after the debates of Cheng, Zhu, Hu, and Su, no settled judgment has finally been reached. Can the sage’s institutions themselves be doubtful? Surely this reflects only the views of those who discuss them.

Viewed from the present, nothing in government matters more than establishing offices, and rules must precede the issuing of commands. Establishing offices depends on finding the right people; issuing commands depends on choosing the right time. These are matters of considerable consequence for good government. Thus government cannot be managed by one person alone. Assigning duties and keeping close to the people, so as to assess good administration and its failings, makes the establishment of offices indispensable [?]. Yet stipends are the means of regulating wealth: if officials are numerous, where will their stipends come from? Under Tang and Yu there were only a hundred officials; under Xia and Shang their number doubled, yet orderly government was still achieved. In the Rites of Zhou, those subordinate to the five principal offices number in the tens of thousands. You, sir, …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
事疑其官之衆而欲究其祿之所自出誠
有見也然内外之備官者制之詳也官事
之必攝者制之善也故周公以冢宰兼三
公召公以三公兼司徒師旅之將帥卽王
朝之卿士皆因事設官事巳而官廢則雖
衆而不爲冗矣乃若田以井授公私内外
之有其差祿以田賦卿士大夫之有所仰
此井田世祿相須而行何有於祿之不給
耶不然使之自食其力祿不足好于其家
===
室人徧謫豈先王恤人之私哉令不可以
弗豫申命行事以鼓舞萬民令之不可已
也然命之靡常視聽惑而民將奚以從乎
古者爲而不有應而不求周禮歲朔孟仲
凡大聚會月必屢至執事疑其令之煩而
慮其爲民之擾固其宜也然會以作事者
義之盡也而徵以時會者仁之至也故飲
射之法以州長行之讀法之法以黨正行
之象魏之布夾日而斂則令之素定民之
punctuated:
事疑其官之衆，而欲究其祿之所自出，誠有見也。然内外之備官者，制之詳也；官事之必攝者，制之善也。故周公以冢宰兼三公，召公以三公兼司徒，師旅之將帥卽王朝之卿士，皆因事設官，事巳而官廢，則雖衆而不爲冗矣。乃若田以井授，公私内外之有其差；祿以田賦，卿士大夫之有所仰。此井田世祿相須而行，何有於祿之不給耶？不然，使之自食其力，祿不足好于其家，室人徧謫，豈先王恤人之私哉？

令不可以弗豫，申命行事以鼓舞萬民，令之不可已也。然命之靡常，視聽惑，而民將奚以從乎？古者爲而不有，應而不求。《周禮》歲朔孟仲，凡大聚會，月必屢至。執事疑其令之煩，而慮其爲民之擾，固其宜也。然會以作事者，義之盡也；而徵以時會者，仁之至也。故飲射之法以州長行之，讀法之法以黨正行之，象魏之布夾日而斂，則令之素定，民之
translation_en:
…you question the great number of officials and wish to investigate where their stipends came from: this is indeed perceptive. Yet providing a full complement of offices within and outside the capital shows the comprehensiveness of the institutions; requiring officials to discharge duties concurrently shows their excellence. Thus the Duke of Zhou served as both Minister of State and one of the Three Dukes, while the Duke of Shao served as both one of the Three Dukes and Minister of Education. Commanders of armies and brigades were themselves ministers of the royal court. Offices were established as affairs required, and abolished when those affairs were concluded. Thus, although numerous, they were not superfluous.
