Fields were allotted under the well-field system, with distinctions between public and private fields and between inner and outer regions; stipends were furnished through revenues from the fields, giving ministers and grand masters a source of support. The well-field system and hereditary stipends thus operated in mutual dependence. How could stipends have been insufficient? Otherwise, if officials were made to support themselves by their own labor, their stipends insufficient to maintain harmony in their households, and their household members all reproaching them, would this accord with the former kings’ solicitude for people’s private circumstances?

Commands must be prepared in advance. Reiterating commands and carrying out affairs to inspire the myriad people are reasons why commands cannot be dispensed with. Yet if commands constantly change, confusing what people see and hear, how will they know what to follow? The ancients acted without claiming possession and responded without seeking anything. In the Rites of Zhou, provisions concerning the year, the new moon, and the first and second months of the seasons [?] meant that great assemblies necessarily occurred several times each month. It is certainly reasonable for you to question the frequency of these commands and fear that they disturbed the people. Yet assembling people to undertake affairs fulfills righteousness, while summoning them to assemble at the proper times expresses the utmost benevolence. Thus the procedures for ceremonial drinking and archery were carried out by the District Chiefs; those for reading the laws aloud were carried out by the Neighborhood Heads. Laws displayed on the palace gate towers were taken down after ten days. Thus the commands were established beforehand, and the people’s…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
素孚雖煩而不爲擾矣矧其振旅詢事而
隨地以致民蒐獮田狩而因時以舉事供
給徵召以有常守而何至於民之不堪邪
不然驅耕夫而役之不得盡力於農畝舍
我穡事豈先王重民之務哉於以見周公
之立法也隨事建官不豫官以待事因時
致令不煩令以勞民此良法美意周道之
所以長也然官非其人人民受其殃好煩其
令雖令不從此則聖人所大懼也故曰官
===
不必備惟其人又曰慎乃出令令出惟行
此又其法外意也知此則選用雖衆固不
病於倖進之私徵會雖煩自不患於非時
之擾矣奈之何去聖愈遠而疑之愈衆或
以王制不合於是有成周理財之疑班爵
不合於是有六國陰謀之疑蓋至於十論
七難之作而其言益肆矣一用於蘇綽無
補於宇文之治再用於劉歆益重乎新室
之誣蓋至於青苗手實之行而其法益病
punctuated: 素孚，雖煩而不爲擾矣。矧其振旅詢事而隨地以致民，蒐獮田狩而因時以舉事，供給徵召以有常守，而何至於民之不堪邪？不然，驅耕夫而役之，不得盡力於農畝，舍我穡事，豈先王重民之務哉？於以見周公之立法也，隨事建官，不豫官以待事；因時致令，不煩令以勞民。此良法美意，周道之所以長也。然官非其人，人民受其殃；好煩其令，雖令不從。此則聖人所大懼也。故曰：「官不必備，惟其人。」又曰：「慎乃出令，令出惟行。」此又其法外意也。知此，則選用雖衆，固不病於倖進之私；徵會雖煩，自不患於非時之擾矣。奈之何去聖愈遠而疑之愈衆？或以王制不合，於是有成周理財之疑；班爵不合，於是有六國陰謀之疑。蓋至於十論七難之作，而其言益肆矣。一用於蘇綽，無補於宇文之治；再用於劉歆，益重乎新室之誣。蓋至於青苗手實之行，而其法益病
translation_en: …long trusted by the people, so that even frequent commands cause no disturbance. Moreover, troops were reviewed and affairs considered, and the people were summoned as local circumstances required; seasonal hunts were conducted and undertakings carried out at the appropriate times. There were established rules governing the provision of supplies and the summoning of people for service: how could these have become unbearable to the people? Otherwise, to drive cultivators into service, preventing them from devoting their full strength to their fields and making them abandon their farming—could this be the former kings’ concern for the people’s work? From this we see how the Duke of Zhou established institutions: he created offices as affairs required, rather than establishing them in advance to await business; he issued commands when the occasion called for them, rather than burdening the people with a profusion of orders. These sound institutions and admirable intentions explain the longevity of the Zhou way of government. Yet when offices are held by unsuitable men, the people suffer the consequences; when rulers delight in multiplying orders, their commands go unheeded. This was what the sages most greatly feared. Thus it is said: “Offices need not all be filled; what matters is finding the right men.” And again: “Be cautious in issuing your commands; once issued, they must be carried out.” This, too, is the intention that lies beyond the letter of the institutions. Understanding this, even when many men are selected for office, one need not suffer from favoritism that enables undeserved advancement; even when assemblies are frequently summoned, one need not fear the disturbance caused by demands made at the wrong season. Why, then, do doubts multiply the farther we grow from the sages? Some, finding discrepancies with the Royal Regulations, consequently suspected that this was a scheme for managing the finances of Chengzhou; finding discrepancies in the ordering of noble ranks, they consequently suspected a conspiracy of the Six States. By the time the Ten Discourses and Seven Objections were written, such assertions had become increasingly unrestrained. Applied on one occasion by Su Chuo, it did nothing to improve the rule of the Yuwen house; applied on another by Liu Xin, it lent still greater weight to the false claims of the Xin dynasty. By the time the Green Sprouts loan scheme and the system of personal declarations of property were implemented, these institutions had become still more harmful…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
矣不知五等通於天下難施於侯國孟子
言於去籍無以考其詳其矛盾相反宜世
議之紛紛也或欲行於上而難其任或欲
究其用而非其時其枘鑿不入宜致用之
弗效也然則周禮非真可疑弗求其實則
通變不知周禮非不可用任匪其人則扞
格無成嘗試考之其建官之制固在也失
之者將必有為人擇官苟取充位其始也
冗雜同途其旣也根據莫解積薪之喻所
===
以有漢人之嘆也出令之法固在也失之
者將必有簿書期會責所不堪其始也若
憂之太殷其究也則擾之已甚種樹之術
是以啓唐人之論也然則議周禮者失周
禮者爾豈周禮之可議哉雖然古今者時
也經制者法也變通者人也時不相沿而
法因以異故周之建官後世多襲其迹而
召會徵令以施之今則擾矣故曰化而裁
之存乎變神而明之存乎人
punctuated: 矣。不知五等通於天下，難施於侯國；孟子言於去籍，無以考其詳。其矛盾相反，宜世議之紛紛也。或欲行於上而難其任，或欲究其用而非其時，其枘鑿不入，宜致用之弗效也。然則《周禮》非真可疑，弗求其實則通變不知；《周禮》非不可用，任匪其人則扞格無成。嘗試考之，其建官之制固在也。失之者，將必有為人擇官，苟取充位。其始也，冗雜同途；其旣也，根據莫解。積薪之喻，所以有漢人之嘆也。出令之法固在也。失之者，將必有簿書期會，責所不堪。其始也，若憂之太殷；其究也，則擾之已甚。種樹之術，是以啓唐人之論也。然則議《周禮》者，失《周禮》者爾，豈《周禮》之可議哉！雖然，古今者，時也；經制者，法也；變通者，人也。時不相沿而法因以異，故周之建官，後世多襲其迹，而召會徵令以施之今則擾矣。故曰：「化而裁之存乎變，神而明之存乎人。」
translation_en:
…indeed. They do not understand that the five ranks of nobility applied throughout the realm but were difficult to implement within the feudal states. Mencius spoke of the destruction of the records, leaving no means of examining the details. Given these contradictions and discrepancies, it is understandable that opinions through the ages have been so divided. Some wished to put these institutions into practice at the highest level but found the responsibility difficult to discharge; others wished to realize their full utility, but the time was inappropriate. Since tenon and mortise did not fit, it is understandable that practical application proved ineffective.

Thus the Rites of Zhou is not truly open to doubt: without investigating its substance, one cannot understand how to adapt it to changing circumstances. Nor is the Rites of Zhou unusable: when responsibility is entrusted to the wrong people, obstruction prevents success. Let us examine this. Its system for establishing offices certainly remains available. Those who depart from it will inevitably choose offices to suit particular people and fill posts merely for the sake of filling them. At first, redundant and miscellaneous appointees follow the same path; later, they become entrenched beyond disentanglement. This is why the metaphor of stacked firewood occasioned a Han man's lament.

Its methods for issuing orders certainly remain available. Those who depart from them will inevitably impose paperwork and deadlines, demanding more than people can bear. At first, they seem excessively solicitous; in the end, they cause excessive disturbance. This is why the art of planting trees inspired a Tang man's discussion. Those who criticize the Rites of Zhou, then, are simply those who have departed from it. How could the Rites of Zhou itself deserve criticism?

Nevertheless, antiquity and the present concern the times; established institutions concern methods; adaptation to change depends on people. Times do not remain the same, and methods consequently differ. Thus later ages largely followed the outlines of Zhou's establishment of offices, but to apply its summonses to assemblies and its requisition orders today would cause disturbance. Hence the saying: “Transforming and shaping things depends on change; making them wondrously effective and intelligible depends on people.”

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
第四問
王應時
同考試官教諭謝批聖人敬天理地之意存乎術數
之外子能言之可謂知聖人矣
考試官學正李批推原天地之理切於民用有見
考試官教授向批談術而本之理是善言天地者
用天之道者善知天者也因地之利者善
知地者也夫天垂象而聖人觀之以立占
作曆授時取於此焉故曰用天之道也地
===
列形而聖人察之以宜民體國經野行其
制焉故曰因地之利也觀天察地凡以為
民則聖人之知天非妄也民功興而天道
昭矣聖人之知地非迂也民物阜而地利
求矣故曰聖人善知天地也執事發策下
詢承學以天地之理愚也學無師授性乏
通悟何足以知之然亦嘗有聞於載籍矣
請掇拾以對夫乾象之說何昉乎自黃帝
命羲和占日月車區占星氣於是有星官
punctuated:
第四問
王應時
同考試官教諭謝批：聖人敬天理地之意，存乎術數之外。子能言之，可謂知聖人矣。
考試官學正李批：推原天地之理，切於民用，有見。
考試官教授向批：談術而本之理，是善言天地者。
用天之道者，善知天者也；因地之利者，善知地者也。夫天垂象，而聖人觀之以立占，作曆授時，取於此焉，故曰用天之道也。地列形，而聖人察之以宜民，體國經野，行其制焉，故曰因地之利也。觀天察地，凡以為民，則聖人之知天非妄也，民功興而天道昭矣；聖人之知地非迂也，民物阜而地利求矣。故曰聖人善知天地也。執事發策，下詢承學以天地之理。愚也，學無師授，性乏通悟，何足以知之？然亦嘗有聞於載籍矣，請掇拾以對。夫乾象之說何昉乎？自黃帝命羲和占日月，車區占星氣，於是有星官
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question
Wang Yingshi

Comment by Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor: The sages’ intent in revering Heaven and ordering the earth extends beyond numerical and divinatory techniques. You can articulate this and may therefore be said to understand the sages.

Comment by Examiner Li, School Instructor: You trace the principles of Heaven and earth to their origins and relate them closely to the people’s practical needs. This shows insight.

Comment by Examiner Xiang, Professor: You discuss techniques while grounding them in principle. This is to speak well of Heaven and earth.

Those who employ Heaven’s Way understand Heaven well; those who make use of the earth’s advantages understand the earth well. Heaven displays its signs, and the sages observe them to establish prognostications. From these they derive the means to make calendars and announce the seasons. Hence this is called employing Heaven’s Way. The earth presents its configurations, and the sages examine them to provide suitable conditions for the people. They lay out the capital and demarcate the countryside, putting their institutions into practice. Hence this is called making use of the earth’s advantages. Observing Heaven and examining the earth are alike undertaken for the people. Thus the sages’ understanding of Heaven is no idle fancy: the people’s undertakings flourish, and Heaven’s Way becomes manifest. Their understanding of the earth is no impractical pursuit: the people and all things thrive, and the earth’s advantages are sought out. Hence it is said that the sages understand Heaven and earth well.

You, sir, have issued a policy question, condescending to ask us students about the principles of Heaven and earth. Ignorant as I am, my learning has lacked a teacher’s instruction, and my nature lacks penetrating insight. How could I adequately understand them? Yet I have encountered something of these matters in written records. Permit me to gather these fragments and offer a reply.

Where did accounts of celestial phenomena originate? When Huangdi commanded Xihe to divine by the sun and moon, and Chequ [?] to divine by the stars and celestial emanations, there came to be astronomical …

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
之書而高陽氏則以南正重司天始有專
官矣至唐虞星鳥星火之分識璿璣玉衡
之首察以求七政之齊而周官則以馮相
保章氏世其業矣其後言天體者有宣夜
周髀渾天宣夜有名而無術周髀有術而
無驗惟渾天之法揚子雲謂其近理以其
能祖述璣衡而後世六合三辰四遊之儀
皆其制之傳也善星官者有巫咸甘德石
申巫咸之書無所考見而甘石善於推步
===
獨爲星經之祖凡今三垣五宮兩極十二
辰野五星列宿干支方位之說皆其術之
餘也楚魏而下代有其人如漢之洛下閎
鮮于妄人唐之李淳風僧一行皆以其術
著名當時而一行之穎悟絕人象數精博
其最優歟宋之沈括邵堯夫元之許平仲
郭守敬各以其說發明天道而守敬之立
法精詳度越千古其尤善歟要之聖人首
出庶物先天不違故能敬天觀象治曆明
punctuated: 之書，而高陽氏則以南正重司天，始有專官矣。至唐虞，星鳥、星火之分識，璿璣玉衡之首察，以求七政之齊；而周官則以馮相、保章氏世其業矣。其後言天體者，有宣夜、周髀、渾天。宣夜有名而無術，周髀有術而無驗，惟渾天之法，揚子雲謂其近理，以其能祖述璣衡，而後世六合、三辰、四遊之儀，皆其制之傳也。善星官者，有巫咸、甘德、石申。巫咸之書無所考見，而甘、石善於推步，獨爲星經之祖。凡今三垣、五宮、兩極、十二辰野、五星、列宿、干支、方位之說，皆其術之餘也。楚魏而下，代有其人，如漢之洛下閎、鮮于妄人，唐之李淳風、僧一行，皆以其術著名當時。而一行之穎悟絕人，象數精博，其最優歟？宋之沈括、邵堯夫，元之許平仲、郭守敬，各以其說發明天道，而守敬之立法精詳，度越千古，其尤善歟？要之，聖人首出庶物，先天不違，故能敬天觀象，治曆明
translation_en:
…books on the stars. Under Gaoyang, Chong, the Director of the South, was charged with overseeing celestial affairs; thus a dedicated office first came into being. In the ages of Tang and Yu, the Bird and Fire asterisms were distinguished, and the celestial pivot and jade sighting tube were examined as a first priority, to ascertain the harmonious courses of the seven luminaries. Under the offices of Zhou, the Masters of Celestial Phenomena (Fengxiang) and Astrologers (Baozhang) transmitted their occupation hereditarily.

Later accounts of the structure of the heavens included the Xuanye theory, the Zhoubi theory, and the Huntian, or spherical-heaven, theory. Xuanye had a name but no method; Zhoubi had a method but lacked verification. Only the Huntian method was judged by Yang Ziyun to approach the true principles, because it carried forward the tradition of the celestial pivot and sighting tube. The later instruments of the Six Directions, the Three Luminaries, and the Four Movements all transmitted its design.

Those skilled in stellar astronomy included Wu Xian, Gan De, and Shi Shen. Wu Xian’s writings are unavailable for examination, whereas Gan and Shi excelled in calculating celestial movements and became the foremost founders of the tradition of star canons. All present-day accounts of the Three Enclosures, Five Palaces, two poles, twelve celestial divisions and their terrestrial correspondences, five planets, constellations, heavenly stems and earthly branches, and directional positions are legacies of their methods.

From the time of Chu and Wei onward, every age had such men. Luoxia Hong and Xianyu Wangren of the Han, and Li Chunfeng and the monk Yixing of the Tang, were all renowned in their own times for these arts. Yixing’s exceptional intelligence surpassed that of others, and his knowledge of celestial phenomena and numerical principles was both precise and extensive. Was he perhaps the most accomplished? Shen Kuo and Shao Yaofu of the Song, and Xu Pingzhong and Guo Shoujing of the Yuan, each elucidated the Way of Heaven through their theories. Shoujing’s methods were precise and detailed, surpassing those of all preceding ages. Was he perhaps especially outstanding?

The essential point is that the sage rises above the multitude of beings and, even when acting before Heaven, does not contravene it. Thus he can revere Heaven, observe its phenomena, regulate the calendar, and clarify…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
時以命其臣而後世則沿襲古制隨時脩
改間有作者又多業非師授言以人殊卒
莫有辨而正之者然則知天之道不亦難
哉夫堪輿之說何始乎維昔黃帝畫野分
州得國萬區當時必有所主之人顓頊氏
命北正黎司地以主民亦必有所治之職
而皆無所於見堪輿亦古掌地之官名嘗
觀吕才著卜宅篇引堪輿經載黃帝對天
老言五姓之說則其書尚存於唐而今則
===
無傳矣周禮惟王建國辨方正位而土方
氏有掌土圭之法大司空有土宜之法皆
以土地相民宅而建邦邑他日周公洛邑
之卜衛文方中之定率用是道而聖人所
以為民之意從可識矣蓋廣谷大川異制
民生其間異俗要亦地氣使然而其風雨
所會陰陽所和者則百物阜安故司馬遷
作地志歷敘天下民俗物產各因其地而
周人辨之必詳者其固用地宜以阜民者
punctuated:
時，以命其臣，而後世則沿襲古制，隨時脩改，間有作者，又多業非師授，言以人殊，卒莫有辨而正之者。然則知天之道，不亦難哉？
夫堪輿之說何始乎？維昔黃帝畫野分州，得國萬區，當時必有所主之人；顓頊氏命北正黎司地以主民，亦必有所治之職，而皆無所於見。堪輿亦古掌地之官名。嘗觀吕才著《卜宅篇》，引《堪輿經》，載黃帝對天老言五姓之說，則其書尚存於唐，而今則無傳矣。《周禮》：「惟王建國，辨方正位。」而土方氏有掌土圭之法，大司空有土宜之法，皆以土地相民宅而建邦邑。他日周公洛邑之卜、衛文方中之定，率用是道，而聖人所以為民之意，從可識矣。蓋廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗，要亦地氣使然。而其風雨所會、陰陽所和者，則百物阜安。故司馬遷作《地志》，歷敘天下民俗物產，各因其地，而周人辨之必詳者，其固用地宜以阜民者
translation_en:
…the seasons, and thereby charged his ministers with their duties. Later generations followed the ancient institutions, revising them as circumstances required. Occasionally someone devised something new, but such practitioners had mostly not received their learning from a master, and their accounts differed from person to person. In the end, no one could discriminate among them and correct their errors. Is it not difficult, then, to understand the Way of Heaven?
Where did the teachings of geomancy (kanyu) begin? Long ago, the Yellow Emperor demarcated the countryside and divided it into provinces, establishing ten thousand domains. At that time there must have been people responsible for these matters. Zhuanxu appointed Li, the Northern Regulator [?], to administer the earth and oversee the people; there must likewise have been an office responsible for this work. Yet no evidence of either is to be found. Kanyu was also the name of an ancient office charged with the land. I once read Lü Cai’s “Essay on Divining Dwelling Sites,” which quotes the Classic of Geomancy, recording the Yellow Emperor speaking to Tianlao about the doctrine of the five surnames. That book thus still existed in the Tang, but it has not been transmitted to the present.
The Rites of Zhou says: “When the king establishes a state, he distinguishes the directions and determines the proper positions.” The Director of Lands had methods involving the earth-measuring tablet, while the Minister of Works had methods for determining the suitability of land. Both used the character of the land to select dwelling sites for the people and establish states and settlements. Later, the Duke of Zhou’s divination concerning Luoyi and Duke Wen of Wei’s determination of his site when the constellation Ding stood at the meridian both followed this Way. From this we can discern the sages’ intentions in acting for the people.
Broad valleys and great rivers differ in their configurations, and the people living among them differ in their customs. In essence, this too results from the vital influences of the land. Where winds and rains converge and yin and yang are in harmony, all things flourish and find security. Thus Sima Qian composed a Treatise on Geography [?], systematically describing the customs and products throughout the realm, each according to its locality. The people of Zhou were necessarily thorough in distinguishing these conditions, presumably because they used what suited the land to bring prosperity to the people…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
歟王公設險以守其國故古稱關中天府
之國百二之勝婁敬進說於漢高范仲淹
建議於宋帝智謀之士所見畧同至朱子
則又極言冀州風水之美豈非以其得地
勝而可以建國者歟若分野之說則又以
天星地域合而言之也其說本於天官星
土之辨不爲無據然觀史傳所載如梓愼
知宋鄭之饑史墨知越之有吳往往徵驗
似未可以星野之不相值而盡疑之也要
===
之聖人德業博厚配地無疆故能相理地
宜體國經野以奠其民而後世則承藉餘
休輯寧幹止間有說者又多流於小數泥
於致遠卒無有明而用之者然則知地之
道不亦難哉善乎唐一行之議曰原古人
所以重曆數之意將以恭授人時欽若乾
象而不在於渾蓋之是非其所以步圭景
之意將以節宣和氣輔相物宜而不在於
辰次之周徑君子謂其言之合理方今
punctuated: 歟？王公設險以守其國，故古稱關中天府之國，百二之勝。婁敬進說於漢高，范仲淹建議於宋帝，智謀之士所見畧同。至朱子，則又極言冀州風水之美，豈非以其得地勝而可以建國者歟？若分野之說，則又以天星地域合而言之也。其說本於天官星土之辨，不爲無據。然觀史傳所載，如梓愼知宋鄭之饑，史墨知越之有吳，往往徵驗，似未可以星野之不相值而盡疑之也。要之，聖人德業博厚，配地無疆，故能相理地宜，體國經野，以奠其民。而後世則承藉餘休，輯寧幹止；間有說者，又多流於小數，泥於致遠，卒無有明而用之者。然則知地之道，不亦難哉？善乎唐一行之議曰：「原古人所以重曆數之意，將以恭授人時，欽若乾象，而不在於渾蓋之是非；其所以步圭景之意，將以節宣和氣，輔相物宜，而不在於辰次之周徑。」君子謂其言之合理。方今
translation_en:
…was it not? Kings and lords establish defensive barriers to protect their states. Thus, in antiquity, Guanzhong was called a land of heavenly abundance, possessing the strategic advantage by which two could withstand a hundred. Lou Jing presented this argument to Gaozu of the Han, and Fan Zhongyan made a proposal to the Song emperor: these men of wisdom and resourcefulness held broadly similar views. Master Zhu, moreover, spoke at length of the excellence of Jizhou’s winds and waters. Was this not because its advantageous terrain made it suitable for establishing a capital?

As for the theory of celestial and terrestrial correspondences, it discusses the stars in heaven and regions on earth together. This theory derives from the celestial officials’ distinctions between stars and their corresponding territories, and is therefore not without foundation. Yet, considering what the historical accounts record—for example, Zishen’s foreknowledge of famine in Song and Zheng, and Shi Mo’s foreknowledge that Yue would possess Wu—such predictions repeatedly proved accurate. It seems that we cannot dismiss them all merely because the stellar divisions and terrestrial regions do not coincide.

In essence, the sages’ virtue and achievements were broad and substantial, matching the earth’s boundlessness. Thus they could examine and regulate the uses appropriate to the land, lay out capitals and demarcate the countryside, and thereby give their people secure settlement. Later generations relied upon the blessings they had left behind, maintaining peace and stability [?]. Those who occasionally offered explanations mostly strayed into petty techniques and became bogged down in attempts to extend their reasoning far afield [?]; ultimately, none understood these principles clearly and put them into practice. Is not the way of understanding the earth difficult indeed?

Excellent was the argument of Yixing of the Tang, who said: “If we investigate why the ancients valued calendrical calculations, their purpose was respectfully to communicate the seasons to the people and reverently to follow the celestial signs; it did not lie in deciding between the correctness of the spherical-heaven and canopy-heaven theories. Their purpose in measuring the gnomon’s shadow was to regulate and diffuse harmonious qi and assist things in attaining their proper conditions; it did not lie in determining the circumference and diameter of the celestial stations.” The gentleman considers his words consonant with principle. At present…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
聖人御極天位乎上而三辰順序地位乎下而
民物咸若蓋以致中和之功而運之於治
化兼歷代之制而守之於臣工億萬世無
疆之休端在是矣執事以爲何如
第五問
洪世遷
考試官學正李批通變宜民深得行法之意此作
以此鋪敘可占其用世之志矣
考試官敎授向批有斷有氣錄之
===
興天下之利者在於宜民行天下之法者
在於通變變不通則無以善法民不宜則
無以善政所謂通變者酌時勢而損益之
非以紊夫法也所謂宜民者卽土俗而權
度之非以徇夫人也通變宜民則政善民
安以之行法則不泥以之興利則可久又
何患於事不成而民不信哉執事下策承
學以錢幣通塞爲問是蓋有意於經國裕
民利用厚生之道愚也何足以知之然亦
punctuated:
聖人御極，天位乎上而三辰順序，地位乎下而民物咸若。蓋以致中和之功而運之於治化，兼歷代之制而守之於臣工，億萬世無疆之休端在是矣。執事以爲何如？

第五問
洪世遷
考試官學正李批：通變宜民，深得行法之意。此作以此鋪敘，可占其用世之志矣。
考試官敎授向批：有斷有氣，錄之。

興天下之利者，在於宜民；行天下之法者，在於通變。變不通，則無以善法；民不宜，則無以善政。所謂通變者，酌時勢而損益之，非以紊夫法也；所謂宜民者，卽土俗而權度之，非以徇夫人也。通變宜民，則政善民安；以之行法則不泥，以之興利則可久，又何患於事不成而民不信哉？執事下策承學，以錢幣通塞爲問，是蓋有意於經國裕民、利用厚生之道。愚也何足以知之？然亦
translation_en:
…the sage occupies the supreme throne. Heaven holds its place above, and the sun, moon, and stars follow their proper order; Earth holds its place below, and the people and all things flourish in accord. This is accomplished by bringing centrality and harmony to perfection and applying them to government and moral transformation, while drawing together the institutions of successive dynasties and having officials uphold them. Here indeed lies the source of boundless blessings for countless generations. What is your judgment on this?

Fifth Question
Hong Shiqian
Examiner Li, School Instructor, comments: “Adapting to change and suiting the people’s needs: this grasps profoundly the purpose of implementing laws. This composition develops its exposition around these principles, revealing the author’s aspiration to serve the world.”
Examiner Xiang, Professor, comments: “It has decisiveness and vigor. Accept it.”

Promoting benefits throughout the realm depends on suiting the people’s needs; implementing laws throughout the realm depends on adapting to change. Without adaptation to change, there is no means of making laws effective; without meeting the people’s needs, there is no means of making government good. What is meant by adapting to change is weighing the circumstances of the times and making reductions or additions accordingly, not throwing the laws into disorder. What is meant by suiting the people’s needs is assessing matters in light of local customs, not yielding to people’s wishes. When change is accommodated and the people’s needs are met, government is good and the people are secure. Applied to the implementation of laws, these principles prevent rigidity; applied to promoting benefits, they ensure lasting results. Why, then, fear that affairs will fail or that the people will withhold their trust?

You have presented a policy question to us students, asking about the circulation and obstruction of currency. Surely your intention is to explore the way to order the state and enrich the people, facilitate the use of resources, and improve their livelihood. How could someone as ignorant as I adequately understand this? Yet I too…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
竊有見焉夫國之有財賦猶人之有元氣
也養身者當益其氣經國者當裕其財錢
也者所以制財貨之源權百物之本也布
帛不可以尺寸爲交菽粟不可以抄勺相
貿錢之爲質操之易持積之不弊以通有
無以定貴賤是其爲物雖小而其爲用甚
大司馬芝曰用錢非徒豐國亦所以省刑
是錢幣之行不可以不講也粤稽之古太
公立九府圜法曰泉者流通如泉也曰布
===
者宣布如布也命名之義蓋有取於此矣
而鄭樵乃謂泉言其形布言其用者吾敢
據以爲然哉管子謂湯鑄莊山之金以贖
人之鬻禹鑄歴山之金以救人之困鑄金
之意蓋因歲儉而爲之也而周禮之司市
所謂凶荒則市無征而作布豈亦禹湯之
遺意歟自是而行於漢高帝作筴錢所以
懲秦之重也其後易而爲八銖爲四銖爲
五銖法因時變名亦多矣而輕重適均者
punctuated:
竊有見焉。夫國之有財賦，猶人之有元氣也。養身者當益其氣，經國者當裕其財。錢也者，所以制財貨之源，權百物之本也。布帛不可以尺寸爲交，菽粟不可以抄勺相貿。錢之爲質，操之易持，積之不弊，以通有無，以定貴賤。是其爲物雖小，而其爲用甚大。司馬芝曰：「用錢非徒豐國，亦所以省刑。」是錢幣之行，不可以不講也。
粤稽之古，太公立九府圜法。曰泉者，流通如泉也；曰布者，宣布如布也。命名之義，蓋有取於此矣。而鄭樵乃謂泉言其形、布言其用者，吾敢據以爲然哉？管子謂湯鑄莊山之金以贖人之鬻，禹鑄歴山之金以救人之困。鑄金之意，蓋因歲儉而爲之也。而《周禮》之司市所謂「凶荒則市無征而作布」，豈亦禹湯之遺意歟？自是而行於漢，高帝作筴錢，所以懲秦之重也。其後易而爲八銖，爲四銖，爲五銖，法因時變，名亦多矣。而輕重適均者
translation_en:
…I nevertheless venture to offer an observation. A state's revenues are like a person's vital energy. Those who nurture their bodies should replenish their energy; those who administer a state should augment its wealth. Money provides the means to regulate the sources of wealth and goods and the basis for weighing the value of all commodities. Cloth and silk cannot be exchanged inch by inch or foot by foot, nor beans and grain traded by tiny scoops and spoonfuls. Coins, by their physical nature, are easy to handle and carry, and can be accumulated without deteriorating. They enable exchanges between those who have goods and those who lack them, and establish relative prices. Thus, although small as objects, they are exceedingly useful. Sima Zhi said: “Using money not only enriches the state; it also reduces punishments.” The circulation of currency therefore demands careful consideration.
Looking back into antiquity, the Grand Duke established the currency system of the Nine Treasuries. Currency was called quan, “spring,” because it circulated like spring water; it was called bu, “cloth,” because it spread abroad like cloth. These names presumably drew their meaning from this. Yet Zheng Qiao maintained that quan referred to its shape and bu to its use. Dare I accept his statement as correct? The Guanzi states that Tang cast the metal of Mount Zhuang to redeem people who had been sold, and Yu cast the metal of Mount Li to relieve people in distress. The intention behind casting metal into currency was presumably to respond to years of poor harvests. And when the section on the Director of Markets in the Rites of Zhou says, “In times of famine, no levies are collected at the markets, and currency is issued,” might this likewise preserve the intention of Yu and Tang? From these beginnings, the practice continued into the Han. Emperor Gao made ce coins [?] to remedy the excessive weight of Qin coinage. Subsequently, these were changed to eight-zhu, four-zhu, and five-zhu coins. Standards changed with the times, and the names were numerous. Yet those whose weight struck precisely the proper balance…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
惟五銖乎自是而行於唐則開通鑄於武
德所以易隋之舊也其後變而為開元為
天寶為乾元名以世易制亦善矣而經久
可行者惟開元乎呂祖謙曰論太重則有
所謂直百當十論太輕則有所謂榆莢三
銖然而皆不得中惟五銖開元銖兩之多
寡鼓鑄之精密相望而不可易蓋有見于
此也宋元以來更造不一或費多而利不
歸上或令煩而事不便民更革無常未容
===
悉議惟我
國家因特定制設局鼓鑄酌輕重之宜行斂
散之法相兼前代布之民間泉貨流通遐
邇歸會百有餘年上無紛更之擾下無匱
乏之患顧行之既久民自殊風大江以北
三幣並行大江以南錢不為市此豈錢之
不行哉公府不入則富者積而無施勢室
不藏則貧民得之無用是宜其滯也執事
之言曰南北異俗不可强同豈獨南北然
punctuated:
惟五銖乎？自是而行於唐，則開通鑄於武德，所以易隋之舊也。其後變而為開元、為天寶、為乾元，名以世易，制亦善矣，而經久可行者惟開元乎？呂祖謙曰：「論太重，則有所謂直百、當十；論太輕，則有所謂榆莢、三銖。然而皆不得中，惟五銖、開元，銖兩之多寡、鼓鑄之精密，相望而不可易。」蓋有見于此也。宋元以來，更造不一，或費多而利不歸上，或令煩而事不便民，更革無常，未容悉議。
惟我國家因特定制，設局鼓鑄，酌輕重之宜，行斂散之法，相兼前代，布之民間，泉貨流通，遐邇歸會。百有餘年，上無紛更之擾，下無匱乏之患。顧行之既久，民自殊風，大江以北，三幣並行；大江以南，錢不為市。此豈錢之不行哉？公府不入，則富者積而無施；勢室不藏，則貧民得之無用，是宜其滯也。執事之言曰：「南北異俗，不可强同。」豈獨南北然
translation_en:
…was it only the five-zhu coin? Coming next to the Tang, the Kaitong coin [?] was cast during the Wude reign to replace the old Sui coinage. Subsequently it changed to Kaiyuan, Tianbao, and Qianyuan. The names changed with the times, and the arrangements were sound; yet was it only the Kaiyuan coin that remained serviceable over the long term? Lü Zuqian said: “As for excessively heavy coinage, there were the so-called ‘worth a hundred’ and ‘equivalent to ten’ coins; as for excessively light coinage, there were the ‘elm-seed’ and three-zhu coins. Yet none achieved the proper mean. Only the five-zhu and Kaiyuan coins matched one another in their weight and the precision of their casting, and could not be improved upon.” He surely understood this point. Since the Song and Yuan, coinage has been repeatedly remade in different forms. Sometimes expenditure was great but the benefit did not accrue to the government; sometimes regulations were burdensome and their implementation inconvenient for the people. Changes were incessant, and there is no room to discuss them all.
Our dynasty thereupon specially established regulations [?], set up offices for casting coins, weighed the proper balance between light and heavy coinage, and implemented methods for collecting and distributing money. Combining the practices of preceding dynasties [?], it distributed coins among the people. Currency circulated, converging from near and far. For more than a hundred years, those above suffered no disruption from repeated changes, and those below faced no shortage. Yet after these practices had long been in effect, popular customs diverged of their own accord. North of the great river, three forms of currency circulate together; south of it, coins are not used in market transactions. Is this really because coins cannot circulate? When government offices do not accept them, the wealthy accumulate them but have nowhere to spend them; when powerful households do not keep them, poor people who acquire them can make no use of them. It is only to be expected that their circulation should stagnate. You say: “The north and south have different customs; they cannot be forced into uniformity.” But is this so only of north and south…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉夫土貨旣殊貿鬻自異利於都邑之肆
者不入徐揚之市便於荆郢之邦者礙乎
兗洛之域王澄甞言之矣自今觀之有行
於一郡而滯於一邑有行於一邑而滯於
一鄉者愚以為此豈民風之殊要在轉移
之耳執事又謂嶺海之間以之貿遷若有
感於閩廣通塞之異而求所以錢幣大行
民情俱協之道愚以為廣谷大川異制民
生其間異俗君子脩其敎不易其俗齊其
===
政不易其宜斯王制之所以經綸天下也
何則民俗旣久更化難施積習已深作新
易擾苟非通變豈能樂成考之周禮外府
掌邦布之入出共其財用之幣齎賜予之
財凡邦之小用皆受焉泉府掌邦市之征
布斂市之不售貨之滯於民者夫周禮掌
財之官非一職也而泉布獨於二府隷焉
者何邪蓋載齎之出入非錢不能以致遠
因其小用者而受之耳貿易之出入非錢
punctuated:
哉？夫土貨旣殊，貿鬻自異。利於都邑之肆者，不入徐揚之市；便於荆郢之邦者，礙乎兗洛之域。王澄甞言之矣。自今觀之，有行於一郡而滯於一邑，有行於一邑而滯於一鄉者。愚以為此豈民風之殊？要在轉移之耳。執事又謂嶺海之間以之貿遷，若有感於閩廣通塞之異，而求所以錢幣大行、民情俱協之道。愚以為廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗，君子脩其敎，不易其俗；齊其政，不易其宜。斯《王制》之所以經綸天下也。何則？民俗旣久，更化難施；積習已深，作新易擾。苟非通變，豈能樂成？
考之《周禮》，外府掌邦布之入出，共其財用之幣、齎賜予之財，凡邦之小用皆受焉；泉府掌邦市之征布，斂市之不售、貨之滯於民者。夫《周禮》掌財之官，非一職也，而泉布獨於二府隷焉者，何邪？蓋載齎之出入，非錢不能以致遠，因其小用者而受之耳。貿易之出入，非錢
translation_en:
…is that so? Since local products differ, trade naturally differs as well. What serves the shops of the capital does not enter the markets of Xu and Yang; what is convenient in the lands of Jing and Ying meets obstacles in the regions of Yan and Luo. Wang Cheng once spoke of this. Looking at present conditions, some currency circulates in one prefecture but is obstructed in a particular county; some circulates in one county but is obstructed in a particular township. In my humble view, can this really be a matter of differing popular customs? The essential thing is to redirect those practices. You further say that currency is used for trade in the region of Lingnan and the southern seaboard. You seem concerned by the difference between Fujian and Guangdong in the ease or difficulty of its circulation, and seek a way for coinage to circulate widely while accommodating the dispositions of all the people. In my humble view, broad valleys and great rivers differ in their configurations, and the people living among them differ in their customs. The gentleman cultivates their instruction without changing their customs and brings uniformity to their government without changing what suits their circumstances. This is how the “Royal Regulations” sets out the ordering of the realm. Why is this so? Once popular customs are long established, reform is difficult to implement; once accumulated habits are deeply rooted, renewal readily causes disturbance. Without adapting to circumstances, how can one bring people to rejoice in the result?
Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that the Outer Treasury administers the receipt and disbursement of the state's currency, supplies the money for its expenditures and the funds for provisions and gifts, and provides for all the state's minor expenses. The Treasury for Markets administers the monetary levies on the state's markets and purchases goods that remain unsold in the markets or lie idle in the people's hands. In the Rites of Zhou, responsibility for finance is not confined to a single office. Why, then, is currency assigned exclusively to these two treasuries? For funds carried on journeys, whether outgoing or incoming, cannot reach distant places without coinage; hence money is received from the Outer Treasury for such minor expenses. As for receipts and payments in trade, without coinage…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
不得以兼濟因民之貨售者而通之耳是
蓋上下相承循環無端今欲行之亦曰流
通之機在上而不在下轉移之術以公而
不以私宋儒有曰古者制賦以穀制祿以
田則錢之權輕是以不行今制賦之法已
定如漕兌之正額無容議矣其他如郡邑
之存留以之而兼輸得無不可乎制祿之
法已定如
上供之正數無容議矣其他如百官羣吏之俸
===
給以之而兼支得無不可乎收之於課稅
者則發之於工役入之於罪贖者則出之
於賑貸里甲之雜辦以之其酬應不可用
乎徭役之差科以之其傭募不可散乎是
其輸者乃所以爲支其出者即所以爲入
其在官者即其在民其在私者即其在公
者也公私交利上下兼濟何必驅之以刑
脅之以威而後爲可行哉然則變通之道
孰有踰於此乎雖然滌流者當導其源齊
punctuated: 不得以兼濟，因民之貨售者而通之耳。是蓋上下相承，循環無端。今欲行之，亦曰流通之機在上而不在下，轉移之術以公而不以私。宋儒有曰：「古者制賦以穀，制祿以田，則錢之權輕，是以不行。」今制賦之法已定，如漕兌之正額，無容議矣。其他如郡邑之存留，以之而兼輸，得無不可乎？制祿之法已定，如上供之正數，無容議矣。其他如百官羣吏之俸給，以之而兼支，得無不可乎？收之於課稅者，則發之於工役；入之於罪贖者，則出之於賑貸。里甲之雜辦，以之其酬應不可用乎？徭役之差科，以之其傭募不可散乎？是其輸者乃所以爲支，其出者即所以爲入，其在官者即其在民，其在私者即其在公者也。公私交利，上下兼濟，何必驅之以刑、脅之以威，而後爲可行哉？然則變通之道，孰有踰於此乎？雖然，滌流者當導其源，齊
translation_en: …cannot provide mutual benefit without money; it merely facilitates circulation through the sale of the people's goods. Thus those above and below sustain one another in an unending cycle. If we wish to put this into practice today, we need only say that the key to circulation lies with those above, not those below, and that the means of directing its movement must operate through public, rather than private, action. A Song Confucian scholar said: “In antiquity, taxes were assessed in grain and official emoluments provided through land; money therefore had little importance and consequently did not circulate.” Now the system of taxation is already fixed: there is no room to debate such matters as the established quota of grain delivered for transport by canal. But for other items, such as revenues retained by prefectures and counties, might it not be acceptable to remit part in money? The system of official emoluments is already fixed: there is no room to debate such matters as the established amounts supplied to the throne. But for other items, such as the salaries of the various officials and clerks, might it not be acceptable to pay part in money? What is collected in taxes should be disbursed for public works; what comes in through payments to redeem criminal penalties should go out in relief loans. For the miscellaneous supplies furnished under the lijia system, could money not be used to meet the expenses? For labor-service assessments, could it not be distributed to hire workers? Thus what is remitted provides the means for expenditure, and what is paid out provides the means for revenue. What is held by the authorities is also what is held by the people; what is in private hands is also what is in public hands. With public and private interests both benefiting, and those above and below mutually assisted, why must people first be driven by punishments and intimidated by force before the system can operate? What method of adapting to circumstances could surpass this? Nevertheless, those who would cleanse a stream must attend to the flow at its source; those who would set in order…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
末者當揣其本苟行之旣久則錢必貴錢
貴則物賤物賤則民傷是所以便民者乃
所以敝之也其將何以處之亦曰通其源
而已故欲法之久也又當議鼓鑄之法重
私造之刑嚴薄惡之戒申磨鎔之令則庶
乎其可矣是在司計者主之非愚之所敢
與也
punctuated: 末者當揣其本。苟行之旣久，則錢必貴；錢貴則物賤，物賤則民傷。是所以便民者，乃所以敝之也。其將何以處之？亦曰通其源而已。故欲法之久也，又當議鼓鑄之法，重私造之刑，嚴薄惡之戒，申磨鎔之令，則庶乎其可矣。是在司計者主之，非愚之所敢與也。
translation_en: …those who would put the branches in order should examine the root. If this practice continues for a long time, money will inevitably become dear. When money becomes dear, goods become cheap; when goods become cheap, the people suffer. Thus what serves to benefit the people becomes a means of impoverishing them. How, then, should this be handled? Simply by opening up the source of supply. Therefore, if this method is to endure, we must also deliberate on regulations for minting coins, increase the penalties for illicit minting, strictly enforce prohibitions against thin and inferior coins, and reiterate the orders concerning the filing down and melting of coins. Then perhaps the method will prove workable. This is for those in charge of financial administration to direct; it is not something in which I, in my ignorance, dare to intervene.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
福建鄉試錄後序
福建鄉試錄成夢雲竊自慶
幸獲與諸執事周旋其間而
得人以告成事乃颺言于末
簡曰夫尼丘毓聖嵩嶽生申
山川之生材不誣也始夢雲
之應聘而至也陟霞嶺涉龍
===
江道武夷之麓望溟渤之洋
奮薄風雲吞吐日月信東南
之巨麗而山海之奇觀也進
而試其文則布體攟華陳高
發隱博而不泛朴而不俚浩
放而有制馳騁於子史而不
詭於道乃作而歎曰美哉郁
punctuated:
福建鄉試錄後序

福建鄉試錄成，夢雲竊自慶幸，獲與諸執事周旋其間，而得人以告成事，乃颺言于末簡曰：夫尼丘毓聖，嵩嶽生申，山川之生材不誣也。始夢雲之應聘而至也，陟霞嶺，涉龍江，道武夷之麓，望溟渤之洋，奮薄風雲，吞吐日月，信東南之巨麗，而山海之奇觀也。進而試其文，則布體攟華，陳高發隱，博而不泛，朴而不俚，浩放而有制，馳騁於子史而不詭於道。乃作而歎曰：「美哉！郁
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination

With the Record of the Fujian Provincial Examination completed, I, Mengyun, privately rejoice in my good fortune: I was able to work among the officials responsible, and we have secured worthy men with whom to report the successful completion of our charge. I therefore proclaim on these closing pages: Niqiu nurtured the Sage, and Mount Song brought forth Shen; that mountains and rivers produce talented men is no empty claim.

When I first came in response to the invitation, I climbed Xialing, crossed the Longjiang, traveled along the foot of the Wuyi Mountains, and gazed out over the vast ocean. Surging against wind and cloud, swallowing and disgorging sun and moon—truly this was the grandeur of the southeast, a wondrous spectacle of mountains and sea.

Then, when I examined the candidates’ writings, I found their compositions well arranged and their literary excellences gathered together; they set forth lofty ideas and brought hidden meanings to light. Broad in learning without being diffuse, plain without being vulgar, expansive yet disciplined, they ranged freely through the philosophical masters and histories without departing from the Way. I rose and exclaimed: “How beautiful! How flourishing…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
郁乎文獻之邦先民之遺澤
在焉其文可徵也夫天地之
精淑峙爲山岳流爲江河散
爲川阜瀦爲海瀆雖派別支
分自爲形體而源委脉絡各
有會同海者山水之鍾而風
氣之聚也閩地負山阻海自
===
武夷雄峙建溪回合盤鬱丹
青迤邐而東會爲芝城之勝
厚儲秀發滲漉凝結蓄爲瑰
奇煥爲文物真精靈淑盡萃
於人而士又得其最秀最靈
以爲之望宜閩士之多材也
夫和氏之玉登爲珪璧琮璜
punctuated: 郁乎文獻之邦！先民之遺澤在焉，其文可徵也。」夫天地之精淑，峙爲山岳，流爲江河，散爲川阜，瀦爲海瀆。雖派別支分，自爲形體，而源委脉絡，各有會同。海者，山水之鍾，而風氣之聚也。閩地負山阻海，自武夷雄峙，建溪回合，盤鬱丹青，迤邐而東，會爲芝城之勝。厚儲秀發，滲漉凝結，蓄爲瑰奇，煥爲文物，真精靈淑盡萃於人，而士又得其最秀最靈，以爲之望。宜閩士之多材也！夫和氏之玉，登爲珪璧琮璜，
translation_en: …flourishing indeed is this land of learned culture and worthy men! The beneficent legacy of its forebears remains here, and its writings bear witness to it.” The pure and excellent essence of Heaven and Earth rises into mountains, flows into rivers, spreads into streams and hills, and pools into seas and waterways. Though divided into separate courses and branches, each taking its own form, their sources, courses, and interconnecting channels all have places where they converge. The sea is where the potency of mountains and waters collects and the influences of wind and vital energy gather. The land of Min has mountains at its back and the sea as its barrier. From the lofty heights of Wuyi, where the Jianxi River winds and converges, the landscape unfolds in luxuriant masses of red and green, extending eastward to unite in the scenic splendor of Zhicheng. Richly stored, this potency issues forth in excellence; seeping through and congealing, it accumulates into rare wonders and shines forth in the products of civilization. Its true essence, spiritual vitality, and purity are all concentrated in people. Scholars, moreover, receive the finest and most spiritual portion and become the leading figures of the region. It is fitting indeed that the scholars of Min should possess so many talents! Now, the jade of Mr. He is raised to the dignity of ritual objects—gui tablets, bi disks, cong tubes, and huang pendants…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
其精神則伏于崑岡汗血之
駒必渥洼乃良焉物固有然
者矣人才之美不但珪璧之
重黼黻之能不但致遠之用
也其鍾英萃美降神通氣以
成能于天下而發舒其精祥
此理之常無足怪者是故三
===
蘇生而眉山草木爲之改觀
二程出而伊洛源流因之益
遠九峰靈鷲固嶺表之卷石
也地不登于禹貢名不列于
職方自朱子結社以來而雲
谷少微之間遂爲名勝至有
裹糧千里快於一登此豈徒
punctuated: 其精神則伏于崑岡。汗血之駒，必渥洼乃良焉。物固有然者矣。人才之美，不但珪璧之重；黼黻之能，不但致遠之用也。其鍾英萃美，降神通氣，以成能于天下，而發舒其精祥，此理之常，無足怪者。是故三蘇生，而眉山草木爲之改觀；二程出，而伊洛源流因之益遠。九峰、靈鷲，固嶺表之卷石也，地不登于《禹貢》，名不列于《職方》。自朱子結社以來，而雲谷、少微之間遂爲名勝，至有裹糧千里，快於一登。此豈徒
translation_en: …its vital essence lies hidden in the Kunlun heights. A blood-sweating steed must come from Wowa to be truly fine. Such things certainly occur in the natural world. The excellence of human talent possesses more than the worth of jade ritual tablets and disks; its capacity to embellish good government offers more than the usefulness of a horse that can travel far. The concentration of excellence and beauty, the descent of spiritual potency and the circulation of vital energy, producing capable people in the world and unfolding their auspicious essence—these are the ordinary workings of principle, nothing to marvel at. Thus, when the three Su were born, even the vegetation of Meishan took on a new aspect; when the two Cheng emerged, the intellectual currents of the Yi and Luo rivers flowed still farther. Jiufeng and Lingjiu were merely little rocky heights beyond the mountain ranges. Their terrain was not recorded in the Tribute of Yu, nor were their names listed in the Offices of the Regions. Yet ever since Master Zhu established a fellowship there, the area between Yungu and Shaowei became a renowned scenic destination. Some even packed provisions and traveled a thousand li for the delight of a single ascent. Could this merely have been because…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
以其風物哉故有斐者興淇
澳之歌而景行者動仰止之
念古人寄興懷人必本地靈
良有以也不然則勝母之里
曾子爲之不入而朝歌之市
墨子爲之回車豈非人之無
良祗以爲地辱耶爾諸士固
===
鍾山海之秀而生者行且進
試澤宮致用有日矣所以發
攄素蘊而闡洩地靈二三往
哲具有真模不必遠學也若
乃窮而學之達則棄之趨逐
紛華以自貽玷缺則是取誚
於山靈而見譏於海若也豈
punctuated: 以其風物哉？故有斐者興淇澳之歌，而景行者動仰止之念。古人寄興懷人，必本地靈，良有以也。不然，則勝母之里，曾子爲之不入；而朝歌之市，墨子爲之回車。豈非人之無良，祗以爲地辱耶？爾諸士固鍾山海之秀而生者，行且進試澤宮，致用有日矣。所以發攄素蘊而闡洩地靈，二三往哲具有真模，不必遠學也。若乃窮而學之，達則棄之，趨逐紛華，以自貽玷缺，則是取誚於山靈而見譏於海若也。豈
translation_en: …because of its scenery and local character? Thus, a refined gentleman inspired the song of the bend of the Qi River, while lofty conduct stirs thoughts of looking up in admiration. The ancients, when expressing their feelings and cherishing the memory of others, invariably grounded these sentiments in the numinous qualities of a place; there was good reason for this. Otherwise, why would Zengzi refuse to enter the village of Shengmu (Defeating Mother), and Mozi turn his carriage back from the town of Chaoge (Morning Song)? Is it not that human failings bring only disgrace upon a place? You scholars were indeed born with the concentrated excellence of the mountains and sea. Soon you will advance to be tested in the examination hall, and the day when you put your abilities to use will come. For expressing your accumulated learning and revealing the numinous qualities of your native land, those few past worthies all provide true models; you need not seek distant examples to emulate. But if you study their ways while obscure, only to abandon them upon attaining prominence, pursuing worldly splendor and thereby bringing blemishes upon yourselves, you will invite rebuke from the mountain spirits and ridicule from the sea god. How could…

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
text:
不惜哉夢雲不佞與諸士有
一日之雅故覼縷而終告之
河南汝寧府光州儒學學正
李夢雲謹序
punctuated:
不惜哉！夢雲不佞，與諸士有一日之雅，故覼縷而終告之。
河南汝寧府光州儒學學正李夢雲謹序。
translation_en:
…would this not be regrettable! Though untalented, I, Mengyun, have enjoyed a brief acquaintance with you gentlemen; thus I conclude by offering you these detailed words of counsel.
Preface respectfully written by Li Mengyun, Instructor in the Confucian School of Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan.

title: 嘉靖二十五年福建鄉試錄
